column2: KuNgoni Art Craft Centre
column6:
The KuNgoni Centre of Culture & Art is a well-known Cultural Centre. It has trained many Malawian carvers and developed their skill. In addition the Centre has, cultural museum and dance group and women development and also  attracts many Malawians, tourists and researchers eager to discover the local culture. 

The overall purpose of KuNgoni is to raise consciousness of and appreciation of the richness and intricacies of Malawi culture.

Specific purposes of the project include:
a) KuNgoni outreach on the local, national and international scale expanded.
b) Preservation of past knowledge of local villagers transmitted younger generations and the people world wide.
c) Women from different tribes and culture empowered and are able to share  ideas of deferent cultural aspects and learn different skills to improve their livelihoods.
d) Pride in culture through live cultural programmes delivered by dancers and drummers recruited from the local community.

column2: TfP Phase 3: International Advisory Group (IAB)
column6:
The Training for Peace in Africa programme, TfP, is an international training and research programme commissioned and funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA). The purpose of TfP is to contribute to strengthening African capacities for effective integration of civilian and police dimensions in African peace operations and peacebuilding missions. In order to achieve this, the programme aims at delivering capacity-building training, research and policy development support that serves to enhance the efforts of the AU and Regional Economic Communities (RECs) in building African capacities for peace missions under UN or AU auspices.

The IAB meetings provide key strategic advice to the TfP programme and its recommendations are to be followed up by both partners and the MFA. The membership of the IAB is drawn from a diverse set of backgrounds such as from relevant international bodies and academia. The IAB has no decision-making power, but advices the MFA and TfP partners on strategic issues related to training, research, policies and advocacy. The IAB will meet twice in 2008, and from 2009 an annual IAB meeting may substitute bi-annual meetings.

column2: REDD+ Participatory Forest Management in South West Ethiopia - NICFI 2021-2025
column6:
The project is a continuation and expansion of a project in Ethiopia supported by Norad since 2013. The main objective is to reduce deforestation in the South West Forest Block (the largest intact tropical forest area in Ethiopia), through assigning forest rights to selected local communities (main target group) as well as establishing sustainable livelihood models that prevent further forest encroachment. The project builds on the use of Participatory Forest Management (PFM) methodology, a step-wise methodology that involves the local population in the formal management of the forest and forest resources. 

Project outcomes are:

1. PFM institutions manage forests sustainably
2. Public institutions have the capacity to provide effective support to PFM institutions in sustainable forest management and diversified livelihoods
3. Forest dependent communities have diversified income base from forest friendly activities

The project will be managed by a consortium led by the Development Fund, with the Ethio-Wetlands and Natural Resource Associaton (EWNRA) being the main implementing partner responsible for implementation of the PFM methodology, and the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) being responsible for documentation and dissemination of best practices, in addition to conducting analysis of forest friendly livelihood options. 

Gender equality is integrated in the project design and implementation, with gender sensitive internal rules and minimum number of leadership roles in forest management institutions, micro-enterprises/cooperatives ring-fenced for women, and training for forest management institutions and micro-enterprises supporting women's active participation.

column6:
This research project will provide for a qualitative study on the Chadian police unit Détachement Intégré de Sécurité (DIS), as part of MINURCAT, and its ability to implement Resolution 1820. The project is propelled by the necessity to provide solid grounds for future decisions determining best practice in supporting mechanisms against sexual and gender-based violence in war and conflict. column2: Synchronizing Teaching with the New Curriculum - Education Ethiopia
column6:
The project is a follow-up/phase 2 on the Norway supported ETH-20/0003 “Curriculum Reform Technical Assistance to Ministry of Education in Ethiopia”. The Ministry of Education revised and developed a new curriculum for the primary level and secondary level, which was respectively introduced in September of 2022 and September of 2023. The Norway supported program ended mid-year 2023. 

As the curriculum has been introduced, the issue of training of teachers to familiarise themselves and understand the new curriculum are still outstanding. Hence, the need to focus on teacher development and teacher’s methodology in a bid to make sure that the new curriculum results in better learning outcomes for learners and further continued transition from grade to grade all the way to higher education/TVET is adamant.

The overall objective of this project is to ensure orientation and training of pre-primary and primary school teachers on the newly rolled out curriculum and initiate the development and implementation of a comprehensive teacher’s professional development programme encompassing pre-service and in-service.

Professional development offerings are key for supporting teachers in the new curriculum initiative. The benefit includes teachers’ increased comfort and skill levels for implementing the new curricula. Holistic, relevant, and effective professional development promotes confidence and greater understanding of the curriculum including the expected learning outcomes. Meaningful teachers’ professional development considers the needs, concerns, and experiences of the teachers and is likely to influence growth for teachers. It also enhances teachers’ pedagogical skills and content knowledge, which leads to increased job satisfaction and professional motivation ultimately shown in children’s learning outcomes.

column2: Small Scale Grant IMR- OfD Programme in Mozambique
column6:
The main activity (hereafter the activity) that will be carried out under the duration of the small-scale agreement between Norad and IMR is the work with a programme document for the next phase of the cooperation with Mozambique under the Oceans for Development programme in Mozambique. The grant will cover expenses in connection with IMR`s deliveries in the preparation of the programme document. IMR will also, in cooperation with Norad, arrange a workshop in Norway in the fall 2022. The grant will cover the expenses for Mozambique to participate in the workshop. 

This activity is a follow up from the conclusions from the fact-finding mission in Mozambique carried out this spring. In the report from the mission (where IMR contributed)  it was made a road map for the cooperation between the Mozambican and the Norwegian institution involved in the Ocean for Development cooperation in Mozambique.

The programme document will be made in cooperation between the Norwegian and the Mozambican Institutions involved in the cooperation under the Oceans for Development programme in Mozambique.  This Agreement also covers the participation of two experts from the Directorate of Fisheries in the Activity. 

The programme document will serve as a long-term basis for the cooperation between Norway and Mozambique under the Ocean for Development Programme in Mozambique. The Programme Document will identify activities of cooperation that will promote a strengthened, sustainable and inclusive ocean economy in Mozambique. The activities carried out under this fund shall be implemented in accordance with the Agreement between Norad and IMR, including the budget attached as annex A to the Agreement between Norad and IMR.

Increased SHF incomes and resilience , especially for women and youth 

Agricultural value chains are more inclusive, viable, for all actors and climate smart 

Outcome 

Farmer Service Centers are commercially sustainable, efficient, credible, well connected and a trusted partner across the value chain 

Products and services effectively and efficiently aggregated by FSC 

Buyers/off takers have increased access to quality aggregated produce at higher volumes more efficiently 

Increased Small holder farmers productivity through adoption of Climate Smart Agriculture   

Target group 

Small holder farmers in Tanzania and Kenya (reached through the farmer service centers). 

In Tanzania, Farm Africa and Nafaka Kilimo are implementing partners and New Zealand is co-donor. The Alliance members are Yara, Syngenta, Bayer, Agra, Rabobank and WFP. 
This is the second funding cycle cupported by Norad.

column5: IDEA - International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance
column6:
The overall goal or impact objective of the proposed project is to contribute to reducing the risk of conflict escalation in countries at risk of political violence in Africa. This impact objective is in line with the third and seventh priorities of the New African Union Commission - which are to (i) Silence the Guns in Africa and (ii) to stimulate African proactive action on the obvious determining factors of crisis in AU members States such as disrespect of constitutionalism, rule of law and exclusion. The project is also in line with the following interlinked aspirations of AU Agenda 2063.
-Aspiration 3: An Africa of good governance, democracy, respect for human rights, justice, and the rule of law.
-Aspiration 4: A peaceful and secure Africa.
-Aspiration 6: An Africa, whose development is people-driven, relying on the potential of African people, especially its women and youth, and caring for children.
Furthermore, the project aims to contribute to Sustainable Development Goal 16 which is about promoting peace, justice and strong institutions at all levels. By involving women in political processes and peace processes the project will also to some extent contribute to SDG target 5.5 (which is about ensuring women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision making in political, economic, and public life) and UN resolution 1325.

column2: Techbridge - End-to-end solution for entrepreneurs in East Africa
column6:
A consortium of TechBridge Invest (AS and Africa), MTI Investment SE, and Sote Hub Ltd will offer an end-to-end solution to boost entrepreneurship and innovation in the sectors of blue economy and marine litter in Kenya and Tanzania. The consortium consists of established actors in Kenya and Tanzania. End-to-end solution means a complete support cycle which ensures that startups and entrepreneurs have access to a seamless progression of resources and expertise, through Innovation challenges and incubation, acceleration programs, post-acceleration supports, and fundraising/Investment opportunities.

In terms of blue economy, the project aims to support entrepreneurs that focus on sustainable fishing practices, innovations in aquaculture, and eco-tourism. In terms of marine litter, the focus will be on effective waste management, enhanced recycling, and the adoption of circular economy strategies.The project has clear gender equality targets and targeted efforts to include women in the program as well as ensuring that the ones that are onboarded get specific follow-up.

column2: Mount Hoyo Peace and Reconciliation Project 2021
column6: Hope in Action DR Congo (HiA) will during a six-month period implement activities aiming to contribute towards peace, stabilization and reconciliation in the area around Mount Hoyo nature reserve in the Democratic Republic of Congo, an area highly affected by insurgency. The expected effects for the target group of the Project are (Outcome) to contribute to a sense of normality, economic empowerment, and active participation for people in the area.The planned main products and/or services of the Project are the following outputs: Distribution of 300 farming kits; 2) Rehabilitation of 13 km of access road in the Mount Hoyo forest reserve; 3) 2 overnight gatherings with local leaders; 4) 4 football tournaments and 5) 2 drama seminars.The intended target group is 300 families directly affected by the insurgency in the area, 170 young men and women at risk of being recruited by, or already recruited by rebel groups, local chiefs, leaders of women’s groups, local church leaders and leaders of local NGOs, local youth and villagers (also as spectators and players). The Security Council's resolution on women, peace and security (1325) constitutes an integral part of the project activities.

column2: Empowering the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
column3: DIHR - Danish Institute for Human Rights
column6: Support is to target identified challenges that fall into three clusters: organisational arrangements concerning formal mandate of the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission and its founding legislation, adequate budget provided by the Ethiopian Parliament and overall reform, restructuring, ICT infrastructures, and strategic planning of the Commission. The second dimension ( human rights competences) addresses capacities at the organisational level, physical and technological infrastructures, strategic leadership and expertise. The third dimension concerns the catalyst function, which includes the Commission’s engagement with national, regional and international human rights bodies and actors. To effectively tackle the human rights concerns and strengthen the human rights landscape in Ethiopia, it is important to strengthen the Commission. This highlights the justification for, and importance of, the partnership with DIHR, which aims to capacitate the Commission to become an independent NHRI.

column2: Promoting Green and Climate Resilient Local Economies in Ghana
column6:
Promoting Green and Climate Resilient Local Economies in Ghana – Applying circular economy and climate smart agriculture principles and solutions to local development pathways. The objective of the Action is to contribute to build green and climate resilient local economies in Ghana, applying circular economy and climate-smart agriculture (CSA) principles and solutions to local development pathways. The Action is expected to achieve its overall objective through increasing selected MMDAs access to climate finance to plan and implement locally led green and climate resilient public investments, while consolidating a country-based and internationally recognized mechanism to channel climate finance for local action through the performance-based climate resilience grant (PBCRG) system. 

Part of the project is to channel performance-based climate resilience grants to local authorities for them to realize green and climate resilient investments. What type of projects the selected local authorities varies and depends on the need in the different municipalities/districts (MMDAs), but historically investments have been in made in disaster risk reduction activities such as  culverts in areas at risk of flooding and tree planting for flood/erosion containment etc. and in biodiversity efforts such as reforestation of degraded forest. In addition, the MMDAs will benefit from capacity building to mainstream climate change adaptation and environmental sustainability considerations into their annual planning and budgeting processes, this includes sensitizing on how climate change affects a communities biodiversity and risk of disasters.

column2: Programme for Social, Political and Environmental Resilience (PROSPERIS)
column6:
The program aims to address socio-economic, political and environmental vulnerabilities in Somalia to build resilience, increase trust in authorities and support long-term stabilization efforts. 

The planned PROSPERIS program interventions are organized into four different thematic areas/component where each theme has specific types of interventions and activities: 
I. Socioeconomic component – covers activities focused on youth empowerment and engagement through sports (NETS) and Employment creation and livelihood opportunities. 
II. Political component (government visibility/presence) includes activities focused on rehabilitation/construction of government/public infrastructure facilities and technical support to relevant political and public institutions. 
III. Environmental component covers activities directed to promote water resource and renewable energy infrastructure development. 
IV. Cross Cutting component – will focus on issues including Monitoring and Evaluation, facilitation of strategic communication for government authorities and community engagement.

column2: Integrity Watch Liberia - Scaling Up Tax Justice Mobilising CSOs media, and parliamentarians
column6:
The project aims at (impact) improved policies and laws to track and stop illicit financial outflows, enhanced fair and equitable tax revenue mobilization and strengthened social contracts in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ghana, Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Cameroun, and Tunisia.

Outcome 1) Capacity of civil society organizations in the targeted countries strengthened to advocate for and engage citizens on tax justice, Domestic Resource Mobilisation (DRM), track and stop illicit financial lows (IFFs).

Outcome 2) Capacity of media organizations in the targeted countries strengthened, to publish stories on tax justice, DRM and IFFs. 

Outcome 3) Capacity of national caucuses of the African Parliamentary Network on Illicit Financial Flows and Taxation (APNIFFT) reinforced. Member of Parliament (MPs) equipped with technical skills to monitor and design supportive policies for equitable taxation to improve DRM, track and stop IFFs.

To enhance expertise on gender equality, particularly the gender dimension of tax justice, TJN-A’s member organisations include feminist organisations and TJN-A collaborates with regional and global women’s organisations such as Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET) and the Association for Women’s Rights in Development (AWID).

Activities will also expand to initiatives that have worked well and that could quickly be scaled up to more farmers.The project aims to contribute to increased agricultural productivity and incomes through; enhanced access to agricultural inputs(land, seeds, tool), capacity building on climate smart agriculture, and support to agriculture-based businesses through value addition, financial education and financial support. The project aims to strengthen climate change adaptation by promoting climate resilient food production as well as increase in local value creation and incomes for food producers. Specifically, this is by promoting climate-smart agriculture technologies, including soil conservation, water harvesting, integrated soil fertility management, crop diversification, and seed variety selection. Additionally, the project seeks to enhance resilience by promoting access to essential agriculture production inputs such as drought tolerant seeds for increased food production and local value addition, increasing market access and incomes.

column2: TLC – Management for Adaptation to Climate Change
column6:
The programme will address vulnerability issues related to climate change. Its goal is to improve the livelihoods of rural communities within a context that develops and secures the capacity of rural communities for adaptation to climate change in a manner that is productive and sustainable. This will be acheived through three objectives:

a) Reduce deforestation by improving the economic use and management of natural resources to supply wood energy and construction materials to meet farm and household needs on a sustainable basis.

b) Improve household food security, nutrition, and incomes by increasing and diversifying farm productivity.

c) Develop opportunities to establish and operate rural-based enterprises with strong links to sound markets.

It is envisioned that the project will in broad terms lead to: a) reduced risks and vulnerability from erratic and unpredictable changes in climate; b) improved food security, nutrition, and general well-being of rural communitie.

The main objective of this plan is to enable Mozambique to declare itself as free of anti-personnel mines in compliance with Article 5 in the MBC, no later than 1 March 2014. 
The main objectives of APOPO’s proposal are: 
-	Conduct humanitarian demining activities in Gaza Province which will ensure clearance of all currently known mined areas by the end of 2011. 
-	Strengthen its survey capacity by promoting the Mine Free District Evaluation (MFDE) in order to provide a clear definition of the remaining extent of the problem and the anticipated completion date for the entire province. 
-	Employ and train two new survey teams, in the conjunction with IND, with a particular focus on establishing a gender-sensitive residual capacity for explosive ordnances (EOD) and Mine Action within Gaza Province.

column5: AGF - African Guarantee Fund - for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Ltd
column6:
The project goal is to improve access to credit for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) which have the potential to scale up innovations in the following sectors: food security, blue economy, marine litter, renewable energy and clean cooking solutions, and aquaculture. The project will operate over four years (2024 - 2027) in Sub-Saharan Africa, with priority to Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Ghana and Malawi. 

To achieve this goal, AGF will offer the following products: Financial Guarantees will be provided to Partner Financial Institutions (PFls), to reduce their potential credit losses and therefore increase their appetite to finance MSMEs. These guarantees will cover up to 75% of the PFI exposure on loans to MSMEs operating in the above-mentioned sectors. Volume of lending targeted toward women owned/led MSMEs are 30 per cent.

Capacity Development support will be provided to PFls and MSMEs through Capacity Development Partners. For PFls, the support will focus on product development, market research, risk management, customer service and any other activities that will help them mitigate risks or develop their pipeline. For MSMEs, the support will focus on bookkeeping, cash-flow management, and other business skills, helping them to reduce information asymmetry, and thus improving risk perception and its related costs and building a pipeline of creditworthy MSMEs for the PFls.

column6: Consultancy to carry out preparatory work for the introduction of a pilot of a pay for performance (P4P) initiative in a limited number of districts in Tanzania. The purpose of the preparatory work is through a scoping study, prepare for the P4P pilot by identifying and addressing the elements that will be necessary for credible process evaluation and (eventually) impact evaluation of the P4P pilot.  Initially the scoping study will have four main components: (1) An assessment of sources of reliable baseline data in Pwani, Lindi and Mtwara regions.  (2) An outline of good practice and possible scenarios in relation to the design of the pilot. (3) An updated evaluation design proposal including an outline of possible baseline sub studies that could be carried out. (4)  An examination of other performance based funding style initiatives in the country and consideration of potential for linkages and cross-learning

column2: Food Security and Adaptation to Climate Change in Rural Niger, Phase II
column6:
The project is a continuation of NER-15/0001, REDSAACC. The overall goal of phase II is to support the Nigerien government to reduce hunger and improve food and nutrition security for the Nigerien population, through a more diversified and sustainable agriculture resilient towards climate change. 
Specific objective: By 2026, 40 000 vulnerable households (280 000 persons) in 40 communites, in Maradi, Tahoua, Tillabéri, Dosso et Zinder will have equitably and significantly increased their food and nutrition security.
The project is very much aligned with one of the major policy objectives of the government of Niger: “La stratégie de l’Initiative 3N (I3N) « les Nigériens nourrissent les Nigériens », which was adopted in 2012 and is still the main policy framework for addressing food security in Niger.
The implementation of the project will continue to mobilize the two main actors: CARE Niger and INRAN. In addition, CARE Norway, national NGO partners and Noragric / NMBU is involved in the project. NGO partners are selected following an open process based on an evaluation of their performance in accordance with Care Niger’s partnership policy.

column2: Offensive against Al-Shabaab in Southwest and Jubaland
column6:
This project is a research project on how clan and local political dynamics may affect the likelihood for success of the current efforts to counter, degrade and “eliminate” al Shabaab as a threat, and strengthen government presence in today’s al Shabaab controlled areas, focusing on South West State and Jubaland State, with comparison to current developments in Hirshabelle and Galmudug State. The research is based on questions developed by Raad. The research will take place in Mogadishu, Kismayo and Baidoa, including data collection and interviews. The project will produce one open policy brief that provides analyses relevant to Somalia’s and the international community’s understanding of the topic, for a wider audience, plus a brief for the Somali government and relevant international partners.

Outputs:
1. Policy brief tailored to the wider public, ATMIS, and UNSOM, and international partners
2. Detailed report to the FGS
3. Workshop in Halane

Outcomes:
1. Better insights and understanding of how the FGS and its FMS can establish a sustainable
and legitimate presence in the eyes of the locals and clans to stabilise these two regions
2. Clarifying potential ways international actors can support this stablisation process

column6:
The overall objective of this project is to promote better business environments for workers and employers in MSEs. This will be achieved through realising the intermediate objective of developing good practice guidelines for labour and labour related laws for MSEs.

This work will help the ILO to develop training and capacity building tools and guidance on good practices. It will inform the ILO’s policy work in this area and build the capacity of constituents to participate in policymaking. Ultimately, by developing good practice guidance on labour law and MSEs, the project will help governments to develop a legal and regulatory environment conducive both to the formation and growth of enterprises and to the realisation of decent work objectives embodied in labour and labour related laws.

column2: NORHED II Environmental Risk management
column6: The main objective of the Environmental RIsk Management Under ExTremes and Uncertainty-MERIT - project is to strengthen capacities of targeted south universities so to provide high quality education, research and outreach in the field of environmental risk and extremes that meet labour market demands, supports sustainable national socio-economic development and achievement of Sustainable Development Goals. MERIT is a partnership of five universities; Norwegian University of Science and Technology (Norway), Makerere University (Uganda), Uganda Marty’s University (Uganda), University of Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) and Haramaya University (Ethiopia). The regional level project responds to knowledge and capacity gaps with respect to environmental risk, increasing extremes and uncertainty linked to climate change and changing demographic and socio-economic conditions. The fundamental challenge which MERIT partnership seeks to address is to identify sustainable development paths for communities and ecosystems under increasing environmental risk, uncertainties and extremes. Our intended development impact is to provide East African countries with co-created new knowledge and tools that helps in propelling the resilience agenda and realization of the UN SDGs and Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030). Our actions over a six-year period are central to NORHED II and include (i) training at postdoctoral, doctoral and masters level (ii) curriculum improvement (iii) infrastructure improvements (iv) creation of knowledge and policy products (v) initiate and carry out high quality research (vi) creation of knowledge hubs and centres (vii) initiate targeted efforts to integrate gender perspectives in research and education (viii) development of digital resilience tools. Our research will focus on unravelling complexities to provide the best possible scientific evidence and solutions to policy and practise for enhancing resilience.

column2: DR Congo Climate Negotiation Secr support
column6:
Formålet med støtten til klimasekretariatet er å sikre faglig kapasitet og administrative rammebetingelser for det kongolesiske forhandligsteamet som kan ivareta Afrikas posisjoner i forhandlingene.

Prosjektet har tre forventede resultater:
•	Den valgte representanten og hele teamet av klimaforhandlere fra DR Kongo har faglig, politisk og operasjonell kapasitet;
•	den valgte talsperson fra DR Kongo oppnår en effektiv koordinering med forhandlere fra de 53 medlemslandene i Afrikagruppen; og
•	afrikanske land deltar på en effektiv måte i klimaforhandlingene, samt at deres synspunkter blir hørt og godt reflektert i sluttdokumenter fra disse.

The Embassy has entered into a strategic partnership with Save the Children Norway (Ethiopia Office) on management and implementation of the Norwegian efforts to erradicate Femal Genital Mutilation (FGM) in Ethiopia. The strategic partnership is linked to implementation of the the Norwegian Government's International Action Plan to Combat FGM. The agreement includes support to three local/international NGOs in the intial phase. The number of implementing partner could be increased.

Agreement partner: Save the Children Norway (Ethiopia office)
Implementing partners: 
1) EGLDAM (National Committee on Traditional Practices of Ethiopia). Project name: Multiple approaches to stop FGM and other harmful traditional practices in Ethiopia. Year 2006 - 2010
2) Population Media Center (PMC). Project: Radio serial dramas to bring about behaviour changes regarding women's rights and harmful traditional practices such as FGM. Year 2006 - 2009
3) CARE International - Ethiopia. Project on women and girls' sexual and reproductive health and livelihoods rights in Afar, with special emphasis on FGM. Year 2006 - 2009

column2: Partnerships for food security and livelihoods - Uganda
column3: PELUM - Participatory Ecological Land Use Management - local office
column5: PELUM - Participatory Ecological Land Use Management - local office
column6:
The project aims to increase food and nutrition security for small-scale food producers and their communities in Uganda.  The long-term impact is to strengthen climate-resilient local food systems by putting small-scale producers at the center and allowing for the widespread use and consumption of locally adapted crops and varieties (including neglected and underutilized food plants), and promoting self-sufficiency.

Outcomes are:
1) Local biodiversity management
2) Local value chains of agrobiodiverse products
3) Innovative Farmer-Researcher partnerships
4) Collaborative environment for policy change

Main activites include:
1) Research agendas on PPB/crop diversity and local food plants/nutrition; increased capacities for PPB, utilization of LFPs, and agroecological crop management; improved seed storage; strong dissemination linkages to create insterest in/market for PPB and nutrition work, and to stimulate demand for marketing.
2) Production and dissemination of high-quality seed of local adapted varieties; increased capacities for food production and value creation/addition; improved local value chains of agrobiodiverse products; strengthened market linkages among value chain actors; increased market access for farmers organizations.
3) New ways of famer-researcher collaboration; increased capacitites for farmer-managed seed and food systems research; successful co-created innovations.
4) Increased influence through evidence-based advocacy; policy reforms proposed; increased capacities for policy influencing. 

Resources will be allocated toward mobilizing, supporting and engaging women’s leadership roles in food production, processing and marketing to empower women as key actors in food production and address the economic and legislative barriers they face. Power dynamics and paradigms will be targeted, including active work on policy change related to women’s access to land.

column2: Enhancing Women’s participation and Influence in Decision Making in Zimbabwe
column3: WiPSU - Women in Politics Support Unit
column5: WiPSU - Women in Politics Support Unit
column6:
WiPSU seeks to strengthen women’s influence in national policies through their active, strategic participation and by enhancing’s women’s capacities to leverage on positions they currently hold, both at Local and National Government to influence policies to be inclusive of women’s human rights (WHR). The project supports women to attain a critical mass to maintain women’s representation and voice in governance. 

The project therefore not only, seeks to influence policy but to use the current opportunity in the electoral cycle to support women to participate equally in all electoral processes in the run up to the 2023 elections, in order to retain their quantitative representation both at Parliament and at Local Government level. This retention will ensure that women’s voices and influence in policy making is sustained beyond 2023 Zimbabwean harmonised elections.

column2: Entrepreneurship Curriculum introduction in Mozambique
column6:
Countrywide expansion of the entrepreneurship curriculum in Mozambique. The aim of this support is to finance the UNIDO technical assistance engaged to assit the Mozambican Ministry of Education introducing the Entrepreneurship Curriculum Program (ECP)in all secondary and vocational schools countrywide.

A limited piloting of this curriculum took place in 8 schools  of Cabo Delgado province during 2005 and 2006. A total of 3200 students have benefited from the training. Encouraging results have led the Minisistry to adopt the  ECP as a standard subject to all secondary and vocattional schools as from 2010. The gradual expansion needs technical support and UNIDO has developed the ECP and already tested in Uganda and few other countries with a remarkable success.

column2: Partnerships for food security and livelihoods - Niger
column3: PELUM - Participatory Ecological Land Use Management - local office
column5: CIRAD -  French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development
column6:
The project aims to increase food and nutrition security for small-scale food producers and their communities in Niger.  The long-term impact is to strengthen climate-resilient local food systems by putting small-scale producers at the center and allowing for the widespread use and consumption of locally adapted crops and varieties (including neglected and underutilized food plants), and promoting self-sufficiency.

Outcomes are:
1) Local biodiversity management
2) Local value chains of agrobiodiverse products
3) Innovative Farmer-Researcher partnerships
4) Collaborative environment for policy change

Main activites include:
1) Research agendas on PPB/crop diversity and local food plants/nutrition; increased capacities for PPB, utilization of LFPs, and agroecological crop management; improved seed storage; strong dissemination linkages to create insterest in/market for PPB and nutrition work, and to stimulate demand for marketing.
2) Production and dissemination of high-quality seed of local adapted varieties; increased capacities for food production and value creation/addition; improved local value chains of agrobiodiverse products; strengthened market linkages among value chain actors; increased market access for farmers organizations.
3) New ways of famer-researcher collaboration; increased capacitites for farmer-managed seed and food systems research; successful co-created innovations.
4) Increased influence through evidence-based advocacy; policy reforms proposed; increased capacities for policy influencing. 

Resources will be allocated toward mobilizing, supporting and engaging women’s leadership roles in food production, processing and marketing to empower women as key actors in food production and address the economic and legislative barriers they face. Power dynamics and paradigms will be targeted, including active work on policy change related to women’s access to land.

column2: AFIDEP 9th African Population Conference
column3: AFIDEP -  African Institute for Development Policy
column5: AFIDEP -  African Institute for Development Policy
column6:
AFIDEP is coordinating the 9th African population conference starting from 20th to 24th May 2024. This is a forum where research studies on population studies are shared, and policies discussed.
Some the policy makers involved in the conference are members of Parliament (MPs)/legislators. 
AFIDEP has been at the forefront in mobilizing the leadership of parliamentarians and other policy makers in championing sexual and reproductive health as well as population and development issues in Malawi and across Africa. 
The MPs formed the Parliamentary and policy forum which will take part this conference. 
The 9th African Population Policy will promote the leadership of parliamentarians and other policy makers in championing reproductive health and population and development issues.
The Forum is expecting 15 Malawian ministers and local MPs and 30 ministers and MPs drawn other African countries, including the African Network of Population and Development Caucuses. 
The Norwegian Embassy in Lilongwe is requested to support expenses for 9 international members of parliament. The rest will be funded through other sources.

column2: Food Security and Climate Resilience in Disaster Affected areas
column6:
This is a nexus project envisages to address the food insercurity problems through the implementaiton of climate change adaptation, nutrition sensitive agriculture and disaster risk management interventions in five conflict and disaster affected communities in Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Somali and Tigray regions. The consortium lead is Action Against Hunger - USA in partnership with other implementing partners; Denmark Refugee Council and International Rescue Committee.

The project addresse climate change adaptation through the implementation of disaster risk reduction and mitigation interventions such as natural resources management, promotion/introduction of climate smart technologies. Gender equality is addressed as cross cutting under respective relevant programme components eg. crop production, value chain development etc. The programme design looks into specific needs of men and women in the context of the programme themes enabling both genders benefit from various programme interventions.

column2: Emergency humanitarian response and Resilience Programme for Food Security
column6: Support to emergency influx av returnees in South Sudan through emergency humanitarian response and resilience programme for food security. Engage targeted communities in resilience building activities including through community asset creation and climate adaptation using a conflict-sensitive and gender-transformative approach. In the longer term, the contribution will enhance the livelihoods and resilience of communities by engaging them in the construction or rehabilitation of productive community and household assets. These will include crop and vegetable farming, community infrastructure development, environment and natural resource management and adaptation to Climate Change through promotion of adaptive crops such as rice and cassava. The assets will facilitate communities’ engagement in livelihoods and income-generation activities beyond the period of interventions. Activities will contribute to improving food production and enhancing household food security and nutrition status, improving livelihoods, reducing pressure and competition over depleted resources, contribute to social cohesion and contribute to peace, improved gender equality and youth employment. To enable communities to withstand and recover from shocks, activities will be complemented through capacity strengthening and investments on climate risk management services including training on climate-smart agriculture and facilitating access to improved agricultural technologies, especially adaptive crops, promote financial literacy and village savings and loans associations and disseminate climate information through radio and public meetings.

column2: UNMPTF 2020-2024
column3: MPTF Office - Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office
column5: MPTF Office - Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office
column6:
The Somalia United Nations Multi-Partner Trust fund (UNMPTF) is one of the largest country-level pooled funds globally. Currently there are 14 Participating UN organisations implementing programmes under the fund and 11 donors, including Norway, are contributing financially to the fund. 
For 2021 and onwards, Norway has identified the following projects/processes as most relevant.  Supporting Inclusive Political continued support to JPLG (the Joint Programme on Local Governance), continued support to Human Rights Project and finally new support to the Programme for Sustainable Charcoal Reduction and Alternative Livelihoods (PROSCAL). In addition, in order safeguard risk mitigation, optimize and enable to UN to deliver on these programmes, continued support to Enablers is also recommended. Below is a brief description of the programme specific main activities and main objectives of these projects.
JPLG III: The main activities are trainings, capacity building, developing and/or revising policies and state-legislations, development of planning-, budget- and revenue-tools and guidelines and civic education. 
Human Rights Project II: Build on elements of success of the first phase (the treaty body reporting work resulting in further commitments, and human rights engagement/dialogue platforms) but at the same time have a stronger focus on working with and strengthening local institutions. 
Enablers III: The main purpose is to enable and ensure that the UN utilizes the full capacity of its peacebuilding, development, and humanitarian work through joint services (like risk management, training, gender and youth advisory). 
PROSCAL: Response to the UN Security Council resolution 2036 (2012) that seeks international cooperation to ban illegal exports of Charcoal from Somalia. 
Inclusive Politics Pillar: advance in the Somali State-building agenda.

icipe is an African-initiated, based and led Centre of Excellence within insect and arthropod science. icipe has research and outreach activities in more than 40 African countries, including in Norway’s five priority countries for food security; Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, Ghana and South Sudan. It also has activity in DRC Congo, Somalia, and the Sahel, which are of importance to Norad’s portfolio on food security.

The expected impact of the Core Activities is to contribute to poverty alleviation, food security, and human and environmental health in Africa.
The expected outcomes of the Core Activities are:
-	increased productivity, sustainability, and resilience of the agri-food systems in Africa;
-	enhanced research and development and innovation capacity in Africa; and
-	increased influence on global and regional insect science and Four-Health policies development processes.  

icipe uses a One-Health approach to its research integrating four Health Themes: Plant Health, Animal Health, Environmental Health, and Human Health. icipe’s research and development agenda is aimed at contributing to reducing climate impact and strengthening resilience to climate change. It carries out research to fill critical knowledge gaps on climate change impact on ecosystem services and invasive pests and deploys climate-smart technologies.

Gender equality is among icipe’s key values. It strives to empower women in its own workforce and applies gender equity principles across its programs, capacity building initiatives and by influencing policy and its partners.

South Africa, Zambia. The two grassroot civil society organizations CDP and ZNWL seeks to learn from each other’s knowledge and use creative arts as a tool to strengthen their advocacy strategies to improve gender equality and to address and counteract gender -based violence (GBV). They wish to include men as part of the solution in the fight against GBV as well as incorporating the creative arts in organisational advocacy work.
ZNWL has an established programme for men and boys to strengthening their capacity and competence on addressing GBV in their local community. They seek to improve this programme by learning from CDP Trust’s ArtasAdvocacy to provide more interactive and expressive art skills. CDP seek to expand men’s involvement in their advocacy programmes regarding gender equality. ZNWL will share their competence on enabling young men to raise awareness among their peers and community about the negative effects of GBV.

The 2022 project aims to continue with activities from the 2021 project, but also to carry out new results. The new components of the 2022 project are that CDP will work with three community high-schools identified in 2021 where they aim to identify boys to be trained as Agents of Change in the fight against GBV. The 6 peer educators that participated

column6:
The agreement seeks to have a study undertaken to review the annual audit report queries follow up process and as well as develop a baseline and targets for RIDP IV project with OAG Zambia. To enhance a complete understanding of the audit queries follow up cycle and promote the follow up reporting for the public and stakeholders' benefit there is need for a short study to document the cycle and to devise means of assessing performance of the follow up on audit queries. 

Further an analysis of the OAG annual audit report will provide information on the overall public financial management issues and findings obtaining at any given time as well as trends of public financial management status over time when earlier years comparators are brought in. Despite methodological challenges the analysis would give a fair indication of the PFM status and progression over time and help recommend appropriate methodology for future analysis which would close the gap in the use of different approaches and thus to an extent standardise analytical approaches utilized. To this end an analysis of the OAG audit report for 2008 is proposed to be part of the study.

column2: Ocean for Development Mozambique
column6: Ocean for Development Programme Mozambique. The program is focused around four main areas for cooperation: 1) integrated ocean management; 2), environment – marine and coastal, 3) fisheries and aquaculture research and development; and 4) fisheries statistics. The framework agreement between Institute of Marine Research and Norad focuses on component 3 and 4: The aim is to strengthen the institutional and human capacity in developing sustainability in the fishery sector and in the emerging efforts to develop marine aquaculture, as well as improved fisheries statistics systems and infrastructure, as well as improved capacity and expertise for collection, analysing and dissemination.

column2: Facilitation for REDD strategy
column6:
The stated project goal is to ‘ensure that Tanzania actively participates and benefits from global markets for ecosystem services, in particular carbon related activities, as a result of reduced CO2 emissions from deforestation and forest degradation’.  

According to the project purpose, IRA will ‘facilitate the National REDD Task Force, in collaboration with other stakeholders, in developing a National REDD Strategy, Action Plan and implementation processes for the plan’.  

The REDD strategy process requires coordination, stakeholder consultations, the application of lessons and technical inputs from in-depth studies and study tours, the management of available knowledge and awareness creation, the development of monitoring and verification mechanisms, and the set up of financial/incentive mechanisms.  The proposal includes 40 activities under eleven outputs, which form the basis for detailed work planning and budgeting.  A flexible, adaptive approach is planned since not all details of an international REDD architecture and national-level priorities are known, and there may be a need to amend activities in the course of implementing the project.

column2: Malawi Agriculture Cluster Initiative (MACI)
column3: Agra - Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa
column5: Agra - Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa
column6:
The Malawi Agricultural Cluster Initiative (MACI) is a program aimed at enhancing food systems in Malawi by developing agricultural clusters to support smallholder farmers and strengthen value chains for crops like soybeans and groundnuts. By coordinating stakeholders such as farmers, local governments, private sector actors, and development partners, MACI seeks to transform Malawi’s agriculture from subsistence to commercial farming. It will address systemic issues like limited market access, low productivity, and insufficient infrastructure by fostering collaboration, shared resources, and sustainable practices. MACI’s goal is to improve productivity, increase rural incomes, and ensure food security while encouraging investments in value-added processing. MACI includes women and youth in all aspects of the project to ensure their economic participation and leadership in agriculture, as well as promotes awareness and attitude changes to create a more inclusive society.

The project will strengthen smallholder farmers' resilience to disasters through training in risk-reducing measures and access to insurance services. This will help reduce the vulnerability of communities and ensures sustainable development. MACI will also implement climate-smart agricultural practices such as drought-resistant seeds and improved water management to increase smallholder farmers' resilience to climate change.

Impact: Increased economic growth and productivity in Malawi's agricultural sector through enhanced value chain efficiency, increased household income, and resilient livelihoods.

Outcome 1: Enhanced coordination mechanisms and effectiveness of cluster/project actors and delivery
Outcome 2: Improved enabling environment for inclusive markets, trade and finance
Outcome 3: Enhanced capacity of key stakeholders on agricultural commercialization


Target group: Smallholder farmers, Youth and Women, Local SMEs, Farmer Organizations

Focus districts: Lilongwe and Kasungu

column2: GFI Increasing DRM by Promoting Corporate, Natural Resource and Professional Integrity Ghana
column6:
Ghana Integrity Initiative (GII). This will conduct research and the produce policy resources, including a report, policy briefs, a video and factsheets on the gaps in the legislative framework of beneficial ownership as well as the connection between beneficial ownership to IFFs in the real estate sector. GII will seek to engage with private and public sector stakeholders to promote the incorporation of illicit enrichment in Ghana’s Criminal Code. GII will also conduct research including a scoping report on the professional standards and Anti Money Londering (AML)  obligations of gatekeepers in Ghana. GII’s advocacy efforts will focus on the publication of factsheets to use for advocacy with government, private sector, civil society and journalists, as well as organizing meetings with stakeholders to highlight the role of professional enablers in facilitating IFFs. GII will play a supporting role in the organization of journalist training for a small component of the training on illicit money going into the real estate sector in Ghana.


Capitalizing on Friends of the Nations’s (FoN'S) expertise and experience in the extractives sector, their  work will focus on research and advocacy on illicit financial flows in the mining, cacao and fisheries sectors of Ghana. This will include the publication of three reports mapping supply chain issues that limit domestic resource mobilization in each of the three sectors, as well as efforts to engage on natural resource and trade
integrity issues with stakeholders in the private sector, government, media, international organizations
and civil society. Finally, FoN will take the lead on providing journalist training, focusing on education and
investigative techniques to produce analysis of illicit financial flows in connection with the mining, cacao
and fisheries sectors.

column2: beyond the Grid Fund for Afrca (BGFA)
column6:
Over 600 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa live today without access to electricity. The Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa (BGFA) aims to reduce this gap by stimulating and accelerating the emergency of new business models to incentivise the private sector to offer affordable and clean energy access at scale to people living in rural and peri-urban areas. The BGFA programme aims at actively promoting, incentivising and transferring best practices regarding gender equality in BGFA target countries. BGFA does this through requiring awardees (energy service providers) to offer equal opportunities for men and women

Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa forms part of the ‘Power Africa’ initiative launched by former President Barack Obama and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goal 7 as well as the Paris Agreement on Climate. The planned period of implementation is in total six years. The BGFA programme aims, with so far four funding rounds, to establish up to 1.45 million energy connections by 2028, benefiting more than 6.5 million people in Burkina Faso, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Liberia, Mozambique, Uganda and Zambia

column6:
Main objective: To provide a multi-sectoral response for the effective return of peace and the resumption of socio-economic life in the area around the Mont Hoyo, Ituri Province in DR Congo.
The expected effects for the target group of the Project are (Outcome) to contribute to a sense of normality, economic empowerment, and active participation for people in the area.
The planned main products and/or services of the Project are the following outputs: 1) Rehabilitation of 13 km of access road + one bridge in the Mount Hoyo forest reserve (employment of people vulnerable to recruitment in local armed rebel groups); 2) Operational costs for one ambulating health clinic; 3) Distribution of 1500 farming kits; ; 4) peace seminars with local civil society groups and local leaderss; 5) 4 football tournaments and 4 drama seminars.The intended target group is local population affected by insurgency and returning IDPs, local chiefs, leaders of women’s groups, local church leaders and leaders of local NGOs, local youth and villagers (also as spectators and players.

column2: Malawi Department of Culture - Cultural Heritage Programme
column5: Malawi Ministry of Tourism, Wildlife and Culture
column6:
The goal of the Cultural Heritage Programme is to have and promote a vibrant Malawian culture for national identity, unity in diversity and sustainable socio-economic development. The programme is designed to achieve the following objectives:
a) Malawi’s intangible and immovable cultural heritage studied, conserved, preserved, interpreted and promoted for a national and international audience.
b) Malawi’s rich cultural heritage sustainably used in the process of economic development; and
c) Archival collections better preserved and managed.

When fully implemented the programme is expected to have achieved the following five general outcomes:
a) Aspects of Malawi’s cultural heritage described, interpreted, safeguarded and disseminated,
b) Malawi’s cultural identify strengthened,
c) Efficient, sustainable, and easily accessible collection and information storage systems established and operational,
d) Economic stand of artists and communities around heritage sites improved,
e) Capacity and competence of the Department of Culture developed, strengthened and improved.

column2: UN Joint Program for Girls Education phase III, Learning for all in Malawi: ensuring the realization of girls and boys learning in Malawi
column3: MPTF Office - Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office
column6: .UN Joint Program for Girls Education phase III, Learning for all in Malawi: ensuring the realization of girls’ and boys’ rights to quality, inclusive and equitable education and life skills. (JPGE III). The Joint Programme for Girls Education phase 3 is a multi-sectoral programme that aims to ensure that school aged girls, boys and adolescents, especially the most vulnerable, benefit from quality education, thus improving their life opportunities. The programme is a continuation of the Joint Programme for Girls Education (JPGE) phase 1 (2014-2017) and phase 2 (2018-2020). The JPGE is a UN joint programme that involves UNICEF, UNFPA and WFP, with the Resident Coordinator office in a coordinating role. The programme involves the following sectors: education, health (Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR)) and nutrition (school meals). The programme has a 4-year timeframe with a budget of 320 million NOK. The Norwegian Embassy in Lilongwe is the only donor to the programme.

column2: Improving Smallholder Resilience through Customized Climate Services
column6:
Assitance to weather and climate forecast with a focus on agricultural end user.

•	Impact: Increased resilience and well-being of small holder farmers in Ethiopia and Malawi to increasing weather and climate risks
•	Intermediate Outcome: Use of forecasts and agricultural meteorological knowledge in decision making
•	Short-term outcome: Agricultural Meteorological Knowledge
•	Output: Weather and climate knowledge
•	Input: Co-production and provision of information

The consortia consist of NORCAP as a lead, the research institutions NORSE, Christian Michelsens Institute (CMI) and NMBU, and the Norwegian Development Fund. The roles are:

NMBU: Investigate the contextual conditions affecting the scope for delivering and deploying the user-oriented CIS that will be developed under the program. This will lay the foundation for developing inclusive and gender-responsive climate services that harness local knowledge and capacities, enhance climate resilience, and increase food and nutritional security for male and female smallholders.
NORSE: Co-producing needs-based, improved sub-seasonal to seasonal weather forecasts for Malawi and Ethiopia. A social scientist’s team will aim to understand the CS value cycle, while meteorologists and climate scientists will work on the upstream quality of climate information, as well as the downstream needs-based forecast products.
CMI: Will design and implement an impact evaluation in the form of a randomized control trial (RCT). They also have diverse and interdisciplinary expertise and in-depth contextual knowledge about Ethiopia and Malawi.
Norw. Dev. Fund: Impl. institution working directly with smallholder farmers who are actively engaged in crop production, to deliver tailored CIS to each context in a timely and efficient manner. Their work will identify vulnerable context, both in terms of those most affected by climate change to provide the best disaster risk reduction, and to identify gender-disaggregated info.

column2: Feasibility Study Distribution and Storage Phase II
column3: IPAN - International Petroleum Associates Norway AS
column5: IPAN - International Petroleum Associates Norway AS
column6:
The present project (phase II) will be linked to the existing support to the Ugandan oil sector, and will also build on a feasibility study regarding the development of a refinery in Uganda (Supported by Norway, UGA-09/016). This study concludes that Uganda should pursue to develop her own petroleum refining capacity.

This study will assess and analyse systems for distributing and storing petroleum products in Uganda when the proposed oil refinery has started its production,  i.e. a supply system from the refinery to the market (refined products). Uganda’s current infrastructure within the sector is based on an “import only” type of market, whilst the development of a national oil production it will require an assessment of  how transport and storage needs can be addressed under a new scenario. Under the current system Uganda imports almost all oil products through the port in Mombasa; from here it is either transported by road or in pipelines to Eldoret (Kenya) and on road/ train from here.

IPAN has been selected to assist MEMD in the process of entering into a contract with an international consultant.

The Goal of the Program is to build sustainable African civilian and police peacekeeping capacities that are needed in order to implement multidimensional UN and AU peacekeeping mandates.

The Purpose of the Program is to build sustainable African capacity for civilian and police dimensions in the areas of planning, recruitment, training, participation and monitoring, relevant to the UN and AU peace operations in Africa, including African peace and security architecture institutions.

The target groups of the Program are the civilian and police dimensions within the African Standby Force and based on the needs and priorities stated by the AU, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), other regional mechanisms and UN in Africa.

6.	Ownership and commitment to the Project of key stakeholders, both inside and outside Somalia, has been secured.

column6: The project will include both the exchange of staff and final year students from Patandi Teachers’ College of special needs education (PTC), Tanzania, and staff from the social educator [vernepleier] study programme at Molde University College (HiMolde), Norway. The students gather information, work-up knowledge and learn about CRC and CRPD. Based on joint knowledge students collaborate about developing educational material (such as films, posters, leaflets or role plays about rights in practice) targeting children and staff in schools for children with special needs. The participants contribute to practical implementation of CRC and CRPD by presenting knowledge to children and staff in the practicing field, and by communicating with them about current practices and how CRC and CRPD can be put into practice. In addition to physical exchange of staff/students, the project also involves several forms of digital knowledge exchange and collaboration, such as meetings, lectures and workshops, including students and staff at both organisations.

column2: Adaptation of Agriculture and Pastoralism to Climate Change in Mali
column6:
Adapting agriculture and livestock to climate change in Mali
Research Cooperation between the Institute for Rural Economy (IER) and Department of International Environment and Development Studies (Noragric) at the Norwegian University of life Sciences                                                                                                     
Goal: Food security and living conditions improved in central and northern regions of Mali
Objective: Agriculture and livestock in central and northern Mali adapted to climate change

Purpose:
Adapt agriculture to climate change
Develop the agro-pastoral system for dromedary production in the region of Kidal
Develop the flood recession cropping system in northern Mali (Lac Faguibine)
Develop systems for protection of irrigation canals in the area of Lac Faguibine
Strengthening the competence of producers, extention agents and researchers related to adaptation to climate change and agricultural developement

column2: Building Resilience for climate change adaptation and combating hunger in south eastern Madagascar
column6:
The overall objective of the project is the strengthened resilience to climate shocks of vulnerable individuals, households, communities, and systems in targeted communities. The project will strengthen food and nutrition security and provide communities, including schoolchildren, with safe, diverse, and nutritious food produced locally from smallholder' farmers. 

Main activities:
- Productivity support for smallholder farmers
- Financial inclusion package impl. with savings and crop index insurance system for smallholder farmers
- Support and train vulnerable hh to diversify livelihoods with non-farm activities
- Set up food processing units to increase availability of nutrient-rich and safe foods and impl. a social marketing plan 
- Impl. a large-scale social marketing strategy to support demand of high nutrition dense food
- Support existing safety nets programmes using cash-based modality with smallholder farmers and processing units’ food production
- Impl. a large-scale social behaviour change strategy to support adherence to nutrition, WASH best practices and climate-adapted practices

Intended outcomes: 
1: Targ. smallholder farmers and vulnerable hh have improved and diversified livelihoods
2: Targ. communities and schoolchildren have an improved and adequate nutritious food intake/practices
3: Targ. communities have effective and long-lasting utilization of quality basic social services and diversified, nutritious diets

Intended outputs:
1.1: Smallholder farmers have improved and stabilized production capacities
1.2: Vulnerable hh have diversified livelihoods
2.1: Targeted communities and children have access and use of nutritious foods/ practices
3.1: Communities and vulnerable hh have an improved access and use of inclusive, quality, gender-sensitive basic social services

WFP, in collaboration with UNICEF as main delivery partner, will provide support in the South-East part of Madagascar (districs Mananjary and Manakara).

column2: Curious Learning: Expanding the Global Digital Library’s Impact by adding Interactive Content
column6: The project aims to leverage existing digital interactivity and assessment tools to enable additional functionality in the Global Digital Library. This will enable the Global Digital Library to be a comprehensive central repository for high quality, free and open early literacy content. The project will contribute towards formal and informal educational and learning settings, targeting children and particularly girls. The project contributes towards making educational resources more widely and freely available, providing literacy training for children and adults alike to enable their broader empowerment, particulalrly targeting inclusion of margializaed groups such as children not able to access formal schooling, and targeting gender equality in literacy training. The project also includes development of new research-based software and innovative solutions.

column2: Muti-Purpose Cash Support for Families in Crises, Khartoum
column6:
The project aims to provide multi-purpose cash to 2000 households (HHs) consisting of 12,000 individuals from female headed households and people with special needs and poor trapped by war in Khartoum and 400 internally displaced households (IDPs) in Kassala. .

The Project main objective can be attained through the following outcomes:
Outcome 1: People affected by crisis including female headed households have access to lifesaving integrated protection and assistance appropriate and relevant to their immediate needs.
Outcome 2: Humanitarian responses are improved through system-wide quality coordination. SUDO's capacity in managing cash transfers and institutional capacity will be enhanced through training and the provision of communication equipment and digital appliances. SUDO will also enhance its linkage with civil society by supporting and building the capacities of women’s groups and youth volunteers.

column2: UNDP. Partnership on Governance and Rule of Law - Phase II
column6:
The purpose of this programme is to strengthen governance and rule of law within the overall framework of supporting peace in Sudan and enabling post-conflict Sudan to progress towards the Millennium Development Goals.

The more direct objectives are to strengthen institutions, systems and processes of democratic governance: to expand the capacity of national/sub-national/state/and local levels of governance to manage equitable delivery of public services; and to ensure that rights are upheld and protected through accountable, accessible and equitable Rule of Law Institutions.

The Programme covers both Northern and Southern Sudan, and will operate in all the ten states of Southern Sudan, while also covering the Red Sea states in Eastern Sudan and the three "protocol areas" of South Kordofan, Blue Nile and Abyei. The rule of law component is implemented also in Darfur.

column2: Chicken and fish feed and organic fertilizer value chain development using Black Soldier fly-based urban biowaste processing in Ghana, Mali and Niger
column3: IITA - International Institute of Tropical Agriculture
column5: IITA - International Institute of Tropical Agriculture
column6:
The project’s overall objective is to improve the livelihoods of smallholder chicken, fish and vegetable producers and other value chain actors and contribute to improved urban sanitation and climate change mitigation. Specific objectives are to (i) understand the current and future biowaste streams to inform the design of a business model for sustainable biowaste management, animal feed, and organic fertilizer production; (ii) establish chicken and fish feed and organic fertilizer value chains; (iii) optimize the potential of BSF biowaste processing and (iv) build capacities and BSF technology knowhow of youth agripreneurs and other stakeholders.
The proposal is highly relevant as it aims to redirect organic waste from municipal solid waste (MSW), back into the food value chain, and hence utilize a presently neglected resource that otherwise is disposed of at uncontrolled dumpsites and landfills, causing local pollution, pose public health risks and contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
Currently, more than 90% of the waste generated in Africa is disposed uncontrolled. Degradable organic materials constitute the major part of MSW, and with a trajectory of economic growth, rapid population growth, and urbanization, the challenge of MSW management, is likely to persist. Accra, Bamako, and Niamey are among the major African cities plagued by MSW management problems, particularly biowaste management.
Chicken and fish farming are among the most rapidly expanding private sectors in African agriculture and are currently based on the traditional animal feed sources (fish-, soybean- and maize-meal). The rapid growth of this private sector demands increased efforts to find alternative feed sources, competitive in price and quality, without occupying additional agricultural land.

column2: Center for Renewable Energy in Aquaculture (CEREA) - WorldFish
column6:
Development of climate-adapted energy-based innovations and practices in Egyptian aquaculture.
Establishment of a Centre for Renewable Energy in Aquaculture. 
Producers and processors to get better access to renewable energy solutions.
The project harnesses science and technical expertise from multiple institutions to contribute to climate adaptation and mitigation efforts in several ways. The project will only pilot and scale renewable energy innovations with demonstrable climate resilience benefits to the aquaculture value chain. These innovations will be used for climate adaptation and environmental sustainability within Egyptian aquaculture. It is also expected that the innovations promoted by the project will make more efficient use of natural resources, reduce waste and loss, reduce reliance on fossil fuels, lower the carbon footprint of food production, and increase the environmental benefits obtainable from aquaculture.

Norad supports Factor[e]'s work as a risk-embracing impact investor which accelerates innovative companies to drive the shift to an equitable, low-carbon economy, transform lives and generate economic returns. Using a unique approach of deep technical thesis-based investing, actively brokering new technologies, and hands-on venture building at the seed stage, Factor[e] spurs innovation in sustainable energy, agriculture, mobility, and water solutions. The project activities consist of two main tracks. It will firstly build a knowledge base through the work of Factor[e] Labs and secondly build new climate tech companies through the work of Factor[e] Ventures. Labs conducts non-competitive work that benefits the sector, emphasising research and development in sectors related to climate. This aims to build an accessible knowledge base around specific problems in advancing renewable energy and other climate technology and solutions in developing countries. Meanwhile, Ventures leverages the research conducted in the labs to make informed investments, oversee portfolio companies, and deliver hands-on support for the success of emerging technologies. In addition to investing in these companies itself, Factor[e] supports them in attracting further financing for scale. The parts of the programme supported by Norad will focus exclusively on companies and technologies directly related to renewable energy: increased generation, access and/or productive use.

As Factor[e] focuses on innovative business models and technologies it contributes to strengthening local private sector ecosystems, bringing in new technology and increased commercial financing. With a potential focus on companies working at the intersection of energy and food security, these investments may also contribute to strengthening local adaptation to the consequences of climate change.

The project aims at (impact) improved policies and laws to track and stop illicit financial outflows, enhanced fair and equitable tax revenue mobilization and strengthened social contracts in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ghana, Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Cameroun, and Tunisia.

Outcome 1) Capacity of civil society organizations in the targeted countries strengthened to advocate for and engage citizens on tax justice, Domestic Resource Mobilisation (DRM), track and stop illicit financial lows (IFFs).

Outcome 2) Capacity of media organizations in the targeted countries strengthened, to publish stories on tax justice, DRM and IFFs. 

Outcome 3) Capacity of national caucuses of the African Parliamentary Network on Illicit Financial Flows and Taxation (APNIFFT) reinforced. Member of Parliament (MPs) equipped with technical skills to monitor and design supportive policies for equitable taxation to improve DRM, track and stop IFFs.

column2: GW Promoting domestic resource mobilisation for a just energy transition Ghana
column6:
The economic transition from fossil fuels to renewables must not place undue burden on, or unjustly affect, those least responsiblefor the climate crisis. While we must scale up clean energy such as solar and wind power to avoid climate-breakdown, Global South countries where large deposits of lithium, cobalt, and copper are located, must also benefit from this process. To address the problem, Global Witness (GW) will work in partnership with civil society network, Publish What You Pay (PWYP), to convene, strategize, and campaign to expose unfair models of extraction that inhibit DRM, investigate harmful and illicit practices, and address barriers to countries benefiting from the renewable energy transition, while supporting strong governance and a robust civil society enabling environment in those target jurisdictions. 
The project’s objectives are to strengthen Global South civil society and its Northern networks to advance global equity by achieving responsible, transparent management of critical minerals resource wealth to optimise DRM, in the context of the energy transition. Target groups include communities affected by: human and environmental harms from irresponsible extractive industries; the suppression of DRM due to poor governance and illicit financial flows; and climate change impacts.
A South-South CSO alliance will be developed to engage on these issues in collaboration with PWYP and their national chapters
working with communities on critical mineral and energy transition issues in Ghana.
A complementary South-North CSO/NGO alliance will be built, supporting the participation of Global South CSOs in leadingadvocacy within international fora and networks.
GW and partner investigations will ground South-North advocacy at the national and international levels. They will expose how exploitative and abusive economic models prevent Global South countries from equitably benefitting from the transition to a green economy

column2: Facilitation of National REDD strategy phase II
column6:
The stated project goal is to ‘ensure that Tanzania actively participates and benefits from global markets for ecosystem services, in particular carbon related activities, as a result of reduced CO2 emissions from deforestation and forest degradation’.  
According to the project purpose, IRA will ‘facilitate the National REDD Task Force, in collaboration with other stakeholders, in developing a National REDD Strategy, Action Plan and implementation processes for the plan’.  

The REDD strategy process requires coordination, stakeholder consultations, the application of lessons and technical inputs from in-depth studies and study tours, the management of available knowledge and awareness creation, the development of monitoring and verification mechanisms, and the set up of financial/incentive mechanisms.  The proposal includes 40 activities under eleven outputs, which form the basis for detailed work planning and budgeting.  A flexible, adaptive approach is planned since not all details of an international REDD architecture and national-level priorities are known, and there may be a need to amend activities in the course of implementing the project.
