column2: Tackling forced and child labour in Ghanaian Cocoa and Goldmining
column6:
The Project’s expected effect(s) on society is that Children and vulnerable people in cocoa and gold-mining communities in Ghana have increased socio-economic resilience and are protected against forced labour and the Worst Forms of Child Labour (WFCL) (Impact).

The expected effects for the target groups of the Project are threefold (Outcomes): 
Outcome 1: The Ghanaian government at a district, regional and national level has implemented efforts to prevent, identify, and address forced labour and WFCL and to protect vulnerable groups.
Outcome 2: Cocoa companies, traders, cooperatives, farmer groups and gold associations have implemented efforts to prevent, identify and address forced labour and the WFCL in their company operations and supply chains, in Ghana, Cd'I, and globally.
Outcome 3: Vulnerable individuals and groups are resilient in the face of recruitment to forced labour and children are protected against the WFCL.

The intended target groups are vulnerable children, youth, women and vulnerable adults in cocoa growing and gold mining communities.

The present project will be linked to the existing support to the Ugandan oil sector, and will also build on a feasibility study regarding the development of a refinery in Uganda (Supported by Norway, UGA-09/016). This study concludes that Uganda should pursue to develop her own petroleum refining capacity.

This study will assess and analyse systems for distributing and storing petroleum products in Uganda when the proposed oil refinery has started its production,  i.e. a supply system from the refinery to the market (refined products). Uganda’s current infrastructure within the sector is based on an “import only” type of market, whilst the development of a national oil production it will require an assessment of  how transport and storage needs can be addressed under a new scenario. Under the current system Uganda imports almost all oil products through the port in Mombasa; from here it is either transported by road or in pipelines to Eldoret (Kenya) and on road/ train from here.

IPAN has been selected to assist MEMD in the process of entering into a contract with an international consultant.

Main beneficiaries are IDPs and host communities. Women, pregnant and lactating mothers are prioritized recipients through gender sensitized response.

Outcomes
1. Basic needs are met, and dignity increased amongst vulnerable households in El-Genina, Kerenik and Kulbus.
2. Increased access to nutritious food through new and restored agricultural livelihoods.
3. Vulnerable households in El Genina, Kulbus and Kerenik have improved, inclusive access to clean and safe water and improved hygiene.

column2: NORHED II Environmental Risk management
column6: The main objective of the Environmental RIsk Management Under ExTremes and Uncertainty-MERIT - project is to strengthen capacities of targeted south universities so to provide high quality education, research and outreach in the field of environmental risk and extremes that meet labour market demands, supports sustainable national socio-economic development and achievement of Sustainable Development Goals. MERIT is a partnership of five universities; Norwegian University of Science and Technology (Norway), Makerere University (Uganda), Uganda Marty’s University (Uganda), University of Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) and Haramaya University (Ethiopia). The regional level project responds to knowledge and capacity gaps with respect to environmental risk, increasing extremes and uncertainty linked to climate change and changing demographic and socio-economic conditions. The fundamental challenge which MERIT partnership seeks to address is to identify sustainable development paths for communities and ecosystems under increasing environmental risk, uncertainties and extremes. Our intended development impact is to provide East African countries with co-created new knowledge and tools that helps in propelling the resilience agenda and realization of the UN SDGs and Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030). Our actions over a six-year period are central to NORHED II and include (i) training at postdoctoral, doctoral and masters level (ii) curriculum improvement (iii) infrastructure improvements (iv) creation of knowledge and policy products (v) initiate and carry out high quality research (vi) creation of knowledge hubs and centres (vii) initiate targeted efforts to integrate gender perspectives in research and education (viii) development of digital resilience tools. Our research will focus on unravelling complexities to provide the best possible scientific evidence and solutions to policy and practise for enhancing resilience.

column2: Support to UNFPA/partners GBV prevention and response in North/East UGA
column6: The prevance of gender-based violence (GBV) is high in Uganda, with 60% of women of reproductive age reporting having experienced GBV, and in North Uganda the number of reported incidents is even higher. The Embassy, as outlined in its gender plan (2008-2011) is intending to emphasise the effort against GBV. This multi-sectoral programme include areas such as health, social protection, justice and security, education and social change, and aims at achieving progress in the struggle to reduce GBV prevalence and provide adequate response to victims. The programme goal is to increase access to and utilization of GBV services by 40% through more functional, coordinated and sustainable prevention and response mechanisms by 2010. The UNFPA will be overall responsible for managing the project, working together with UNIFEM and FAO, in addition to a consortium of NGOs including American Refugee Committee, Arbeiter Samariter Bund, CARE International Uganda, Christian Children's Fund Inc. Uganda, Cooperazione Internazionale, International Rescue Committee Uganda and War Child Canada.

column2: Matantala Phase Out
column6:
Matantala Rural Integrated Development Enterprise (Matantala-RIDE) undertakes a programme for Community Development with Traditional Leaders in Southern Province of Zambia.

Goal

The goal of the project is to support durable solutions that address underdevelopment in rural areas

Specific objectives include:

- Ensurie that school children have access to improved primary and secondary education as well as life sustaining skills
- Ensure access to quality health services
- Create sustainable rural mechanisms which reduce poverty through stimulating agricultural production and other off-farm       activities
- Stimulate wealth creation ventures to diversify the rural economy and improve food security on a sustainable basis
- Change positively attitudes of men, women and youth in the way they relate to each other and their outlook towards life
- Reduce the impact of HIV/AIDS on families in the area
- Ensure effective implementation of projects, delivery of services and record keeping, accounts and documentation

This is the final phase of the project being financed by Norway and is mainly a phase out agreement.

column2: Close the Gap: Sufficient, Competent and Motivated Nurses and Midwives - Rwanda
column5: RNMU - Rwanda Nurses and Midwives Union
column6: The Norwegian Nurses Organisation (NNO/NSF) aims to create democratic, accountable, inclusive and sustainable organisations for nurses and midwives in four countries in Africa. Cooperation with Rwanda Nurses and Midwives Union (RNMU) goes back to 2013. The aim for this project period is to build the financial and organisational  sustainability of RNMU, and their capacity as an effective watchdog and advocate for nurses and midwives and solution provider for the government, contributing to a stronger and more resilient health system to deliver Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and good health for all in Rwanda. The project includes a focus on nurses and midwives’ equal opportunity to leadership training and positions (gender equality) and the rights of nurses and midwives with disabilities. It also aims to train nurses and midwives in health-related climate adaptation, in the face of increased climate change and extreme weather related health emergencies. Finally, the project aims to train the nurses and midwives to provide the best possible assistance to patients with disabilities and with SRHR to female patients.

column6:
Kenya, Malawi, South Africa, Uganda. The Slum Dwellers International (SDI) network and all affiliated federation organisations (such as CCODE and ACTogether Uganda) have a unifying mandate of seeking to transform slums into resilient neighbourhoods and inclusive cities by collectively driving a women-led, bottom-up change agenda for (1) securing tenure; (2) increasing residents’ access to basic services, housing and livelihoods; and (3) adapting to a changing climate.
The proposed project idea is clearly grounded in this mandate, and focuses on addressing prevailing challenges faced by slumdwellers throughout the network by:

1.	Skills transfer – particularly related to locally-led climate adaptation and the development of climate resilient communities – to ensure that skills, approaches and competencies developed within one affiliate are disseminated across the network.
2.	Leadership development, with a particular focus on developing a systematic way to encourage and nurture youth leadership, with the goal of ultimately establishing an SDI Youth Leadership programme.
3.	Relationship building within the network to facilitate greater cooperation and intra-network mentoring and idea sharing.

column2: Masimanyane Girls Soccer Initiative
column6:
The goal of the Masimanyane Ibhola Ekhatywaya Ngamantombazana project is to contribute towards the prevention of GBVF and the building of social cohesion by using girl’s soccer to create safe spaces for healthy and purposeful participation. 

The purpose of this pilot is to further the whole-of-society approach outlined in National Strategic Plan on GBVF. The aim is to ensure that everyone is involved in addressing GBVF in a systematic, holistic and comprehensive manner. 

Project Objectives
Through the establishment of a soccer academy in Buffalo City, the objectives of this pilot project are as follows: 
1.	To make soccer more accessible to young girls as a sport. 
2.	To challenge and change unhealthy norms and attitudes in young boys who play soccer. 
3.	To empower young girls to fully participate in an internationally recognised sport. 
4.	To develop relevant knowledge, skills, and tools that can used to reduce levels of rape, domestic violence and femicide in local communities. 
5.	To uncover skills that could generate financial income. 
6.	To create safe spaces for engaging in healthy, purposeful sporting activities. 

The Soccer Academy will provide comprehensive training for young aspiring women and men in a safe supportive environment. Our aim is to nurture their skills and promote healing. Additionally, we will ensure that participants have the opportunity to play in soccer matches and fixtures. Furthermore, the Academy will serve as a training center for existing teams, focusing on addressing GBVF issues. 

Results
Our intention is to achieve the following results in the target sites of implementation: 
 .	Visible increase in girls play soccer in public open spaces. 
 .	100% Boys demonstrably understand gender equality on the field, at home and in the community. 
 .	50% Girls are recruited into established national teams. 
 .	10% Annual reduction in GBV incidences across target communities 
 .	5% Annual increase in reporting GBV cases

column2: Nourish Tanzania: Empowering Smallholder Farmers for Food Security and Climate Resilience
column6:
Empowering Smallholder Farmers for Food Security and Climate Resilience (NOURISH Tanzania) aims to achieve resilient food security for SHF households in key regions of Tanzania.
The project focuses on two areas: the central-northern zone (Singida, Dodoma, Manyara) which suffers from acute food insecurity, and Southern Highlands (Songwe,Rukwa) which faces chronic malnutrition.
The project targets 200,000 SHFs and 100 MSMEs and farm organisations, with special emphasis on vulnerable SHFs. With a focus on four high-potential value chains (sorghum, sunflower, common bean, and vegetables), the project will tackle barriers to SHF food security through three interconnected outcome pathways:
1) Increased productivity: strengthening SHF climate-smart agricultural knowledge, skills, and access to inputs and finance.
2) Increased and diversified food supply to local markets: fostering collaborations among market actors, promoting digital solutions, and empowering SHFs and MSMEs.
3) Improved utilization of household resources to provide nutritious and diverse food: promoting nutritious diets, household food budgeting, and enabling women to have greater influence in HH decisions. Improved utilisation of HH resources (time, finances, food, land) to bring about food security and good nutrition outcomes, in particular for women of reproductive age and young children.

SNV will partner with Farm Africa and five local organisations including two local CSOs, RECODA and MIICO.

column2: The Southern and Eastern Africa Trade Information and Negotiations Institute (SEATINI) - Scaling Up Tax Justice
column6:
The project aims at (impact) improved policies and laws to track and stop illicit financial outflows, enhanced fair and equitable tax revenue mobilization and strengthened social contracts in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ghana, Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Cameroun, and Tunisia.

Outcome 1) Capacity of civil society organizations in the targeted countries strengthened to advocate for and engage citizens on tax justice, Domestic Resource Mobilisation (DRM), track and stop illicit financial lows (IFFs).

Outcome 2) Capacity of media organizations in the targeted countries strengthened, to publish stories on tax justice, DRM and IFFs. 

Outcome 3) Capacity of national caucuses of the African Parliamentary Network on Illicit Financial Flows and Taxation (APNIFFT) reinforced. Member of Parliament (MPs) equipped with technical skills to monitor and design supportive policies for equitable taxation to improve DRM, track and stop IFFs.

To enhance expertise on gender equality, particularly the gender dimension of tax justice, TJN-A’s member organisations include feminist organisations and TJN-A collaborates with regional and global women’s organisations such as Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET) and the Association for Women’s Rights in Development (AWID).

The overriding aim of the project will be to build the capacity of local partners in such a way that the ILO’s approaches and tools in women’s entrepreneurship will be embedded and continuous.

Building on the tools and methodologies developed over the previous six years under an Irish funded ILO project in East Africa and South East Asia, the project will work with national governments, constituents and partner agencies to remove the obstacles that women face in starting and growing their businesses. There will be an emphasis on building the capacity of constituents and partners to carry out research, deliver training, and to lobby government on behalf of the interests of women entrepreneurs.

column2: NPA Rapid Response and Social Safety for Local Actors in repression Zimbabwe 2022-2024
column6:
Overall goal
To provide support and safety for victims under danger or threat due to civic repression and ongoing retribution in Zimbabwe.
Objectives
-	To provide, rescue identified victims of escalating civic repression, pre and post –election political violence by removing them from dangerous and threating situations.

-	To provide assessment documentation and information dissemination for the preparation of situation rooms.

-	To build the capacity of women, 65 women’s organisations, journalists, and community human rights defenders’ response mechanisms to pre and post-election violence. 
Target groups: Victims of the protests, CSOs, election observers & monitors, voter education mobilisers, families and relatives of members of targeted human rights defenders, journalists and members of the community perceived to be opposition supporters

column2: Sustainable Tilapia Value Chain Development" in Tamatave, Madagascar
column3: Det Kgl. Selskap for Norges Vel
column6: The expected impact of the programme is improved food security in Tamatave and Antananarivo on Madagascar. This intervention will ensure sustainable climate smart fish farming.

column2: Oxfam IBIS - Fair recovery - Strengthened civil society and media for fiscal justice Regional
column6:
Putting African governments on a path to a fair recovery will require governments, regional and international actors to redouble their efforts to strengthen progressive and gender sensitive tax collection, while at the same time reversing the plans for austerity, halt the debt crisis, and put an end to harmful Illicit Financial Flows that all conspire to undermine public budgets and weaken the link between increased tax and development outcomes. The project will strengthen the capacity of civil society and investigative journalists to push for fiscal justice, putting the financing of the SDGs and a strengthened social contract at its heart. The programme will focus on three countries – Ghana, Uganda and Kenya. In addition, the programme will seek to influence regional economic communities, the African Union, and global institutions and donor countries to create the conditions that will support African governments to pursue fiscal justice in response to the crises.

Objective 1: Tax revenue and public budgets are expanded and made significantly more progressive and gender-sensitive in the target countries (Uganda, Kenya and Ghana).

Objective 2: Regional and global institutions, policies and agreements support the fulfilment of fiscal justice in African countires.

The general objective of the project is “to improve health and environment of the project’s target community”.  The specific objectives are (i) “To improve the system of distribution and conservation of vaccines in the Health Units, as well as the use of gas as an alternative to kerosene and firewood” and (ii) “To improve access to sources of environmentally friendly energy, by communities”. 
 
The core project activities will be geared towards building the capacity of the health national system, through a) improvement of the cold chain and vaccination control system; b) training on the job of vaccinators to improve the quality of services provided to the communities c) improvement of access to Vaccine immunization program and Motherhood Child Care by the communities through better planning of Vaccination Mobile Teams; d) capacitating the local CBOs/NGOs in the districts in order to mobilize and educate the communities for women and childhood health care; e) improve the linkage among health Units and community, through establishment, capacity building and make operational the Community Health Committees as well as direct support to Vidagas to expand their capacity to deliver LPG

The overall NIF project’s primary objective is to enhance opportunities for marginalized persons to benefit from and participate in sports. Emphasis is on the inclusion of women and girls, children/youth, persons with disabilities, and refugees.

Outcome 2) Capacity of media organizations in the targeted countries strengthened, to publish stories on tax justice, DRM and IFFs. 

Outcome 3) Capacity of national caucuses of the African Parliamentary Network on Illicit Financial Flows and Taxation (APNIFFT) reinforced. Member of Parliament (MPs) equipped with technical skills to monitor and design supportive policies for equitable taxation to improve DRM, track and stop IFFs.

Train the trainers program for new and existing vocational training centres.

The main focus area for the project are: 
1) Train the trainers 
2) Improved curricula standards 
3) Develoment of 3-5 pilot centres (Soyo, Luanda and Cabinda) which can serve as future models and reference for a more extensive reform programme of the INEFO Training Structure 
4) Develop a model for enhanced co-operation between INEFOP Training Centres and Private Industry.    

Angolan implementing partner is INEFOP

column2: Civil Society Engagements for Civic Space and Democratisation in South S
column6:
The goal of the project is to strengthen civil society actors so that they engage and claim civic space for democratisation in South Sudan.The project has three priorities:

-  Strengthen civil society's capacity to coordinate and engage with civic and political leaders and claim civic space. 
- Advance legislative reform to enable respect for human rights and inclusion of women and youth in decision-making processes.  
- Promote civic education and engagement with grass-roots communities on civil rights and electoral processes.
 
Indicative Activities:
During the implementation of this project, selected partners will submit applications with tailored activities that will be in line with the broad results anticipated under the project. Some of the indicative activities will include:
o Holding of civic space roundtables which shall bring together key political and security sector leaders. 
o Town hall engagements at a subnational level between citizens and political leaders to discuss democratisation, violation of human rights etc.
o Radio programmes to encourage dialogues on national values, democratic principles and the role of citizens in bringing positive change in the country including through nonviolent means. 
o Use of arts and social media to promote democratisation
o Youth mentorship initiatives through democratic clubs in schools and workshops to ensure that they learned democratic principles and values, because as they say, ‘no one is more dangerous than a misguided youth’.
o Consultative community dialogues and civic education including on pending pieces of legislation including the permanent constitution.
o Civil society strategy and coordination meetings to build consensus on peace, human rights, and democratic-related processes and be able to issue common positions to influence other stakeholders’ decisions.  
o Support to civil society technical teams during the Kenya-mediated peace talks for South Sudan.

column2: SP - Woord en Daad - Bee a Champion
column6:
The project’s long-term goal is to create a competitive and inclusive apiculture sector in Uganda in which smallholder producers, processors and service providers collaborate effectively to increase productivity and efficiency leading to improved revenues and an increase in jobs and incomes.

Overall, by creating a competitive and inclusive honey sector, the project works towards the goal to lower poverty levels (SDG 1: End poverty in all its forms everywhere) and towards new opportunities for employment by lowering the entry levels to start beekeeping as a business (SDG 8: Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all). Beekeeping enhances pollination and honey is a nutritious food product, both contributing to SDG 2 (End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture). Beekeeping is a climate smart practice, and a rich biodiversity is necessary for good quality honey. Beekeeping requires conservation of bee species, tree resources and enrichment of flowering plants for pollination. This contributes to climate change mitigation (SDG 13) and a sustainable use of natural resources (SDG 15). The project focusses on gender equality as a cross-cutting issue (SDG 5) aiming at least 50% of participants as women.

column2: NORHED II Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks
column6:
AdEMNEA (Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks for East Africa) will design, develop, and deploy a flexible network of data gathering and monitoring stations for meteorological data as well as a wide variety of data including audio, image, and video data as well as field reports and telemetry data, integrating both existing sensing platforms and customised components for specific research areas. This is targeting the thematic sub-area Climate Change and Natural Resources.

These data points will be aggregated through resilient and energy-efficient ICT networks from the field to researchers conducting data analysis using machine learning, pattern recognition, and other artificial intelligence and analytical methods in order to support researchers in the application domain.
The targeted application domains will be weather monitoring, building on the results and infrastructure established in the NORHED WIMEA-ICT project, and using this data together with the additional sensing and measurement sources to support researchers initially in the entomology domain. Both weather monitoring and the direct analysis of the presence, prevalence, and behaviour of pollinators and pests will offer important insights into the effects of climate change on natural resources for both the natural environment and particularly agriculture.

column2: Humanitarian Integrated Food Income and Livelihoods Project (HI-FILP)
column6: Caritas intends to improve on the food, nutrition, and livelihood situations in 9 000 households (45 000 individuals) in Bidibidi Refugee Settlement and neighbouring host communities. The intervention includes promotion of climate smart agriculture production, value addition, skilling in income generating ventures and access to markets. The initiatives are designed to increase household incomes of women and girls, enabling acquisition of assets to curb vulnerability to future food insecurity crisis. The target group of the project is a total of 9000 households (70% female and 30% male-headed) households, 70% refugees and 30% in host communities, 5% (450) PWDs. For skills training the target group is girls and women between 15 and 30 years of age.

MMCT was established with funding from GEF to mprovide sustainable funding mechanism for the Mulanje Mountain Biodiversity Conservation project (MMCBP). The goal of MMCBP  is to maintain the vital watershed (headwater for nine rivers) and to benefit local communities by establishing sustainable management of the natural resources vital to Malawi’s economic growth and environmental protection through cooperation between the Forest Department, local authorities and communities. column2: NORHED II Environmental Risk management
column6: The main objective of the Environmental RIsk Management Under ExTremes and Uncertainty-MERIT - project is to strengthen capacities of targeted south universities so to provide high quality education, research and outreach in the field of environmental risk and extremes that meet labour market demands, supports sustainable national socio-economic development and achievement of Sustainable Development Goals. MERIT is a partnership of five universities; Norwegian University of Science and Technology (Norway), Makerere University (Uganda), Uganda Marty’s University (Uganda), University of Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) and Haramaya University (Ethiopia). The regional level project responds to knowledge and capacity gaps with respect to environmental risk, increasing extremes and uncertainty linked to climate change and changing demographic and socio-economic conditions. The fundamental challenge which MERIT partnership seeks to address is to identify sustainable development paths for communities and ecosystems under increasing environmental risk, uncertainties and extremes. Our intended development impact is to provide East African countries with co-created new knowledge and tools that helps in propelling the resilience agenda and realization of the UN SDGs and Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030). Our actions over a six-year period are central to NORHED II and include (i) training at postdoctoral, doctoral and masters level (ii) curriculum improvement (iii) infrastructure improvements (iv) creation of knowledge and policy products (v)  initiate and carry out high quality research (vi) creation of knowledge hubs and centres (vii) initiate targeted efforts to integrate gender perspectives in research and education (viii) development of digital resilience tools. Our research will focus on unravelling complexities to provide the best possible scientific evidence and solutions to policy and practise for enhancing resilience.

column2: Participation and leadership of women in peace, security and recovery
column6:
The overall objective of this project is that women and girls contribute to and to have greater influence in building sustainable peace and resilience, and to benefit equally from the prevention of conflicts and disasters in Mozambique. The specific objectives include:
•	Empower women and gender equality advocates to have greater influence in decision-making in political, peace and security processes, contribute to crisis response, and create resilience. 
•	Build the capacity of the Government of Mozambique to implement Women, Peace and Security (WPS) commitments and ensure monitoring and accountability frameworks are emplaced at national, regional and provincial levels.
•	Foster greater coordination of the implementation of WPS commitments; and
•	Facilitate the access to sustainable livelihoods and socioeconomic opportunities to women affected by conflict.

Access to safe, inclusive, and enabling learning environment is provided with the construction/ rehabilitation of 40 inclusive classrooms and distribution of assistive devices for children with disability.

column2: Appraisal update Mputa IPP Power Plant, substation and transmission line
column6: GOU has decided to exploit the petroleum potential at Lake Albert. The oil concessionaire Tullow Oil has in partnership with Jacobsen Elektro proposed the Mputa IPP thermal power plant, substation and transmission line  as a basis for this development. The proposal builds on an earlier version of the Mputa project that included a mini refinery and clustered develpoment of up to 35 production wells at the Mputa oil field. In March 2009 Norconsult, in a revised draft appraisal report commissioned by Norad, concluded negatively regarding the economic sustainability of the project.. Now, in January 2010, an updated feasibility study for the Mputa project has been submitted, with a number og changes in the project structure, financial and economics. The main purpose of the appraisal update is to assess the new project features as a basis for decisions in GIEK and the Norwegian ODA administration regarding i) JEL application for GIEK for the HFO power plant and transmission line components of the Mputa EPS and ii) the GOU application to GON for financial support for transmission facilities from Mputa to the national grid.

column3: SPRODETA - Small Producers Development and Transporters Association
column5: SPRODETA - Small Producers Development and Transporters Association
column6:
Malawi, Tanzania. The proposed project focuses on empowering young socio-economically marginalised women (especially young, unmarried mothers) with the aim of enhancing their economic self-sufficiency through income generating activities (IGAs) in combination with contextually relevant education on nutrition, sexual and reproductive health, and environmental management. 

Exchange of competencies
Several of the IGAs which SPRODETA has expertise in centre on the use of ‘Climate Smart Agricultural Technologies’, which enable beneficiaries to produce enough food to both meet their daily nutritional needs and to sell the surplus for profit. These technologies help enhance food security at the community level, and also enable the beneficiaries to be more resilient to the adverse effects of climate change on crop production. 

SHALOM has well-established experience in promoting traditional vocational skills training such as tailoring, hairdressing and food preparation/ sale at the community level. 

Participants from SPRODETA are thus expected to share their knowledge and skills on Climate Smart Agricultural Technologies with both SHALOM staff and their beneficiaries (primarily young, unmarried mothers), and at the same time to learn how to promote entrepreneurship using more traditional vocational skills training. At the same time, participants from SHALOM will train SPRODETA staff and beneficiaries on traditional vocational skills, and will similarly learn how to use and train others on Climate Smart Agricultural Technologies.

column6: The main objective is to contribute to capable and competent management of the petroleum sector in South Sudan. column2: MoU 2010. HI. Mine Action Programme in Inhambane Province.
column3: HI - Humanity and Inclusion (former Handicap International)
column5: HI - Humanity and Inclusion (former Handicap International)
column6:
HI aims to conduct humanitarian demining activities in the region of Inhambane in Mozambique. Mozambique's National Demining Institute has appointed HI as the responsible demining unit in this province, as a part of the National Mine Action Plan 2008-2014. The main objective of this plan is to enable Mozambique to declare itself free of landmines, in compliance with Article 5 in the MBC no later than 1 March 2014. HI will conduct both manual demining activities and demining activities with the use of mechanical equipment. The mean is to clear at least 300.000 m2 suspected hazardous areas (SHA) in Inhambane Province, in the districts of Morrumbene and Vilankalos. 
Expected outputs are;
-	Full clearance of all reported SHAs in Morrumbine district and partly clearance of reported SHAs in Vilankalos district in the Inhambane Province. Thus, providing affected communities an environment free of landmines and UXOs.
-	Contribute to social and economic development, in particular by allowing the extension of electricity into the district of Funhaluro and further progress with the overall provincial development planning.

column2: Climate Disaster Risk Management in EDM
column6:
Summary: 
Technical and institutional support to the climate risk work within the Risk Office (Gabinete de Auditoria e Risco) of Electricidade de Mocambique (EDM), to assess and reduce climate risk impacts to electricity infrastructure in Mozambique. 

Context: 
Mozambique is the world's second most climate affected country. as manifiested by cyclones Idaí and Kenneth. EDM owns and maintains the power grid in Mozambique, which is old and many places has fallen into disrepair. There is acute need to build back better, both exisiting and new transmission and distrbution infrastructure - including substations - to increase climate adaptation and resilience, Rapidly changing climate dictates new codes for physical resilience of buildings and equipment, to withstand impacts such as floods and cyclones. Mozambique is a hydropower nation, with more than 60% hydropower notably Cahora Bassa and a number of smaller hydropower plants. These are increasingly subject to changes in hydrology due to extreme drought and precipitation events. This poses physical and an economic risks to EDM and to the population of Mozambique, which heavily rely on hydropower dams for electricity and for basin regulation. Competence on hydrology within EDM is limited. Mozambique is the 13th least prepared country for the effects of climate change.

Background: 
In 2021, Electricidade de Mocambique, with support of the Swedish Embassy, established a Risk Office with the responsibility for assessing, overseeing different aspects of operational and physical risks to EDM's portfolio, and to recommend mitigation measures. Climate risk is one dimension. The work of the unit is still in its infancy and there is still substantial need for further capacity building and technical support

column2: Think Africa Partnership (TAP)
column6: The Think Africa Partnership (TAP) is a multi-partner fund administered by the World Bank Africa region. Its objectives are to promote economic transformation across Africa by supporting African policy-makers to make better use of evidence and knowledge. The contribution from Norad will support a new work programme called Strategic Partnerships for Private Sector Development and Growth (SP4PG). The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) in Ghana will be the key implementing partner.  In 2024, an amendment with explicit focus on women’s economic rights and opportunities in selected sub-Saharan African contexts, with project implementation 2024-2026 (Total budget NOK 126 177 000) was added to the agreement. Project implementors for this amendment are Word Bank Group units Africa Gender Innovation Lab (Africa GIL) and Women, Business and the Law (WBL). The 2024-2026 WEE project partnership with Africa GIL and WBL will contribute to TAP 2023 outcome-level pillars 1 (“Amplify the knowledge base and support African talent development”) and 3 (“Building the bridge to policy impact”), with a focus to strengthen TAP outcomes with specific targets relating to identification of gender gaps and constraints to women’s empowerment in GIL and WBL’s advisory and knowledge distribution activities to advance women’s economic rights and opportunities in Africa and improve the African knowledge ecosystem.

Prosecution of child trafficking offenders; and 4. Partnerships with stakeholders to combat child trafficking. It is planned that through this strategy the project will raise awareness of children and their caregivers on the risks posed by trafficking to children. column2: Ethiopia Interfaith Initiative 4 Forest Conservation & Climate Action - NICFI 2021-25
column6:
The project will build on a pilot project to conserve church forests supported by the Norwegian embassy in Ethiopia. The project aims to contriibute to rehabilitation and conservation of 28 750 hectares of forest, reach up to 21 million people to follow laws protecting forests through awareness and mobilisation campaigns and directly benefit 95 000 people dependent on forests. This will be done by applying the church forest methodology developed in the pilot, drawing lessons from six Ethiopian Orthodox churches and further strengthening the Ethiopia Interfaith Climate Platform (EICP) established in the pilot and ensure this is functioning and advocating for change in, and implementation of climate and forest policies and strategies. 

Main outcomes are:

1. Sacred forests are included into Ethiopian forest legislation and policies
2. Faith leaders and faith communities have mobilised communities to respect and follow the theological rationale and government policy for forest protection 
3. Forests are conserved, and green corridors are established
4. Communities have improved livelihoods without adding pressure on the forest resources
5. Project lessons and learnings shared and practiced at local and global 

The project will have an interreligious approach and work together with the following local implementing partners: 

• The Ethiopian Orthodox Church Development and Inter Church Aid Commission (EOC-DICAC)
• The Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus Development and Social Services Commission (EECMY DASSC)
• Ethiopian Muslims’ Relief and Development Association (EMRDA)

In addition, The World Agroforestry Center (ICRAF) will be a resource partner. 

The project will also work to increase women's participation in local and national decision-making structures and ensure equal participation of women in emergency task forces and in climate resilient assessments. Community disaster risk management plans will be made and regularly updated.

column2: Institutional Co-operation Uganda Timber Growers Association /NORSKOG
column6:
The Objective of the collaboration is to develop UTGA into a viable organisation for the provision of services to the private and public sector for the sustainable development, management and utilisation of forests in Uganda and to contribute to the mitigation of climate change.

The Purpose of the collaboration is to build capacity within UTGA to become a viable organisation supporting private forest investments, especially in the areas of financing, lobbying and providing high quality technical support to tree growers.

The expected Outputs over the four-year implementation period are:
- UTGA becomes a stand alone and sustainable organisation within four years;
- UTGA members become capable partners for further development of the forestry sector and forest industries in Uganda. 

Norwegian cooperating partner: NORSKOG

The Objective of the collaboration is to develop UTGA into a viable organisation for the provision of services to the private and public sector for the sustainable development, management and utilisation of forests in Uganda and to contribute to the mitigation of climate change.

The Purpose of the collaboration is to build capacity within UTGA to become a viable organisation supporting private forest investments, especially in the areas of financing, lobbying and providing high quality technical support to tree growers.

The expected Outputs over the four-year implementation period are:
- UTGA becomes a stand alone and sustainable organisation within four years;
- UTGA members become capable partners for further development of the forestry sector and forest industries in Uganda. 

Norwegian cooperating partner: NORSKOG

Antler EA is applying for support to its incubator/accelerator and implementation of the following interventions during the project period from 2023-2026. Intervention 1 would support Antler EA’s ongoing programs in Nairobi while interventions 2-4 would take Antler EA’s infrastructure in Africa to the next level in terms of reach and impact: 

1. Opex support to run and improve Antler EA’s startup incubator programs in Nairobi 2. Additional portfolio support to maximize founder success rates 3. Make Antler’s IP available to the wider African ecosystem 4. Africa expansion

column2: F&F Bridging the divide: empowering grassroots institutions CFI 2010-12
column6:
The project’s overall purpose is to support the Government of Liberia to develop a national pro-poor REDD strategy which aligns with the national Poverty Reduction Strategy, Forest Sector Reform process, Liberia’s Low Carbon Development plans and Liberia’s Readiness Preparation Proposal (RPP).

Although some progress has been made in REDD strategy formulation in Liberia, particular attention still needs to be paid to raising REDD awareness, consulting on REDD and strengthening REDD capacity for starting and expanding REDD demonstration initiatives. Main goals are to: 

• Empower and enable government, civil society organizations and community-based
organizations (CBOs) in particular to understand and engage in REDD strategy and
project development. We will do this by building from lessons learned on the ground from
integrating REDD with community-based forest management (CBFM) approaches in two
prospective pro-poor REDD pilot sites in Liberia. Particular emphasis will be placed on
REDD awareness raising, consultation and capacity building.

• Disseminate lessons from Fauna & Flora International’s (FFI’s) global REDD
portfolio and this field component locally, nationally

column2: Community stabilization for conflict-affected communities in northern Mo
column6:
Agreement to support IOMs work with community stabilization and combatting violent extremism in Northern Mozambique (Niassa, Cabo Delgado and Nampula), including support to communities in the form of small grants, community revitalization projects, peace clubs, as well as reintegration of former combattants. 

For six years, the province of Cabo Delgado in northern Mozambique has experienced attacks by armed groups affiliated with the Islamic State causing over 700,000  people to be internally displaced and leaving many communities affected by loss, destruction, as well as negative economic and social impact. The insecurity in northern Mozambique is multi-faceted with many drivers including perceptions of historical marginalization and lack of economic opportunities. 
This project will seek to promote community stabilization and preventing violent extremism in Northern Mozambique, particularly in communities affected by conflict with a specific focus on youth, women and girls. 

In pursuit of this objective, IOM will build upon its previous work supporting community-led conflict prevention and creating a conducive environment for communities to live peaceful and productive lives through income generation activities, school-based peace clubs, community-based projects prioritized by communities and support to the Government of Mozambique to discuss mechanisms and frameworks for reintegration of former and eligible non-state armed group (NSAG) members.

IOM will conduct flexible, ongoing, context specific research, and allow this research to drive interventions in the northern, eastern and southern districts of Cabo Delgado, with a potential to expand to  the province of Nampula and Niassa.

APOPO has been working in Gaza for three years conducting clearance and survey work, and has reduced the remaining areas down to approximately 1 045 000 sqm. Central to the framework as a whole is enabling the UN Country-Team to act and deliver as one in Tanzania, delivering on UN reform at the country-level and enhancing inter-agency cooperation.

The UNSDCF covers all 17 SDG's, although only 10 can be listed in PTA. The 10 selected are representative for the aims of the UNSDCF.

column2: Oxfam IBIS - Fair recovery - Strengthened civil society and media for fiscal justice Uganda
column6:
Putting African governments on a path to a fair recovery will require governments, regional and international actors to redouble their efforts to strengthen progressive and gender sensitive tax collection, while at the same time reversing the plans for austerity, halt the debt crisis, and put an end to harmful Illicit Financial Flows that all conspire to undermine public budgets and weaken the link between increased tax and development outcomes. The project will strengthen the capacity of civil society and investigative journalists to push for fiscal justice, putting the financing of the SDGs and a strengthened social contract at its heart. The programme will focus on three countries – Ghana, Uganda and Kenya. In addition, the programme will seek to influence regional economic communities, the African Union, and global institutions and donor countries to create the conditions that will support African governments to pursue fiscal justice in response to the crises.

Objective 1: Tax revenue and public budgets are expanded and made significantly more progressive and gender-sensitive in the target countries (Uganda, Kenya and Ghana).

Objective 2: Regional and global institutions, policies and agreements support the fulfilment of fiscal justice in African countires.

column2: Micro-Macro Issues in Peacebuilding
column6:
This projects aims at producing new knowledge relevant for peacebuilding efforts in Sudan, with focus on the inter-relationships between conflicts at micro (local) and macro (national) levels. It will further build capacity and competence at selected universities in Sudan, and improve the knowledge base for policy debate in Sudan and Norway. The project will provide training for young Sudanese researchers; produce academic publications on basic issues such as land ownership, demarcation of internal boundaries, and position of ethnic groups in the frontier areas; translate publications into Arabic; extend the network of academic contacts; and contribute to a dialogue on policy relevant research with Sudanese and Norwegian authorities. 

This is a collaborative project between the Chr. Michelsen Institute (CMI), the Khartoum University, and the Ahfad University for Women. A previous phase (2005-09) of the project was funded by Norad.

column2: Katapult - Innovation and Entrepreneurship climate and blue economy
column6:
The vision of the project is to strengthen a long-lasting ocean and climate entrepreneurship infrastructure on the African continent, furthering a joint mission of moving more people, capital and businesses towards positive impact. 

Impact – Impact Ventures within blue economy and climate adaptation scale, attract more capital, create jobs and providing products and services in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Outcome 1 – Dealflow generation: A pipeline of startups within the blue economy, marine litter, and climate adaptation is generated and shared with Ocean and Climate Investors and Networks

Outcome 2 – African startups trained to a level where they are investment ready

Outcome 3 – Investment catalyzed into program participants’ ventures (from Katapult funds and other investors)

Outcome 4 - More female founders start and scale businesses.

The project will execute two Pre-seed startups Growth Programs, tailored thematically to support entrepreneurs in the Ocean/Blue economy space through OHA and Katapult, and to support climate entrepreneurs through ATV and Katapult. To accelerate and inspire 60 African-based ocean-minded entrepreneurs and support them moving away from startup pains into the more desirable growth (i.e. scaling and landing growth investment), change the narrative about impact entrepreneurs in Africa by supporting and showcasing successful ocean-impact entrepreneurs. The African Tech Vision (ATV) team has built a highly regarded and innovative program for female tech entrepreneurs in Africa. Through this workstream, the project will scale up and professionalise the program and operations, working in lockstep with Katapult and the project partners and deliver a growth program with a focus on gender inclusion. ATV will empower and support 50 brilliant Climate founders during the 3 years of implementation while keeping a strong gender-lense aiming at 50% female founders

column2: Southern Agricultural Growth Corridor II - (SAGCOT) Investment Blueprint
column6:
The aims of SAGCOT are to encourage and stimulate commercial agricultural growth in selected parts of Southern Tanzania. This will be done by facilitating the development of three to four clusters of high potential agricultural land in which profitable farms and agribusinesses in the Southern Corridor can develop . The essential element of the approach is to establish a critical mass of profitable, modern commercial farming and agri-business, focusing on carefully selected areas and crops with high market potential.

The main sets of integrated activities:
1) Development of a partnership organisation that brings together key stakeholders involved in commercial agriculture
2) Complement donor and government funding with the introduction of new types of finance
3) Development of a project development company able to structure startup or greenfield opportunities and bring them to the point where they are attractive to private investors
4) Working with national and district Government to improve the investment climate to stimulate sunstantial commercial agricultural development

column2: Support to the National Demobilisation and Reintegration Programme
column5: Ethiopia Ministry of Finance and Economic Development
column6:
The project aims to support the National Demobilization and Reintegration Programme (NDRP) of the National Rehabilitation Commission (NRC) to demobilizing and reintegrating ex-combatants with the overarching goal of increasing security and stability in post-conflict situations so that recovery and development can begin. The NDRP will be implemented in Afar, Amhara, Benishangul, Gambella, Southwest and Southern regions of Ethiopia with an estimated number of beneficiaries being approximately 371,971 ex-combatants (there is a possibility of this figure being revised if a peace agreement is concluded for the Oromia region with the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), and if negotiations in Amhara reach a conclusion with regards to the ongoing conflict). There are multiple development partners supporting the programme and the funds will be channeled through a UNDP basket fund. 

The first phase of the project aims to demobilize 75,000 ex-combatants out of which an estimated 40,000 will be women, persons with disability and children associated with armed groups. Moreover, the project has an output aimed at supporting women and persons with disabilities needing MHPSS, SGBV-related and/or rehabilitation support.

column2: NRC's project to increase food security and reduce hunger
column6: The project aims to increase food security in Nigeria, Somalia, and Ugand, through building on existing food production work in the target areas based on on-going or recently phased out project initiatives. Activities will also expand to initiatives that have worked well and that could quickly be scaled up to more farmers. The project aims to contribute to increased agricultural productivity and incomes through; enhanced access to agricultural inputs(land, seeds, tool), capacity building on climate smart agriculture, and support to agriculture-based businesses through value addition, financial education and financial support. The project aims to strengthen climate change adaptation by promoting climate resilient food production as well as increase in local value creation and incomes for food producers. Specifically, this is by promoting climate-smart agriculture technologies, including soil conservation, water harvesting, integrated soil fertility management, crop diversification, and seed variety selection. Additionally, the project seeks to enhance resilience by promoting access to essential agriculture production inputs such as drought tolerant seeds for increased food production and local value addition, increasing market access and incomes.

column2: Community Based Forestry Project
column6:
The Goal of the Programme is to contribute to improve national food security through continuous public awareness on soil and water conservation and sustainable use of natural resources and mitigate the effect of land degradation. Female and male farmers will be involved in the planning, implementation and monitoring of the program. The purpose of the program is to:
- To promote public awareness on forestation and natural resources conservation through National Greening Campaign
- To rehabilitate the degraded project area through tree planting, soil and water conservation measures by individuals and/or community (female and male) members.
- To build capacity on community based forestation and use of energy saving technologies.
- To encourage and promote community forestry in the project area through tree planting by, farmers, communities (female and male) and other institutions.
- To support community nursery for increasing the provision of seedlings at the local community level.
- To supply forestry tools to females and males participants in the communities within the project area.
- To distribute improved traditional stove (mogogo) to households in the project area.

column2: W. Giertsen - Affordable Energy for Agricultural Food Chains in Africa
column6:
The feasibility study will focus on increasing access to affordable energy for agricultural food chains in Africa based on PV
self-consumption energy systems, with an initial industry focus on poultry in the East African region. Self-consumption energy systems are PV energy systems designed where the amount of energy produced is directly consumed by the PV system owner. With many African countries shifting from a vegetable-based to a protein-based diets, the poultry industry is expected to grow between 8%-10% annually as the protein of choice/preference. Africa and Eastern Africa in particular is well positioned to supply this demand. However, a thorough mapping and analysis is required to understand, develop, design and scope the best PV self-consumption system, with the goal of supporting the greening and productivity, while reducing its current CO2 footprint.

column2: National Archives Angola
column6:
Support to the "Arquivo Historico de Angola" or the Angolan National Archive.  The support started in 2003 with two separate sub-projects, 1)  Electronic cataloguing of core-documents from the colonial administration, and 2)  Gathering of oral historical sources:  The massacre at Baixa de Kasanje 1960 – 1961. 
 The current project will broadcast historical material from the National Archices in national languages thru the National Radio.  A main objective of the project will be to assist the Archives to adapt the information to popular consumption, as well as contribute to reinforcing the common cultural heritage of the people of Angola.

The main objective of the general support  is to strenghten the National Archives as an institution and to enhance the preservation of important, historical information, and secondly to improve the services and material it can offer to the public.

The support will be channelled through a third entity in order to avoid entering into a bilateral "state-to-state" agreement.  In this case, the funds will be channelled through the NGO Centre for Common Ground (CCG).

Support to AERC. AERC is  a public not- for-profit organization devoted to advanced economic policy research and training. AERC's mission is to strengthen local capacity for conducting independent, rigorous inquiry into the problems facing the management of economies in sub-Saharan Africa. The mission rests on two basic premises. First, that development is more likely to occur where there is sustained sound management of the economy. Second, that such management is more likely to happen where there is an active, well-informed group of locally based professional economists to conduct policy-relevant research. Specifically, AERC intends to:
•	Enhance the capacity of locally based researchers to conduct policy-relevant economic inquiry, 
•	Promote the retention of such capacity, and 
•	Encourage its application in the policy context. 

Through AERC Norad supports Master and PhD students and research

column6:
Co-financing with Sida of a Integrated Water Resource Management and Development Project for the  Kagera, the Mara and the Sio- Mabala-Malakisi Basins. 

The three mentioned basins forms part of the wider Nile Basin Catchment, and the projects have been prioritied and formulated within the Nile Equatorial Lakes Subsidiary Programme (NELSAP), under the Nile Basin Initiative (NBI).

The projects have been tailored for the three individual transboundary basins, to achive the following common objectives: 

1. To establish a suitable framework for joint management of the water resources. 
2. To develop a joint integrated water resources management strategy, and build capacity for its implementation and upgrading. 
3. To implement a selected number of small-scale investments.

The projects will be implemented by a PMU for each of the three basins, and under the overall political and technical guidelines of the NBI cooperative structures.

column2: CLO - Continuing the Gains from the KNDR Process
column3: UNOPS - UN Office for Project Services
column6:
The agreement partner and project service provider is the United Nations Office of Project Services (UNOPS).The project "Continuting the gains from the Kenya National Dialogue and Reconciliation (KNDR) Process" will be implemented by the Coordination and Liason Office (CLO) on behalf of the Panel of Eminent African Personalities. 
The overall goal of the project is to promote sustainable peace, stability and justice in Kenya through the rule of law and respect for human rights. The objective is to support the effective and comprehensive implementation of the KNDR agreements. A logical framework for the project describes the different activities and outcome indicators under each of the three planned outputs:
1) Political dialogue maintained between the Coalition Government and the AU-Panel.
2) The findings of the comprehensive and coordinated monitoring and evaluation system for the implementation of the KNDR agreements are processed and analysed by key stakeholders.
3) Best practices and lesson learned from the KNDR process are analysed, documented and disseminated so that replication of good practices is ensured.

Project description: Developing and growing the GALA Queer Archive’s cultural and academic public programming.

Impact, Overall Goal: GALA’s overall objective is to increase knowledge, awareness and pride in/of LGBTQ+  histories, identities and lives in Africa. Our various project streams are aimed at the general public, queer historians and researchers, academics, artists, writers, queer youth/students, activists. These groups are reached through our archive collections, library, publications and cultural and educational programming.

The library space doubles as GALAs offices and is used for seminars, staff meetings, archive students and safe space for students. Supporting GALA’s Cultural Programming.

Persons with disabilities (PwD) are among the target groups of the project. The programme will be implemented in six countries: Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda.

column2: Digital assistive technology accelerator programme and linking startup ecosystems in Norway and Kenya
column3: GDI Hub - Global Disability Innovation Hub
column5: GDI Hub - Global Disability Innovation Hub
column6: Incubation program for Assistive Technology for disabled. The Project’s planned effect(s) on society (Impact) is to create a more conducive enabling environment for entrepreneurs, start-ups, and SMEs in the field of Assistive Technology (AT), and better access to local and foreign investments in the AT sector. It will foster entrepreneurs by running programmes to help start-ups grow, and simultaneous work to build capacity and raise awareness within the ecosystem and among investors whilst deepening digital fluency among disabled innovators. Fundraising efforts will aim both at securing follow-on investment for accelerator graduates, as well as opportunities to co-fund accelerator activities. This will also include deepening cooperation with existing accelerators in the region. Through a rigorous reporting structure, the project will amplify the learnings to a wide audience. Specifically, it will connect: the Kenya and Norway innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystems, The intended target groups are high growth potential AT start-ups in Kenya and East Africa

column2: UNICEF Girls and Nomadic Education in Eastern and Transitional Areas
column6:
The project's overall goal is to bridge gender disparities in basic education through the child-friendly schools approach, and thus contribute to achieving the Millennium Development Goals 2 and 3 towards UPE and gender equality and empowerment of girls.

The target group is 100,000 learners primarily girls and nomadic children in Eastern Sudan and the Three Transitional Areas of South Kordofan, Abyei and the Blue Nile State. Expected results include establishment of five pilot boarding upper basic and secondary schools for girls in nomadic communities; at least 100,000 girls and nomadic children enrolled in 250 remote rural community schools by 2012; a reduction of number of untrained teachers; reduced number of children dropping out of school; and 50,000 girls participating in extra-curricular activities, including outreach to community education on child rights, health and hygiene education.

column6:
The overall objective is strengthened governance and increased compliance with national and international laws related to fisheries operations in West Africa, contributing to the conservation and optimum use of living marine resources.
In the Gulf of Guinea, Illegal fishing accounts for a significant share of the catches and therefore affect jobs creation and contribute to poverty increase in fishing communities which are responding in various ways to the impacts of illegal fishing and declining fish stocks. Through the Fisheries Committee for the West Central Gulf of Guinea (FCWC), the countries of Liberia, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Benin, and Nigeria, work to ensure a sustainable development of the fisheries resources in the FCWC Convention Area. The project proposal builds on the foundations and progress made to date under previous phase to specifically meet these objectives:
Outcome 1 - FCWC Member States are cooperating and effectively acting to reduce illegal fishing and associated crimes at the national, regional, and international level
Outcome 2 – The FCWC is effectively achieving its mandate to promote cooperation among its Member States to ensure the conservation and optimum use of their living marine resources

column2: NASFAM: Enhancing Member Livilihoods through an Alighned Self-Sustaining Enterprise
column3: NASFAM - National Smallholder Farmers Association of Malawi
column5: NASFAM - National Smallholder Farmers Association of Malawi
column6:
Supporting smallholder farmers to produce for pre-identified specific, reliable and more-rewarding markets, with particular focus on food processors, value addition and export markets including fair trade sector. The immediate objective is to transision the NASFAM System into a financially sustainable enterprise. In the long term the project aims to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers in Malawi and subsequently contribute towards resilient sustainable food systems and poverty reduction. 

Outcomes
a) improved smallholder farmers access to profitable markets - to be achieved through promotion of contract farming, collective marketing and provision of incentives.
b) increased member yields in an environmentally sustainable manner - climate smart agriculture will be promoted
c) a more engaged and socio-economically empowered membership built.
d) a robust and effective system that support the NASFAM business model developed.
e) Financial sustanability of the NASFAM System achived. value addition and agroprocessing of maize, rice, groundnuts, chillies will be intensified.

Total budget for the entire programme is NOK159.328 million. Part of this will be financed by Irish Aid who will provide the sum of NOK75 million over a period of five years.

column6: Center for the Development of People has experienced two break in-s and two unauthorized razzias of their office since December 2009. Their health campaign to raise awareness conserning HIV and AIDS amongst men who have sex with men, although important and recognized by the Malawian authorities, has been perceived to be improper by some, and CEDEP has been accused of spreading pornographic material. CEDEP is now moving to Lilongwe and need an office for the next few months, as well as some office equipment. Most of their office equipment has been destroyed by vandals, and campaign material has been confiscated by the police. The Embassy will provide CEDEP with funding for office relocation to get CEDEP started until funding from other partners will be available later this spring.

column2: Climate Change Impacts, Adaptation and Mitigation in Tanzania (CCIAM)
column6:
Research and education programmes on climate change with a focus on reduced deforestation/REDD initiative. The programme will be implemented by Sokoine University of Agriculture in collaboration with University of Dar es Salaam, Ardhi University, Tanzania Meterological Agency and Norwegian Institutions. The partners in Norway will be represented through UMB. The programme will have a specific focus on research related to a successful implementation of the REDD initiative. The programme will develop linkages with the NGO pilot programmes funded by Norway. The research will be based on competitive research grants to participating institutions. It is estimated that 17 PhD and 50 MSc will be trained under the capacity building component of the programme. 

The programme was intended to start in July 2009 but due to negotations regarding the bilateral agreement it will only start on 1 January 2010. 

The CCIAM programme is funded from the special grant from Norway for climate change mitigation pledged in the UNFCCC COP in Bali in December 2007. It is part of the MoU signed between Norway and Tanzania in April 2008.

African Journals Online (AJOL) is a non-profit organization working for increased quality, quantity, accessibility, recognition, and use of African-published research. AJOL is an online publishing platform – based on Free and Open-Source software – of peer-reviewed, African research journals in all research disciplines and in several African languages. AJOL provides quality assessment of and support to hundreds of research journals throughout the African continent, journal-specific mentoring, online training and webinars, online hosting of journals and Open Access resources. It also promotes the voice and representation of African academic publishing in global forums.

AJOL’s vision is that African research increasingly contributes to real world constructive change and its impact goal is a more equitable role for African journals within the global research publishing landscape. 

AJOL is a critical open content host and journal index for the African continent and has the potential to influence global efforts towards Open Science.

column2: UiO Support of TFESSD Seminar Tanzania 2011
column6:
The Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Finnish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Norad in cooperation with the World Bank are arranging a seminar in Tanzania in connection with the Norwegian and Finnish owned Trust Fund for Environmentally and Socially Sustainable Development. The objective of the seminar is to bring together donors, Bank staff, and Tanzanian and East African counterparts to discuss progress and challenges in environmental, poverty, and social aspects in which the TFESSD has been providing support, foster south-south learning, and gain a better understanding of knowledge transfer and capacity building in Africa. The seminar will focus on how practical knowledge and capacity can promote synergies between environmental and social sustainability in Tanzania and neighboring countries. 

Norad and the Norwegian MFA have invited Dan Banik from the University of Oslo to participate as advisor and will cover his travel expenses and logdging per diem.

column2: Agricultural Growth and Improvement For Livelihood Enhancement AGILE
column6: The Agricultural Growth and Improvement for Livelihood Enhancement (AGILE) project aims to enhance the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, women and youth living within the Nawuni Sub-Catchment of the White Volta River Basin (WVRB), through food production, improved agricultural practices, finance and market access. Overall impact of the planned project is the increased crop yield and household incomes of farming families living in the Nawuni Sub-Catchment area in the White Volta River Basin.Target Group: The project will target an estimated 3,325 people in six (6) communities (three each in Savelugu Municipal and Kumbungu District) which includes 300 community water user group members (50 in each of the 6 communities), 30 local water committee members (5 in each of the 6 communities), 25 sub-basin committee members, 420 smallholder farmers (70 in each of the 6 communities, including women and youth), 30 Community Based Advisors / Private Service Providers (5 in each of the 6 communities), and 2,520 people smallholder farmer households. The project will also indirectly benefit over 31,000 people living within the six (6) project communities in Savelugu Municipal and Kumbungu District. The project aligns with national and international commitments to climate resilience, gender equality, and biodiversity conservation. It promotes climate-smart agriculture to enhance food security, strengthen resilience, and protect natural resources (SDG 2 & SDG 13). Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) improves governance, protects riparian zones, and fosters social cohesion, ensuring sustainable land and water use (SDG 6 & SDG 15). Strengthening market access and inclusive financing empowers smallholder farmers, especially women and youth, fostering economic growth and gender equality (SDG 5 & SDG 8).

column2: GW Promoting domestic resource mobilisation for a just energy transition DRC
column6:
The economic transition from fossil fuels to renewables must not place undue burden on, or unjustly affect, those least responsiblefor the climate crisis. While we must scale up clean energy such as solar and wind power to avoid climate-breakdown, Global South countries where large deposits of lithium, cobalt, and copper are located, must also benefit from this process. To address the problem, Global Witness (GW) will work in partnership with civil society network, Publish What You Pay (PWYP), to convene, strategize, and campaign to expose unfair models of extraction that inhibit DRM, investigate harmful and illicit practices, and address barriers to countries benefiting from the renewable energy transition, while supporting strong governance and a robust civil society enabling environment in those target jurisdictions. 
The project’s objectives are to strengthen Global South civil society and its Northern networks to advance global equity by achieving responsible, transparent management of critical minerals resource wealth to optimise DRM, in the context of the energy transition. Target groups include communities affected by: human and environmental harms from irresponsible extractive industries; the suppression of DRM due to poor governance and illicit financial flows; and climate change impacts.
A South-South CSO alliance will be developed to engage on these issues in collaboration with PWYP and their national chapters
working with communities on critical mineral and energy transition issues in the DRC, 
A complementary South-North CSO/NGO alliance will be built, supporting the participation of Global South CSOs in leadingadvocacy within international fora and networks.
GW and partner investigations will ground South-North advocacy at the national and international levels. They will expose how exploitative and abusive economic models prevent Global South countries from equitably benefitting from the transition to a green economy

column2: Eradicationg Child Labour in Uganda
column6:
The project will contribute to eradicating child labour in Uganda, protecting children in over 12,000 families. The project will focus on two regions of Uganda where child labour is very common.

1. Busoga sub-region (Jinja, Bugiri, Kaliro and Iganga) has the highest rate of child labour in the country, with 38% of children in work, and agriculture the main sector (UNICEF’s Child Poverty report 2019), particularly in sugarcane and rice production, as
children are a source of cheap labour with the nature of the work extremely hazardous.

2. Central region, specifically Greater Kampala Metropolitan area. Older children migrate from the rural areas to seek paid employment in a number of informal sector activities including petty trading, domestic work, trading, hawking, bar and restaurant
work, and prostitution; 88.8% of working children in Kampala are involved in hazardous work, 53.4% are paid child labourers (street vendors, porters, scrap collectors) (National Labour Force and Child Activity Report, 2012).
In both areas, poverty is one of the main drivers of child labour. This situation has worsened with the outbreak of COVID-19 due to the strong measures undertaken by the Government of Uganda including lockdown of the economy to control the spread of the
virus. Poor understanding of child rights and the legal framework which could protect them amongst both rights holders and duty bearers is a further barrier to sustained change.

The project will enable over 12,000 families to be more resilient in the face of recruitment to child labour though increasing understanding on preventing and combating child labour - with community taskforces, sensitised duty bearers, and awareness-raising in the media. It will strengthen social protection of targeted families, improving incomes and access to skills, establish public/private partnerships including a child-free zone in UMA Industrial Park; thus improving the implementation of ILO conventions on child labour.

column2: NRC's project to increase food security and reduce hunger
column6: The project aims to increase food security in Nigeria, Somalia, and Ugand, through building on existing food production work in the target areas based on on-going or recently phased out project initiatives. Activities will also expand to initiatives that have worked well and that could quickly be scaled up to more farmers. The project aims to contribute to increased agricultural productivity and incomes through; enhanced access to agricultural inputs(land, seeds, tool), capacity building on climate smart agriculture, and support to agriculture-based businesses through value addition, financial education and financial support. The project aims to strengthen climate change adaptation by promoting climate resilient food production as well as increase in local value creation and incomes for food producers. Specifically, this is by promoting climate-smart agriculture technologies, including soil conservation, water harvesting, integrated soil fertility management, crop diversification, and seed variety selection. Additionally, the project seeks to enhance resilience by promoting access to essential agriculture production inputs such as drought tolerant seeds for increased food production and local value addition, increasing market access and incomes.

UNDP programme title: Multi-donor Assistance for the 2005 National Election in Ethiopia.

Implementing institution: Electoral Reform International Services (ERIS)

Norwegian and/or other partner institution: None

Goal:	Contribute to the development of a free, open and accountable political system of governance and the consolidation of democracy in Ethiopia through the organisation and conduct of the forthcoming national elections in May 2005, in accordance with the constitution.

Project Summary
The project ‘Reintegration Assistance to Liberia DDRR Programme Residual Caseload Beneficiaries’ is designed to provide reintegration support to up to 8,789 ex-combatants who have not received any assistance from the DDRR Programme and who are still in need of reintegration assistance, by providing them with reintegration support aimed at increasing their probability for employment across Liberia. The support will be provided using funds from the Norwegian Government equivalent to US$ 7.03 million.
