column2: NORHED II Environmental Risk management
column6: The main objective of the Environmental RIsk Management Under ExTremes and Uncertainty-MERIT - project is to strengthen capacities of targeted south universities so to provide high quality education, research and outreach in the field of environmental risk and extremes that meet labour market demands, supports sustainable national socio-economic development and achievement of Sustainable Development Goals. MERIT is a partnership of five universities; Norwegian University of Science and Technology (Norway), Makerere University (Uganda), Uganda Marty’s University (Uganda), University of Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) and Haramaya University (Ethiopia). The regional level project responds to knowledge and capacity gaps with respect to environmental risk, increasing extremes and uncertainty linked to climate change and changing demographic and socio-economic conditions. The fundamental challenge which MERIT partnership seeks to address is to identify sustainable development paths for communities and ecosystems under increasing environmental risk, uncertainties and extremes. Our intended development impact is to provide East African countries with co-created new knowledge and tools that helps in propelling the resilience agenda and realization of the UN SDGs and Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030). Our actions over a six-year period are central to NORHED II and include (i) training at postdoctoral, doctoral and masters level (ii) curriculum improvement (iii) infrastructure improvements (iv) creation of knowledge and policy products (v) initiate and carry out high quality research (vi) creation of knowledge hubs and centres (vii) initiate targeted efforts to integrate gender perspectives in research and education (viii) development of digital resilience tools. Our research will focus on unravelling complexities to provide the best possible scientific evidence and solutions to policy and practise for enhancing resilience.

column2: Conflict Affected States in Africa Program
column6:
IFC-CASA was established in 2008 as a 5year multidonor trust fond for fragile and conflictaffected states in Africa.

The objectives of IFC in implementing the Program are:

(i)	To contribute to peace and stability in fragile and conflict affected countries in Africa through private sector-led growth.
(ii)	To form partnerships with selected donors, including the Donor, which will aim to complement the strategies of such donors and IFC;

CASA aims at developing and implementing integrated country strategies together with private sector, responsible governments, multi- and biltareal donors.Focus areas are improved framework conditons,SME competitiveness, reestablishment of financial markets and institustions, privat sector participation in public infrastructure and services.

CASA has been part of the Norwegian Trust Fund for Private Sector and Infrastructure (NTF-PSI), but was agreed upon at the Annual Consultations to the singled out along with 5 other global programmes to be administered outside the NTF PSI over bilateral agreements.

column2: UNCDF- Decentralised climate investment
column6: The project is implemented through an agrement with UN-Tanzania,The Local Climate Adaptive Living (LoCAL) Facility designed and hosted by the UN Capital Development Fund serves as a mechanism to integrate climate change adaptation into local governments’ planning and budgeting systems, increase awareness of and response to climate change at the local level, and increase the amount of finance available to local governments for climate change adaptation. LoCAL combines performance-based climate resilience grants (PBCRGs), which ensure programming and verification of climate change expenditures at the local level, with technical and capacity-building support. It is implemented at the local government level, under the leadership of the President’s Office-Regional Administration and Local Government (PO-RALG), in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP) and Vice President’s Office (VPO), with financial support from the EU and the Government of Sweden. The project will contribute to the strengthening of resilience in the selected districts and to the integration of climate change concerns with the recipient countries’ development objectives through capacity development at local government authorities level.The pilot phase implementation will potentially benefit more than 800,000 people, particularly women. Following the pilot phase, LoCAL is expected to be scaled-up to other districts.

column2: CAFI Invest
column6:
The "CAFI Invest" project focuses on financing projects and companies that aim to reduce deforestation and promote sustainable land-use practices across Central Africa. The project is aligned with national REDD+ strategies and CAFI's results framework through targeted interventions in sustainable agriculture, agroforestry, and forest conservation. 
CAFI Invest follows a three-pronged strategy operationalized through the creation of three separate investment windows. Through these windows Catalytic aims to accelerate capital flow towards sustainable land use, agroforestry, and sustainable forest management respectively, addressing at the same time both environmental and socio-economic challenges in Central Africa 

Investment Windows: 

Window 1: Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) – This window incentivizes communities and landowners to preserve forest ecosystems by providing financial rewards based on the delivery of ecosystem services. 

Window 2: Technical Assistance and Capital Acceleration Facility – This window provides direct technical assistance grants, venture debt, and venture capital to projects and companies at an early stage of development. 

Window 3: Investment Fund – This window uses a blended finance approach to de-risk and catalyze significant additional private sector investments in various sustainable practices.

TI-U will further have a
supporting role in our work regarding corporate transparency in Uganda. , TI-U will focus on beneficial ownership as it connects to the real estate sector, producing a report and fact sheets on the issue and engaging with stakeholders to raise awareness for the issue of illicit financial flows in the real estate sector in Uganda.

column2: UNIDO - Quality Policy and compliance infrastructure development
column6:
Sierra Leone has been a member of WTO since 23 July 1995. However, the country does not dispose
of a National Quality Policy; a well developed Competent Authority for fisheries to ensure the quality
and safety of the exported fishery products which is one of the major exports of the country or basic
capabilities for micro-biological and chemical testing of products and facilities for equipment calibration
for ensuring the accuracy of measurement. As a consequence of the non-existence such infrastructure
local population is at various risks through imported sub-standard products whilst exports are
inevitably more difficult and the country is thus not in a position to meet the EU export requirements for fisheries and capitalize on this area of exports which is an important trade flow for developing
countries around the world.
This project will focus on
a) Supporting the development of a National Quality Policy
b) Supporting the development of a Competent Authority for fisheries exports and
c) Upgrading and development of the national testing laboratory infrastructure with respect to
chemical, microbiological, metrology/calibration laboratories.

column2: Norturing Sustainable Oil and Gas Supply Industry in Ghana
column6:
In consultation with Ghanaian partneres SINTEF has worked out a framework for joint research and development of sustainable oil supply industry in Ghana.  The overall objective is to design, anage and recommend policy instruments that will enable Ghana to establish and drive local support companies for its emerging oil and gas industry.  The project will anlayse and develop specific improvement proposals for existing companies and facilitate intercompany cooperation/cluster development. It will involve local key actors inn the establishment of a network for joint learning and development to increase local content.  There will be capacity building in the leading national Science and Technology Policy Research Institute (STEPRI) and knowledge transfer to the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) to address the challenges of policy formulation, implementation and review in line with Ghana's development aganda and to create the conditions for stimulating local innovations in the oil sector.

Shared funding between NUMI and Oil for development 50/50%

column2: One UN COVID-19 Response Plan for Nigeria Basket Fund
column6:
One UN Covid-19 Response Plan Basket Fund (the basket fund) will support the government of Nigeria’s (GoN) National Covid-19 multi sectoral response plan. It will contribute to optimum care of confirmed covid-19 cases and containment of spread of the outbreak, including through improvements in health infrastructure such as WASH facilities, and provide access to essential health services. It will also contribute to reducing other socio-economic, including through food security interventions, and conflict related impacts of the outbreak. 
IMPACT: Nigeria response to the COVID-19 pandemic supported by ensuring optimum care of the confirmed cases and contain further spread of the outbreak and pathway for rapid recovery and resilience is established
OUTCOME: Rapid implementation of Nigeria’s National COVID-19 Multi-Sectoral Pandemic Response Plan strengthened
Output 1: Rapid procurement of disease commodity packages for surveillance, prevention and control, and clinical management improved
Output 2: Complementary ongoing Risk Communication Strategies for sustained community engagement and cooperation are supported
Output 3: Development of tailored and decentralized response strategies at state-level aligned to the coordinated framework at the Federal level is supported
Output 4: Access to essential health services maintained (this output includes improvement of WASH facilities)
Output 5: Pro-active early recovery, social protection and cohesion is enhanced, targeting vulnerable groups supported (this output includes cash transfers and food distribution as food security and pro-poor measures for vulnerable groups)
Output 6: Coordination of partnerships and mobilization of resources for collective response are improved

column2: Partnerships for food security and livelihoods - Africa Regional
column3: PELUM - Participatory Ecological Land Use Management - local office
column5: PELUM - Participatory Ecological Land Use Management - local office
column6:
The project aims to increase food and nutrition security for small-scale food producers and their communities in Malawi, Uganda and Niger.  The long-term impact is to strengthen climate-resilient local food systems by putting small-scale producers at the center and allowing for the widespread use and consumption of locally adapted crops and varieties (including neglected and underutilized food plants), and promoting self-sufficiency.

Outcomes are:
1) Local biodiversity management
2) Local value chains of agrobiodiverse products
3) Innovative Farmer-Researcher partnerships
4) Collaborative environment for policy change

Main activites include:
1) Research agendas on PPB/crop diversity and local food plants/nutrition; increased capacities for PPB, utilization of LFPs, and agroecological crop management; improved seed storage; strong dissemination linkages to create insterest in/market for PPB and nutrition work, and to stimulate demand for marketing.
2) Production and dissemination of high-quality seed of local adapted varieties; increased capacities for food production and value creation/addition; improved local value chains of agrobiodiverse products; strengthened market linkages among value chain actors; increased market access for farmers organizations.
3) New ways of famer-researcher collaboration; increased capacitites for farmer-managed seed and food systems research; successful co-created innovations.
4) Increased influence through evidence-based advocacy; policy reforms proposed; increased capacities for policy influencing. 

Resources will be allocated toward mobilizing, supporting and engaging women’s leadership roles in food production, processing and marketing to empower women as key actors in food production and address the economic and legislative barriers they face. Power dynamics and paradigms will be targeted, including active work on policy change related to women’s access to land.

column2: Building Resilient Value Chains and Food Security in Northern Ghana
column3: WARC Group LLC - The West African Rice Company
column5: WARC Group LLC - The West African Rice Company
column6:
Impact: Food Security strengthened in rural Northern Ghana.

Outcome 1: Agricultural sector strengthened through market linkages; Outcome 2: Enhanced access by smallholder farmers to market, knowledge and employment through hubs; Outcome 3 Increased adoption by smallholder farmers of regenerative agricultural practices.

Warc is planning to establish rural infrastructure over three years, including container-based trading hubs, 100MT silos, storage facilities and cold rooms to enhance operational efficiency and inventory management. Additionally, Warc plans to invest in trucks for efficient transport of crops between hubs and systems to distribute produce to downstream buyers. This network will engage a total of 21,000 farmers (50% women and youth) with improved inputs, training, and market access. 

Warc will purchase 54,000 MT in total of maize over three years (Y1 – 9,600 MT, Y2 20,400 MT and Y3 24,000 MT), injecting €21 million into the local economy and creating 147 direct full-time jobs, with a strong focus on gender inclusion. Warc aims to supply Koudijs, a subsidiary of the Dutch animal feed company De Heus, their key partner with 30,000 MT of maize over the next three years. This collaboration contributes to sustainable agriculture, rural development and long-term food security in Ghana.

column2: Integrating Aquaculture-Agriculture to Combat Food Insecurity
column3: CDF Canada - Co-operative Development Foundation of Canada
column5: CDF Canada - Co-operative Development Foundation of Canada
column6:
This project is part of the Agriculture for Development portifolio (Farmer and Cooperative Organizations as Knowledge Partners)

The aim of the project is to increase the productivity and income of, and access to markets by, small-scale food producers, especially women, engaged in integrated aquaculture-agriculture sytems comprising of fish, crops, livestock and agroforestry sub-systems to combat food insecurity

The project outcomes are:
1) Increased adoption of diversified climate-resilient technologies such as IAAS
2) Increased knowledge among farmers on managing climate risks
3) Increased organization of smallholder farmers with strong input and output market linkages
4) Improved forest cover in fishery communities

The main project activities are:
1) Promote integrated fish, livestock and bio-fortified crops; integrated pond-based polyculture of tilapia and other indigenous fish species with livestock (chickens and goats); climate-smart post-harvest fish processing; and growing of orange sweet potato and nutrient-dense food. 
2) Promote reforestation and planting of native bamboo species in riparian zones and wetlands; enhanced ecosystem services benefiting from the relationship between planting trees, water table protection; fish farming, soiil fertility, etc.
3) Increase the participation of small-scale producers in off-farm value chain activities: strengthening and developing cooperatives/farmer organizations, SMEs, particularly women-led.
4) Increase access to climate-smart farming inputs (resilient fish seeds; strengthened fish hatchery operations; fish feeds, etc.) and markets (fresh and processed) by smallholder farmers, especially women.
5) Increase equitable provision of inclusive agricultural extension and advisory services (aquaculture, crops, livestock and forestry): strengthened capacity of informal, publi, and private stakeholders in climate-smart integrated farming systems and their value chains to scale up innovative practices.

The Programme titled “Strengthening the roles of science granting councils in Africa’s science systems“ is part of the Science Granting Councils Initiative phase 2 (SGCI-2) funded by IDRC, Norad, FCDO, Sida, South Africa’s National Research Foundation (NRF) and the German Research Foundation (DFG). This initiative seeks to strengthen systems, capacities, and research funding of 17 science granting councils in sub-Saharan Africa. The SGCI participating countries are Botswana, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Namibia, Nigeria, Mozambique, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

The expected Impact is strong national science systems that contribute to economic and social development in sub-Saharan Africa. The expected Outcome is more effective investments by the Councils in research, development and innovation. To meet these goals, the Programme has four interrelated objectives:

i)	Support research projects with potential for commercialization and upscaling and carried out in partnership with the private sector/ industry and social sector including community-based organizations and groups. Support fundamental research projects that can contribute to global stock of knowledge and build new research fields; 
ii)	Strengthen the Councils’ research management systems and practices; 
iii)	Promote gender equality and inclusivity; and 
iv)	Support knowledge sharing, interactive learning and networking among researchers, Councils and other actors

The direct target group is science granting councils and the intended end target groups are research actors, private sector actors and social sector actors.

column2: FAO Seed Security Phase II (2007-2011) Oromia
column3: FAO - Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations
column5: FAO - Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations
column6: Phase II of the "FAO Harerge Seed Security" Project (see ETH-00/319 for phase I). The project is situated in the Oromia Region, an area experiencing massive land degradation and periodic shortfalls in rainfall. Prior to the establishment of this project there was little or no sustained research aimed at developing drought resistant varieties of the main food crops, which could benefit smallholder farming communities. These farmers traditionally depend on the seeds that can be retained from their previous harvest. However, droughts have made this seed saving practise an unreliable source of planting from season to season. The project adresses this problem through applied research and direct implementation within local communities on the establishment of seed banks for increased seed security, the introduction of more resilient seeds, crop diversification and marketing strategies for the beneficiaries aimed at improving their livliehoods.

column2: MIREME-NVE Institutional Cooperation Phase II
column6:
The second phase of the institutional cooperation program between the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), the Ministry for Mineral Resources and Energy (MIREME) and the Energy Regulatory Authority (ARENE). Experts from NVE, including both back-office support seconded, resident advisers will work alongside partners in MIREME and ARENE to support their needs. The program aims to achieve a comprehensive management of the energy sector as a tool for long term economic development, with the ultimate target to support socio-economic development through increased access to sustainable electricity supply on- and off-grid. 

The targets are to be achieved through targeted efforts in the areas of development and implementation of the legal framework and capacity building in the administration, both in the ministry MIREME and the regulator ARENE. There are four components in the program, focusing on legal framework, governance of the power sector, strategy development in the regulator and skills anhancement in the regulator. The short-term outcomes include application of a complete revised legal framework for the energy sector in Mozambique; application of a new energy sector strategy and efficienty coordination of on- and off-grid electrification efforts in the ministry MIREME; and optimal operation and efficient casehandling in the regualtor ARENE. 

This is a continuation of a cooperation which started in 2017. the main achievements in the first phase, which was concluded in 2022, was the contributions to the new electricity law in Mozambique, adopted in 2022.

column2: Strengthening Education Systems, Bridging Learning Loss (SESBiLL) due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
column6:
The project aims to address learning loss experienced during the prolonged closure of schools due to the Covid-19, including refugees and host communities. The disruption in learning has inevitably had a negative impact on the efforts to improve learning outcomes and overall quality of education. It has compounded the pre-existing education disparities and reduced opportunities for learning continuation for the vulnerable groups in poor, rural communities.

The project outcomes include improved knowledge and competencies of primary students & excellerated  learners, provision of teacher training and protection of children and improved education management and coordination in project schools. School feeding and empowering school management committees as well as child protection to reduce violence against children and actions to reduce risks of modern slavery of children are also part of the project.

column2: Scaling-up improved food security, nutrition, and sustainable livelihoods in Borno, Adamawa, Yobe and Taraba States
column3: FAO - Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations
column5: FAO - Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations
column6:
This programme is strengthening resilience of crises affected population in the four states of Borno, Adamawa, Yobe and Taraba to alleviate hunger and poverty in the region. 
The project impact is to enhance food and nutrition security on a sustainable basis. 

This 3-year intervention will directly benefit about 307,930 persons (37,400 households) with at least 45 percent of women as direct beneficiaries who will receive agriculture starter kits (inputs/tools/animals), knowledge and skills and to enhance their resilience. The beneficiaries will be IDPs, host communities and returnees/relocated households with special attention to women headed households.

The four main priorities are: 

Priority 1: Promote Climate Resilient Diversified Agriculture for Sustainable Household Food and Nutrition Security 
Priority 2: Enhance agricultural value chains and stimulate local markets
Priority 3: Enhance sustainable natural resource management and utilization 
Priority 4: Strengthening data analysis for advocacy and evidence-based decision making

column2: IMLU - Support to prevention of torture
column6:
The overall objective of the project is to reduce the prevalence of torture in Kenya through a rehabilitative and preventive approach that focuses on documentation, litigation and capacity enhancement of key stakeholders. Target groups are: 1) Victims and survivors of torture in Kenya, 2) Victims and survivors of torture in the marginalized areas of Northern Kenya, 3) Legal, health and media practitioners, and 4) IMLU: Organisation and staff.

Specific objectives are:
-	To conduct documentation and rehabilitation of 50 torture survivors and 10 deaths related to torture, in custody or other suspicious deaths
-	To provide legal assistance for 10 of the torture survivors
-	To document cases of torture and related human rights violations in the marginalized Northern frontiers of Kenya
-	To conduct advocacy and awareness campaign on the nature and prevalence of torture in Kenya at national, regional and international levels
-	To enhance capacity of 60 legal and media practitioners in dealing with torture
-	To enhance the capacity of the organization and its staff to respond to security matters and new challenges as human rights defenders

column2: ZI Zimbabwe Institute
column6:
The project’s main activities and main objectives (impact, outcomes, outputs) and target group

The Overall Goal of the action is: To contribute to the promotion and attainment of an inclusive democratic, peaceful and developmental Zimbabwe through Zimbabwean-driven national dialogue processes aimed at political and electoral reforms that reduce disputes over electoral outcomes.

Priority Area 1: Partnership Building (focusing on Conflict Prevention)

Objective 1: To support inclusive intra and interparty engagements on dialogue with a specific focus on conflict prevention and creating a peaceful electoral environment towards 2023 elections. 

Outcome 1: Entrenched culture of inclusive political dialogue that helps to reduce political conflicts and electoral disputes in the conduct of the 2023 elections. 

Priority Area 2: Institutional Building (focusing on Protecting the Vote)

Objective 2: To facilitate political party strengthening in EPAs database development for inclusive and efficient EPAs recruitment and training by July 2023

Outcome 2: Enhanced capacity of political parties to protect the vote in 2023 elections.

Priority Area 3: Equality and Inclusion

Objective 3: To promote increased political participation of women and youth political party leadership processes and the 2023 elections.
Outcome 3: Gender inclusive political parties with opportunities for political participation of women and youth

Main Target group: 
Political parties are the main targeted beneficiaries, and they will benefit from the project’s institutional strengthening activities and dialogue activities which will help to create conditions for peaceful electoral contests and management of political transitions.

column2: Strengthen Ethiopia's Adaptive Safety Net Programme (PSNP 5)
column5: Ethiopia Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
column6:
The support goes to the government initiated Productive Safety Net Programme phase 5 (PSNP5) being implemented in collaboration between the World Bank and more than 10 development partners. The objective of the programme is to enhance service delivery of Ethiopia’s adaptive rural safety net to improve the well-being of extremely poor and vulnerable households in drought prone communities.

This phase of support will build on experiences and lessons learned from early phases of implementation and will seek to make key enhancements to the program under three components:

• Comp. 1 focuses on the delivery of safety net operations for core program beneficiaries. It includes: the delivery of core transfers to public work (PW) and PDS beneficiaries; the implementation of the PW subprojects by which most beneficiaries earn their safety net benefits; services for children between 1 and 5 years old, and mothers; and complementary livelihood services to enable PSNP beneficiaries to enhance and diversify their incomes.

• Comp. 2 will (a) support the Government to expand the geographic coverage of PSNP in additional drought-prone woredas and (b) enhance PSNP capacity to function as an integrated shock responsive social safety net, building on the GoE’s recent decision to consolidate the operations management of humanitarian food assistance and PSNP under the FSCD in the MoA.

• Comp. 3 relates to the modernization of systems, capacity development, and overall management of the PSNP. It includes activities focused on strengthening service delivery and the Government institutions’ ability to manage all aspects of program implementation.

Building on the successes of previous phases of support PSNP5 actively seeks to address the gender gaps in Ethiopia on female labor market participation, access to transactional accounts, agriculture productivity, and entrepreneurship.

column2: Protection and durable alternatives to modern slavery in DRC
column6:
The project aims to scale up ongoing, joint efforts in Mwenga, SouthKivu, by Caritas Norway and Caritas Congo to combat modern slavery, through a threepronged approach in cooperation with a local partner; Croisade Humanitaire. Targeting authorities, the corporate sector and especially vulnerable population groups, the proposed project will: 

(i) step up and reinforce the dialogue between civil society and, on the one hand, authorities at all levels (local, national and regional) and, on the other hand, private sector entities (locally and internationally), to reduce the scope and prevalence of destructive practices of modern slavery in the South Kivu province. 

(ii) Protect, empower and build resilience of younger children who are victims of- or at risk of being forcibly recruited into the worst forms of child labour, as well as especially vulnerable women and adult girls suffering other types of modern slavery in and around the mines. Sustainable alternatives will be offered to a total of 1200 vulnerable individuals and 600 households.

column2: REDD pilot project by Jane Goodall Institute
column6:
A REDD pilot activity in Western Tanzania. This project builds on JGI’s 15 years of successful fieldwork in western Tanzania and focuses in the Masito Ugalla ecosystem (MUE), an expansive forested landscape of approximately 10,827 km2 under varied management and ownership regimes with an average annual deforestation rate of 1.7%.  The project will work with 15 villages in MUE area, including seven villages along the shore of Lake Tanganyika in Kigoma district to protect about 700 km2 (70,000 ha) of native forests currently classified as “General Lands” . 
Goal: To enable communities and high bio-diversity value forests in western Tanzania benefit from REDD based global approaches to climate change mitigation. 
Purpose: To build awareness and enhance capacity and governance mechanisms for local communities and government institutions to administer and benefit from REDD-related obligations and opportunities in the Masito Ugalla ecosystem in support of national REDD readiness

column2: UNICEF Catalytic funding to support the Education Services Joint Fund
column6: Catalytic funding to support the Education Services Joint Fund (ESJF). The ESJF is a critical aspect of the Ministry of Education, UNICEF and RNE partnership which directly contributes to the National Education Sector Investment Plan (NESIP) priority on improving governance and management. Through the Fiduciary Agent, UNICEF and RNE will contribute to MoE capacity building in financial management, procurement and programme implementation, key functions to deliver on the NESIP. The Fiduciary Agent and UNICEF complement each other in the provision of the necessary capacity required by the MoE, with the former focusing on finance and procurement and the latter on overall management and program implementation. The agreement further supports the Malawi government on inclusive education focusing on children with disabilities, improving opportunities for continuous professional development of teachers and evidence-based policy development.

column2: HALO Trust Mine Clearance in Somaliland 2011-2012
column6:
HALO Somaliland aims to clear and render safe 320,000m² of suspect mined areas to reduce the occurrence of death and injury due to mines and Explosive Remnants of War and to reduce poverty and hunger by improving the local communities’ access to land, water and roads.

•	Goal 1: Casualty Reduction - to reduce the occurrence of death and injury to humans and livestock, due to mines and Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) 
•	Goal 2: Restore and improve access - to play a crucial part in reducing poverty and hunger by removing the threat of mines and ERW thereby improving the local communities’ access to land, water and roads. 
•	Goal 3: Effective & efficient clearance - to continue the increase in clearance productivity rates and promote the successful deployment of metal detectors to speed up humanitarian mine clearance in Somaliland. 
•	Goal 4: National capacity building – to continue training national staff including female deminers and encourage the development of skills useful for future employment. 
•	Goal 5: Assist the Government to comply with Geneva Call – to continue with mine clearance and provide assistance to the Government to comply with the Geneva Call deed of commit

column2: PACT Sudan 2010- Sudan Three Areas Peace Fund
column6:
The purpose of the PACTproject “Three Areas Peace Fund” is to improve the local, regional and national capacities to mitigate conflict in Sudan’s Abyei, Blue Nile and Southern Kordofan states – collectively referred to as the Three Areas – by serving as the Managing Agent of a fund that undertakes four types of activities. 

The expected outcome of the project is to increase awareness of key factors that support the implementation of the CPA in the Three Areas, increased capacity of local organization to contribute to enhanced stability, local reconciliation and peace building in the Three Areas, and increase sharing of information, best practices and lessons learned regarding peace-building in the Three Areas between agencies and communities.  More detailed specification of the activities is outlined in the proposal and the “2011 Additional Activities Implementation Plan”.

column2: Civil Society Peace Building in Northern Uganda
column6:
The project "Civil Society Peace Building in Northern Uganda: Supporting and enabling women participation in local communities across LRA-affected areas to increase their advocacy for conciliation peace building". is an Addendum II to previous support to Consiliation Resources. 

The overall goal of CR's work in the LRA-affected areas of Uganda, Sudan, DRC and the Central African Republic is to contribute to a non-violent end to the conflict between the governments involved and the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA) through a process which makes it possible for the rebels to leave the LRA and return to their home – areas. 

This specific support aims at promoting Women’s Participation in peace building initiatives. Because of the unequal way the LRA conflict has affected women, a separate, safe spaces for women to voice their opinions and raise issues that are of concern to them will be created. CR will work with grassroots women and women organizations in the LRA affected areas- to convene meetings and workshops on the issues of cross-border peace building in the LRA affected areas. Women and Women’s organizations will participate in these meetings to define their role in the peace

column2: Women lead and benefit from inclusive peace and security in Uganda
column6:
Women lead and benefit from inclusive peace and security in Uganda - WPS Phase II
Implementation of Uganda's National Action Plan (NAP) for UNSCR 1325, in close partnership with UN Women. 
The proposed project aims to focus on the priority outcomes and medium-term outcomes of Uganda's NAP III for the next four years, building on the results of the first phase of the project.
By 2026, the WPS Project Phase II will achieve the following desired Outcomes: 
Outcome 1: By 2026, Women participation in enhancing social cohesion and reducing interethnic conflicts increased 
Outcome 2: Increased participation of women in reduction of violent extremism
Outcome 3: By 2026, Women, including young women participate in preventing and mitigating natural and human made disasters 
Outcome 4: Systems and structures for the implementation and coordination of the NAP III strengthened

column2: Aceli Africa -  increased lending to agricultural SMEs
column6:
Aceli Africa provides financial incentives (first loss portfolio coverage) to banks to enable them to increase lending to agricultural small and medium sized enterprises. Aceli Africa works in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, and Zambia.

The intended impact and main goal of this project is to create a “more competitive financial market serving agricultural SMEs that improve livelihoods for smallholder farmers and enterprise employees, particularly women, in Sub-Saharan Africa”.

Key outcomes are:
•	Outcome 1: Improved ability by the financial institutions supported by Aceli Africa to serve agri-SMEs, particularly those owned by women, that promote food security and build climate resilience
•	Outcome 2: Improved access to finance for agri-SMEs that create economic opportunities for small-scale farmers and workers, especially women.
•	Outcome 3: Expanded supply of nutritious food, including the sustainable production of aquaculture, for African consumers and increased climate resilience by agri-SMEs meeting Aceli's impact bonuses.
•	Outcome 4: Increased evidence demonstrating financial incentives as a pathway to a thriving financial market serving agri-SMEs.

column6:

covertly foisted on Africa by neocolonial or decadent Western forces.The project seeks to address information manipulation and its impact on human rights defenders championing gender and sexual identity rights as well as climate activists working towards a green transition by mapping and the mis/disinformation ecosystems in target countries as well as enhancing the capacity of media practitioners, researchers and activists to respond to, report on and pursue punitive measures for mis/information in country contexts as well as transnationally. The geographical focus of the project will be determined during the inception phase but will target South Africa and potentially Zimbabwe, Namibia, Madagascar, Botswana and Lesotho.

column2: REDD+ Investment Program Phase II
column3: Ethiopia Ministry of Finance and Economic Development
column5: Ethiopia Ministry of Environment and Forest
column6:
The agreement is between Government of Ethiopia and the Royal Norwegian government. The current agreement is the continuation of the REDD+ investment phase I of the result based payment for Ethiopia to achieve  result based payment. Main objectives are to contribute to climate mitigation, climate adaptation and biodiversity conservation. Ethiopia has moved from REDD+ phase I to phase II of the bilateral Forest and Climate Partnership Agreement. Through RIP II Ethiopia is making investments on the ground with main target audience being local forest dwellers and communities, to eventually achieve phase III of the Partnership: verified carbon emission reductions from forest. Conserving and restoring forest in Ethiopia is contributing to increased resilience against the adverse effects of climate change, rural livelihoods and poverty reduction, maintained/increased water resources and to biodiversity. 

RIP phase II has an overarching goal to contribute to enhanced forest conservation by avoided deforestation and forest degradation, and to increased forest cover through tree planting and restoration of degraded forest areas. Particularly through the target related to increased forest cover, the program will also target national climate adaptation goals. The program also focuses beyond climate-related objectives, such as on provision of livelihoods, and social and environmental benefits for women, girls, youth, and other forest-dependent people, with the aim of protecting their rights, including equity and fair distribution of benefits. RIP II is contributing to forest conservation, landscape restoration and private sector engagement. It will also contribute to various SDGs such as climate actions and improved life on land.

column2: Festival of the Desert 2011
column6:
The Festival in the Desert started out as a local music festival of nomads in Essakane in northern Mali near Timbuktu. It has now become one of the largest cultural events in Mali and one of the most exotic world music festivals in the world. Norway supported the festival which took place in January 2010 (ref. “Festival au Desert, Rapport Technique et Financièr 2010”).  The Association du Festival au Desert (EFES) plans to develop a three-year plan to professionalize the festival and develop the festival into an environment friendly event inspired by the Hove Festival’s cooperation with UNEP in Norway.  

The activities, called “Operation Clean Desert” will counteract one of the most negative impacts of tourist attractions of this kind: the accumulation of garbage. In addition to the consequences for the esthetics of the desert, garbage also has a negative impact on the fragile ecosystem and biodiversity of the desert where everything, including biodegradables, takes much more time to decompose.  Focus will be on collecting and incinerating the garbage as well as organizing a campaign on the negative consequences of tourism.

column2: Sub-regional meeting on world heritage
column6:
Norwegian support to East Africa sub-regional meeting on World Heritage within the framework of the second cycle of the periodic reporting for Africa. 
The overall goal of the project is to strengthen capacity on world heritage management in the African countries, to increase the sharing of knowledge across the African continent, and reduce the dependency on international expertise. 
The purpose is to host an East African sub-regional meeting on world heritage within the framework of the second cycle of the periodic reporting for Africa to UNESCO in Nairobi on May 4-6, 2010. 
The output is to be a draft report, presented on the 34th session for the World Heritage Committee in July 2010. The final report together with a follow-up action plan and a training strategy from the analysis of the periodic reports shall be presented to the 35th session of the World Heritage Committee in 2011. Other expected outcomes: 
-	Sharing of issues and challenges
-	Reinforced on-site conservation mechanisms
-	Sound understanding of the significance of the World Heritage Periodic Reporting and its effective use as self-monitoring and peer-reviewing tool for World Heritage Sites by the concerned States Parties.”

column2: Powergen renewable Energy East Africa Ltd. - feasibility study South Sudan
column6: South Sudan has one of the lowest electrification rates in the world, with only 1% of its 12.5 million people able to access to grid electricity, leaving many others to without power or reliant solely upon expensive, dirty diesel generators for limited supply. PowerGen is developing a partnership with a local solar developer, SunGate Solar, to develop a pipeline of at least 15 mini-grids in South Sudan. In the partnership between PowerGen and SunGate Solar, SunGate will bring their local expertise and ability to implement on the ground, while PowerGen will bring the “know-how” for mini-grid development, design, and operations. These mini-grid projects will connect approximately 10,000 connections to electricity, providing access to reliable 24-hour AC power access to approximately 30,000 people i.e. 25,000 residential people and 5,000 businesses. The project will focus on deploying mini-grids in the vibrant market areas of towns, which present an exciting opportunity to power productive uses of energy that will spur further economic activity. Further, these market-focused mini-grids could be good project investments, with robust unit economics due to high consumption and willingness-to-pay among the businesses powered.

column2: GW Promoting domestic resource mobilisation for a just energy transition Madagascar
column6:
The economic transition from fossil fuels to renewables must not place undue burden on, or unjustly affect, those least responsiblefor the climate crisis. While we must scale up clean energy such as solar and wind power to avoid climate-breakdown, Global South countries where large deposits of lithium, cobalt, and copper are located, must also benefit from this process. To address the problem, Global Witness (GW) will work in partnership with civil society network, Publish What You Pay (PWYP), to convene, strategize, and campaign to expose unfair models of extraction that inhibit DRM, investigate harmful and illicit practices, and address barriers to countries benefiting from the renewable energy transition, while supporting strong governance and a robust civil society enabling environment in those target jurisdictions. 
The project’s objectives are to strengthen Global South civil society and its Northern networks to advance global equity by achieving responsible, transparent management of critical minerals resource wealth to optimise DRM, in the context of the energy transition. Target groups include communities affected by: human and environmental harms from irresponsible extractive industries; the suppression of DRM due to poor governance and illicit financial flows; and climate change impacts.
A South-South CSO alliance will be developed to engage on these issues in collaboration with PWYP and their national chapters
working with communities on critical mineral and energy transition issues in Madagascar.
A complementary South-North CSO/NGO alliance will be built, supporting the participation of Global South CSOs in leadingadvocacy within international fora and networks.
GW and partner investigations will ground South-North advocacy at the national and international levels. They will expose how exploitative and abusive economic models prevent Global South countries from equitably benefitting from the transition to a green economy

column2: CapaCare Capacity Building in Surgical Care 2024-2028
column6: CapaCare is training medical professionals in the areas where there is a shortage of such personnel. The aim of the surgical training programme is to increase the level of surgical skilled health staff at district hospitals in Sierra Leone. The goal of this programme is to train, each for 2 years, Medical Doctors (MD) and /or nurses and community Health Officers (CHOs) for the country's district hospitals, to be able to handle the most common surgical and obstetrical emergencies that without treatment would lead to disability or death. CapaCare has a focus on increasing the quality of surgical and obstetric provision by offering courses in quality improvement and research methodology to MD candidates. As part of the courses, the students have a mandatory six-month assignment of undertaking a quality improvement assessment. Bi-annual studies of surgical site infection and postoperative mortality are also planned to be part of the mandatory assignments. There is moreover a focus on disseminating the results from the projects through presentations and peer-reviewed publications.

column6:
ASAP+ is a Trust Fund set up to design programmes that support IFADs Programme on Loans and Grants (Polg). ASAP+ will support climate adaptation for small scale food producers in Low and Middle income countries. It will also contribute to climate mitigation in cases where a win-win outcome can be achieved. ASAP+ is a multi donor fund with the ambition to raise USD 500 million. The goal are to achieve climate adaptation among 10 million small scale food producers. Partcipation of women, youth and indigenous people will be prioritized.The impact goal for ASAP+ is that small-scale producers and landless poor rural households are more resilient to climate change and embark on low emissions development pathways
The intendet outcomes are
1.	Increased resilience of vulnerable households to the impacts of climate change on their food security and nutrition, focusing particularly on rural women, youth, indigenous peoples 
2.	Reduced emissions from win-win interventions with significant development benefits, particularly for food insecure and marginalized groups
The Norwegian contribution is earmerked for countries in Sub-Sahara Africa.

Tanzania, Uganda. Their idea is related to climate change and the need of creating sustainable livelihoods/more income generating sources that do not have a negative impact on the environment (TEG is in the Morogoro region close to the Uluguru mountain area in Tanzania, and ACOYDE in the Mbarara district South-West in Uganda). Economic skilling for women and youth which is in line with environmental conservation is the main objective of the project. TEG wants specifically to learn how to use banana fibres and banana stems (surplus from banana production- a huge income source in Tanzania) to make quality and income generating handicrafts, which ACOYDE have a lot of experience through their social enterprise CHACHA Banana Fiber Project. The teaching program ACOYDE provide for youth and women through the enterprise are constantly helping a huge amount of youth and women in Uganda with 
income from handicrafts. Participants will exchange crafting skills and teaching skills, as well as help developing organisational capacity. In general, they wish to increase knowledge and abilities related to ecological income generating sources. ACOYDE would like to learn more about running ecotourism project as a source of income, which TEG has a lot of experience from. They will also learn about forest conservation, and the use of storytelling to teach communities on climate change and how to engage in eco-tourism as a way of creating income as well as protecting nature.

column6: Conflict in northern Mozambique atributed to extremism has exposed untold suffering, political violence, displaced millions, destroyed public and private property and mobilised the international community to assist. Access to accurate and timely information is paramount. The need for reliable data on violence patterns, drivers, and actors is critical to facilitating informed dialogue and negotiatios at all levels, fostering conflict-sensitive and effective program design and accountability. The primary goal of the Project is to ensure that its data and analysis reach decision-makers in position to enact tangible policy changes by enhancing the capacity of local data partners, increasing awareness and understanding among policy makers and practitioners. The expected outcomes and impact are six-fold; (i) enhanced global understanding, (ii) increased media coverage, (iii) adaptive programming, (iv) support for peace initiatives, (v) operational effectiveness, and (vi) proactive planning and response.

column2: Building back better post Covid-19. Enhancing skill development and job creation fot the youth in Angola
column6:
The COVID-19 pandemic consitutes an unprecedented crisis with adverse sicioeconomic impacts in Angola. The negative shock on jobs and education has exacerbated multidimensional poverty and inequalities within the context of prolonged economic recession. RIsing unembplyment, informal work and school closure have hit the young Angolan population - eight out of ten Angolans will be under 35 yesars by 2021. This has led to tensions in densely-populated urban and peri-urban areas, which as resulted in social unrests.
The project aims at enhancing skills development to foster job opportunities for Angolan youth through the promotion of quality technical and vocational training (TVET), youth employment and entrepreneurship, and youth  engagement. Gender ratio in the project is 60% girls and 40 % boys.

column2: Lake Chilwa Basin Climate Change Programme
column3: Malawi Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Affairs
column6:
In order to maintain the important food security, economic and social benefits of agricultural and natural resources in the face of known climate variability, planned adaptation and cross-sectoral collaboration at local, basin and national scales is required. This project seeks to understand the impacts of climate change adaptations on livelihood resilience in Lake Chilwa Basin. 

Programme goal: secure sustainable management of natural resources to promote and secure a basis of livelihoods for 1,5 million people and build capacity of rural communities to manage the impacts of climate change.                              - basin wide climate adaptation in support of the NAPA developed and is enhancing the capacity of communities to adopt sustainable livelihood and natural resource management practices.

specific purposes- strengthening local and district institutions to better manage and govern natural resources and build resilience to climate change.
- improving household and enterprise adaptive capacity in Basin hotspots.
- facilitating and help build cross-basin and cross-sector sustainable natural resource management and planning for climate change throughout the Basin.

column2: WFP Scaling up Anticipatory Action phase II
column6: The World Food Programme (WFP) has been implementing the “Multi-Country Programme (MCP) for Scaling-up drought anticipatory actions for food security in Africa” (MCP-AA4FS) in Madagascar, Mozambique, Niger and Zimbabwe with support from the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (NORAD) since 2020. The proposed interventions build on the achievements of the MCP-AA4FS phase I implemented in Madagascar, Mozambique, Niger and Zimbabwe, by further strengthening existing capacities at national and local levels to deliver anticipatory actions (AAs) ahead of climate shocks and expanding the programme to Burkina Faso, Malawi and Tanzania. While the previous phase was focused on drought only, this next phase will also include other hazards such as floods and cyclones. As part of the programme, WFP commits to continuing to generate rigorous evidence on AA for multiple hazards and contexts, which will contribute to stronger programme design, institutionalization and scale up of this innovative approach. WFP will carry out gender role analyzes in all country contexts with the aim that the intervention should meet the needs of women, men, girls and boys to an equal extent, and contribute to increased equality.

column2: Feasibility study - Increasd cocoa production in the Ivory Coast
column6: The Norwegian chocolate producers are dependent on the import of cocoa from the Ivory Coast.  To secure their future they need secure deliveries and deliveries of a good quality.  The industry in Norway employs 1 300 workers.  The production of cocoa in the Ivory Coast is ineffective and non sustainable.  The workers are poor and uneducated and the children are taken out of school at an early age to assist their parents.  The project is to improve the working conditions of the workers through education.  Education related to cocoa production makes a better quality of the product produced.  And the workers will learn more about environemental protection, marketing and market access.  The applicant wants to join forces with producers/sellers in other Nordic countries to improve the living conditions of the workers and avoid child labour.  They want to undertake a study related to the present conditions and will implement the feasibilty study together with UNDP, ICI and WCF.

column2: Interpol EVEXI - forensic capacity building, East Africa
column6:
Project EVEXI seeks to deliver the following tasks in the context of a multinational approach to the investigation of the organized crime aspect of maritime piracy:
1. To generate intelligence deriving from interviews of released hostages and Somali prisoners detained in relation to piracy attacks and exploit physical evidence collected during the detention and arrests of pirates.
2. To gather intelligence through targeted interviews, to obtain intelligence that can be used to initiate or support existing international investigations on maritime piracy.
3. To utilize the Analytical Work File (AWF) of EUROPOL to create links of information regarding the financing of Somali pirates by citizens of European countries.
4. To assist and support the Participating Countries in analyzing the information gathered in the interviews and exploitation of physical evidence and forward all raw data and analytical outputs into the Analytical Work File (AWF) on Piracy at EUROPOL for global analysis, aiming to learn more about the Pirates networks and identify the high-value targets (HVTs) of Piracy and their assets.

Norway and France will share the project costs on a 50-50 basis.

Project EVEXI seeks to deliver the following tasks in the context of a multinational approach to the investigation of the organized crime aspect of maritime piracy:
1. To generate intelligence deriving from interviews of released hostages and Somali prisoners detained in relation to piracy attacks and exploit physical evidence collected during the detention and arrests of pirates.
2. To gather intelligence through targeted interviews, to obtain intelligence that can be used to initiate or support existing international investigations on maritime piracy.
3. To utilize the Analytical Work File (AWF) of EUROPOL to create links of information regarding the financing of Somali pirates by citizens of European countries.
4. To assist and support the Participating Countries in analyzing the information gathered in the interviews and exploitation of physical evidence and forward all raw data and analytical outputs into the Analytical Work File (AWF) on Piracy at EUROPOL for global analysis, aiming to learn more about the Pirates networks and identify the high-value targets (HVTs) of Piracy and their assets.

Norway and France will share the project costs on a 50-50 basis.

column5: COSTECH - Tanzania Commission for Science and Technology
column6:
The overall goal of the climate research program is that contextually relevant knowledge on climate change adaptation and mitigation is in use by governmental and non-governmental stakeholder at various levels across Tanzanian society.  

Expected Outcomes:
Tanzanian climate change research is strengthened.  
The capacity of Tanzanian HLIs and R&D institutions to conduct climate change research is increased  
Collaboration between research teams and other actors (government and non-governmental institutions, private sector, training institu
The institutional capacity of COSTECH to undertake large competitive research calls is enhanced

Expected Outputs:
A broad range of Tanzanian interdisciplinary research Programmes on climate change are funded and completed (w/specific target of female project leaders)
The participation of PhD and master students in climate change research Programmes is increased (w/specific target of female students)
The participation of a broad specter of Tanzanian HLIs and R&Ds in climate research is increased
Collaboration between research teams and a broad specter of other actors ensured
The programme is implemented in line with the principles in the COSTECH grant manual

Thematic priorities of the calls: 
Climate-adapted food production. 
Nature-based solutions to climate change adaptation and mitigation. 
Alert systems and climate services, including addressing loss and damage.  
Health challenges exacerbated by climate change  
Institutions and governance. 
New technologies and innovative funding instruments. 
 
The program is designed to promote female participation in research (Project leaders, other researchers and students). Project indicators include disaggregated data with specific targets for women (40% female project leaders and students funded). The project also includes other mechanisms to promote female participation. For instance, through the assessment criteria guiding the review of research projects

Expected Outcomes:
Tanzanian climate change research is strengthened.  
The capacity of Tanzanian HLIs and R&D institutions to conduct climate change research is increased  
Collaboration between research teams and other actors (government and non-governmental institutions, private sector, training institu
The institutional capacity of COSTECH to undertake large competitive research calls is enhanced

Expected Outputs:
A broad range of Tanzanian interdisciplinary research Programmes on climate change are funded and completed (w/specific target of female project leaders)
The participation of PhD and master students in climate change research Programmes is increased (w/specific target of female students)
The participation of a broad specter of Tanzanian HLIs and R&Ds in climate research is increased
Collaboration between research teams and a broad specter of other actors ensured
The programme is implemented in line with the principles in the COSTECH grant manual

Thematic priorities of the calls: 
Climate-adapted food production. 
Nature-based solutions to climate change adaptation and mitigation. 
Alert systems and climate services, including addressing loss and damage.  
Health challenges exacerbated by climate change  
Institutions and governance. 
New technologies and innovative funding instruments. 
 
The program is designed to promote female participation in research (Project leaders, other researchers and students). Project indicators include disaggregated data with specific targets for women (40% female project leaders and students funded). The project also includes other mechanisms to promote female participation. For instance, through the assessment criteria guiding the review of research projects

Outcome 3) Capacity of national caucuses of the African Parliamentary Network on Illicit Financial Flows and Taxation (APNIFFT) reinforced. column2: WFP-FAO DRC Resilience Programme
column6:
This agreement is the third phase of a joint WFP-FAO Resilience project which adopts an holistic approach to contribute to lasting and sustainable food security in the Tanganyika Provicince in the DRC. The agreement is between the Norwegian Embassy in Kinshasa and WFP, whereas the latter has an MOU with FAO regarding the division of labour.

It aims to strengthen the resilience of fragile communities, with the following goals:
1. Reducing food insecurity and poverty and malnutrition help build resilience and promote social cohesion. The joint resilience-building programme supports smallholder farmers and vulnerable communities achieve food security and better nutrition to enable them respond to shocks and have better sanitation.
2. The provision of food assistance and capacity building to crisis affected populations enables communities to grow their own food and diversify their incomes. Through the support of the programme, affected populations are able to join hands to diversify their livelihoods through farmer organizations.
3. Empowering women contributes to breaking the vicious cycle of violence against them. The joint resilience approach gives women the necessary tools to manage better their family’s dietary requirements, resources and take active role in the management of farmer organizations.
4. The joint resilience programme provides an integrated support to vulnerable communities and contributes to social cohesion and peace. By combining resilience with WASH and nutrition support, communities derive multiple benefits, leading to consolidation of peace.
5. The joint resilience programme continue amidst Covid-19 as building the resilience of vulnerable populations to shocks is key for a sustainable response to the pandemic. The strong anchor the resilience programme has in targeted communities is leveraged to pass on messages on Covid-19 preventive measures, mitigate rumours and stigma against the survivors and affected populations.

column2: NORHED II Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks
column6:
AdEMNEA (Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks for East Africa) will design, develop, and deploy a flexible network of data gathering and monitoring stations for meteorological data as well as a wide variety of data including audio, image, and video data as well as field reports and telemetry data, integrating both existing sensing platforms and customised components for specific research areas. This is targeting the thematic sub-area Climate Change and Natural Resources.

These data points will be aggregated through resilient and energy-efficient ICT networks from the field to researchers conducting data analysis using machine learning, pattern recognition, and other artificial intelligence and analytical methods in order to support researchers in the application domain.
The targeted application domains will be weather monitoring, building on the results and infrastructure established in the NORHED WIMEA-ICT project, and using this data together with the additional sensing and measurement sources to support researchers initially in the entomology domain. Both weather monitoring and the direct analysis of the presence, prevalence, and behaviour of pollinators and pests will offer important insights into the effects of climate change on natural resources for both the natural environment and particularly agriculture.

AdEMNEA (Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks for East Africa) will design, develop, and deploy a flexible network of data gathering and monitoring stations for meteorological data as well as a wide variety of data including audio, image, and video data as well as field reports and telemetry data, integrating both existing sensing platforms and customised components for specific research areas. This is targeting the thematic sub-area Climate Change and Natural Resources.

These data points will be aggregated through resilient and energy-efficient ICT networks from the field to researchers conducting data analysis using machine learning, pattern recognition, and other artificial intelligence and analytical methods in order to support researchers in the application domain.
The targeted application domains will be weather monitoring, building on the results and infrastructure established in the NORHED WIMEA-ICT project, and using this data together with the additional sensing and measurement sources to support researchers initially in the entomology domain. Both weather monitoring and the direct analysis of the presence, prevalence, and behaviour of pollinators and pests will offer important insights into the effects of climate change on natural resources for both the natural environment and particularly agriculture.

column2: Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa - Zambia
column6:
Over 600 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa live today without access to electricity. The Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa (BGFA) aims to reduce this gap by stimulating and accelerating the emergency of new business models to incentivise the private sector to offer affordable and clean energy access at scale to people living in rural and peri-urban areas. The BGFA programme aims at actively promoting, incentivising and transferring best practices regarding gender equality in BGFA target countries. BGFA does this through requiring awardees (energy service providers) to offer equal opportunities for men and women

Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa forms part of the ‘Power Africa’ initiative launched by former President Barack Obama and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goal 7 as well as the Paris Agreement on Climate. column2: Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa - Zambia
column6:
Over 600 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa live today without access to electricity. The Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa (BGFA) aims to reduce this gap by stimulating and accelerating the emergency of new business models to incentivise the private sector to offer affordable and clean energy access at scale to people living in rural and peri-urban areas. The BGFA programme aims at actively promoting, incentivising and transferring best practices regarding gender equality in BGFA target countries. BGFA does this through requiring awardees (energy service providers) to offer equal opportunities for men and women

Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa forms part of the ‘Power Africa’ initiative launched by former President Barack Obama and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goal 7 as well as the Paris Agreement on Climate. The planned period of implementation is in total six years. The BGFA programme aims, with so far four funding rounds, to establish up to 1.45 million energy connections by 2028, benefiting more than 6.5 million people in Burkina Faso, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Liberia, Mozambique, Uganda and Zambia

column2: NORHED II Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks
column6:
AdEMNEA (Adaptive Environmental Monitoring Networks for East Africa) will design, develop, and deploy a flexible network of data gathering and monitoring stations for meteorological data as well as a wide variety of data including audio, image, and video data as well as field reports and telemetry data, integrating both existing sensing platforms and customised components for specific research areas. This is targeting the thematic sub-area Climate Change and Natural Resources.

These data points will be aggregated through resilient and energy-efficient ICT networks from the field to researchers conducting data analysis using machine learning, pattern recognition, and other artificial intelligence and analytical methods in order to support researchers in the application domain.
The targeted application domains will be weather monitoring, building on the results and infrastructure established in the NORHED WIMEA-ICT project, and using this data together with the additional sensing and measurement sources to support researchers initially in the entomology domain. Both weather monitoring and the direct analysis of the presence, prevalence, and behaviour of pollinators and pests will offer important insights into the effects of climate change on natural resources for both the natural environment and particularly agriculture.

Using Judo, strenghten sport governance and practices to deliver safe, inclusive and responsible sport and physical activities for all, special emphasis on persons living in refugee settlements, girls and women and youth with a disability. 

The overall NIF project’s primary objective is to enhance opportunities for marginalized persons to benefit from and participate in sports. For to achieve this, NIF focuses on 1) To build lasting partnerships and networks to gain sustainable organizations that deliver safe, equitable and inclusive sports activities, 2) To enhance management resources in the development of inclusive and equitable partner programs with resources, and 3) Strengthened capacity of sports organizations to implement safe, equitable and inclusive sport. Emphasis is on the inclusion of women and girls, children/youth, persons with disabilities, and refugees.

column2: African Environment Day 2010
column6:
The African Union has since 2002 been commemorating African Environment Day (AED). On 3-4 March 2010, Tanzania will be hosting this annual event. Around 300 participants, including Ministers of Environment from AU countries, UN, academia NGOs and the general public will be coming to Arusha to celebrate the event. Gov. of Tanzania is requesting a total amount of 240,000 USD to be able to implement the event as in accordance with the programme document. 

The theme of the event in 2010 is: Africa Resilience to Climate Change: Biodiversity Conservation and Enhancing Traditional Knowledge. 

The support will be channelled through an amendment to the contract with Institute of Resource Assessment at University of Dar es Salaam. IRA will manage and administer the funds and also assist in the preparations and implementation of the event. A MoU between IRA and Vice Presidents Office-Dep of Environment has been signed.

column2: Close the Gap: Sufficient, Competent and Motivated Nurses and Midwives - Malawi
column5: National Organisation of Nurses and Midwives of Malawi
column6: The Norwegian Nurses Organisation (NNO/NSF) aims to create democratic, accountable, inclusive and sustainable organisations for nurses and midwives in four countries in Africa. Cooperation with the National Organisations of Nurses and Midwives in Malawi (NONM) goes back to 2006, and will be phased out between 2024 and 2026. The aim in this last phase  is to build the sustainability of NONM as an effective watchdog and advocate for nurses and midwives, and solution provider for the government, contributing to a stronger and more resilient health system to deliver Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and good health for all in Malawi. The project includes a focus on nurses and midwives’ equal opportunity to leadership training and positions (gender equality) and the rights of nurses and midwives with disabilities. It also aims to train nurses and midwives in health-related climate adaptation, in the face of increased climate change and extreme weather related health emergencies. Finally, the project aims to train the nurses and midwives to provide the best possible assistance to patients with disabilities and with SRHR to female patients.

The project is a follow-on project to the Burundi Emergency Demobilization, Reinsertion and Reintegration Program (EDRRP).

The overall goal is to contribute to peace and stability in Burundi and improve the security in the Great Lakes region. The purpose is to support the efforts of the Government of Burundi to: (i) demobilize membrs of the FNL and the FNL-Dissidents (FNL-D); and (ii) provide socio-economic reintegration support to said beneficiaries, as well as to remaining caseload demobilized under the EDRRP, with a particular focus on the provision of such support to such female, child and disbled ex-combantants.

1) Demobilization of FNL and FNL-D forces
2) Reinsertion support of new demobilized ex FNL and ex FNL-D
3) Transitional socio-economic reintegraton support for all demobilized adults ex-combatants, as well as a small pending caseload from EDRRp
4) Support to vulnerable groups. Specialized support and/or additional protection to vulnerable groups.

column2: Integrated, Adaptive and Climate-smart Response to Food Insecurity
column6:
The project aims to ensure that vulnerable people in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, particularly small-scale producers, women and people living with disabilities, have access to local climate-resilient and nutritious food production, are supported to improve their resilience and livelihoods, as well as to prevent and mitigate the impacts of climate change. The consortium aims to scale-up existing interventions in each targeted project locations, using best practices and lessons learned to implement an integrated, adaptive programme that can respond to both the risks associated with food and nutrition crisis situations and structural vulnerabilities. The holistic project will employ a rights-based, community-driven approach that emphasizes inclusion of marginalized groups and support to women’s access to and control over resources, implemented across the following four strategic objectives:
SO1: Strengthening small-scale producers’ climate-resilient food production capacity
SO2: Improving financing opportunities for small-scale producers, women, youth and people living with disabilities
SO3: Improving adoption of recommended practices to prevent malnutrition and reduce malnutrition
SO4: Strengthening local governance systems to empower women and other marginalized smallholder farmers in food security programming

column2: ITI - Enhancing and Strengthening the Peace Making Process
column6:
Enhancing and strengthening the peace making process, the development agenda and the transition to democracy and national reconciliation in selected countries in Africa, through the exposure to the South African transitional experience.

Objective
To strengthen the various efforts and prospects in four main countries towards achieving processes for peace and stable development, based on a common understanding of the main challenges facing the specified country.  

Beneficiaries /target group 
This project aims through stronger national and regional consensual processes to strengthen the prospects for sustainable peace and stable development in 4 main countries, notably CAR, Lesotho, South Africa and Zimbabwe . 

ITI proposes to continue to support peace and stability processes in four African countries under 3 thematic areas notably national reconciliation and social cohesion; Democratic Reforms; and Economic Transformation. The countries of focus to be targeted under these themes are the Central Africa Republic (CAR), Lesotho, South Africa and Zimbabwe. During the course of the project, short term engagements with a few other African countries might be taken on board. This project will be a continuation from previous programme phases and is aimed at building up from these phases and further consolidating on the investments and achievements thus far accomplished. 

In line with the thematic approach, the theme of National Reconciliation and social cohesion will target CAR and Lesotho. This theme speaks to the strengthening of a national consensus towards achieving sustainable peace. This involves establishing and strengthening the various key stakeholders including elites and institutions to come to the table and agree to a common vision and roadmap for peace and work in complementarity towards achieving this roadmap.  Currently the levels of fragmentation are too high to sustain any momentum for meaningful peace and stability in the target countries.

column6:
Enhancing and strengthening the peace making process, the development agenda and the transition to democracy and national reconciliation in selected countries in Africa, through the exposure to the South African transitional experience.

Objective
To strengthen the various efforts and prospects in four main countries towards achieving processes for peace and stable development, based on a common understanding of the main challenges facing the specified country.  

Beneficiaries /target group 
This project aims through stronger national and regional consensual processes to strengthen the prospects for sustainable peace and stable development in 4 main countries, notably CAR, Lesotho, South Africa and Zimbabwe . 

ITI proposes to continue to support peace and stability processes in four African countries under 3 thematic areas notably national reconciliation and social cohesion; Democratic Reforms; and Economic Transformation. The countries of focus to be targeted under these themes are the Central Africa Republic (CAR), Lesotho, South Africa and Zimbabwe. During the course of the project, short term engagements with a few other African countries might be taken on board. This project will be a continuation from previous programme phases and is aimed at building up from these phases and further consolidating on the investments and achievements thus far accomplished. 

In line with the thematic approach, the theme of National Reconciliation and social cohesion will target CAR and Lesotho. This theme speaks to the strengthening of a national consensus towards achieving sustainable peace. This involves establishing and strengthening the various key stakeholders including elites and institutions to come to the table and agree to a common vision and roadmap for peace and work in complementarity towards achieving this roadmap.  Currently the levels of fragmentation are too high to sustain any momentum for meaningful peace and stability in the target countries.
