column2: Improve Foundational Learning Outcomes - Southern Regions
column6:
The project will improve foundational learning outcomes in response to the pressing learning crisis in Southern Ethiopia Regional State (SERS) and Southwest Ethiopia People's Region (SWEPR). The overall outcome of the proposed programme is to ensure that by 2027 the disadvantaged children in the primary school grades (1-6) in the targeted primary schools learns and achieves improved and meaningful learning outcomes. The project intend to support every child to learn by making effective instructional practice clear and doable. Key interventions will ensure that teachers deliver effective instruction in the classroom, contributing to learning with shared accountability among key education stakeholders to ensure every child learns. 

Five major strategies will be used:

1) Developing and rolling out a context-specific and evidence-based learning approach through the TaRL approach
2) Strengthening the capacity of primary school teachers to use participatory, learner-centered, inclusive and gender-responsive pedagogy through both the pre-service and in-service models.
3) Provision of dignity kits, teaching and learning materials, including assistive devices for children with disabilities
4) Provision of school grants as seed funding to support school improvement plans
5) Strengthening shared ownership and accountability for improved teaching and student learning outcomes at the school, community and Woreda levels
6) Strengthening evidence generation to enhance evidence-based decision-making to continually improve learning achievement.

Full title of project is: The Modelling Accountability and Effective Instruction Programme to Improve Foundational Learning Outcomes in the Southern Ethiopia Regional State and Southwest Ethiopia People's Region 2024 - 2027

column2: Empowering marginalized teen girls in Morocco. Girls Soar with the Norwegian Embassy (GSN)
column6:
In a 2019 survey, the Moroccan High Commission for Planning found that 57% of women across all age groups had been subjected to violence. Girls and young women ages 15-19 had a yet higher prevalence rate, with 71% having been subjected to violence. The project will have an overarching goal of fostering gender equity by empowering marginalized teen girls in Morocco. Target groups include: 1) teen girls - the majority are 13-18 and living in poverty in underserved areas with parents who have limited education; and 2) community members - living in an underserved community where project activities take place.

The Project’s expected effect(s) on society (Impact): 
Greater gender equity in 12 marginalized communities in Morocco as target girls stay in school and avoid child marriage. 

The expected effects for the target group of the Project (Outcome):
1.	Teen girls better equipped to advocate for their rights, including gender equality. 
2.	Teen girls better equipped to manage their physical wellbeing.
3.	Increased community awareness of issues essential to teen girl rights and wellness.

column2: Feasibility study for the launch of electric cookstoves business in Ghana
column6:
The agreement is under Norad's Enterprise for Development Scheme (EDFJ). 

Norad supports a feasibility study, an environmental and social impact assessment, and a market assessment to assess the viability and market feasibility of our electric cooking products in Ghana. The study will entail conducting extensive pilot sales and marketing pilot to determine cost of cooking fuels, mobile money usage, grid reliability in urban and peri-urban areas, product pricing and preferred customer payment plans and customer cooking behaviour and preferences among others. column3: ICAN - International Civil Society Action Network
column5: ICAN - International Civil Society Action Network
column6:
The Project’s expected effect(s) on society is to prevent and solve violent conflicts and building lasting peace. The project aims to ensure that peace and reconciliation processes facilitate participation by women-led CSOs and WPBs in all phases and that, with their support, the implementation of peace agreements safeguards the rights of both women and men (Impact).

3. Increase the number of children, especially girls, Almajiri, and children with disabilities and children exiting armed groups actively engaging in quality learning and skills development opportunities, including via alternative and remote modalities (Innovation, quality, and learning)

column6:
This UN coordinated emergency appeal calls for $316.4 million to respond to the immediate COVID-19 public health response and the most urgent needs generated by the secondary consequences caused by the COVID-19 outbreak for the most vulnerable Ugandans. The appeal prioritizes the most urgent interventions to be carried out in Uganda in the next six months (April to September 2020) in support of the Government-led response to COVID-19. Complementing the Government of Uganda and the Ministry of Health’s response, the appeal focuses on: 1) the immediate public health response to COVID-19, and 2) response to the secondary impacts of the pandemic on vulnerable Ugandans, including children, the elderly, women, people living with disabilities, people living with HIV, refugees, migrants, and those displaced by natural disasters. 

The appeal targets at risk communities across Uganda under five core themes: 1) Life-Saving Health Services, including the immediate COVID-19 public health response; 2) Food Security, Livelihoods and Nutrition; 3) Social Protection and Life-Saving Essential Services; 4) Refugees and Displacement; and 5) Immediate Economic Support & Digital Innovation.
Under each theme, the Appeal presents two sets of time-bound interventions, as follows: 1. The most urgently required immediate interventions for the public health emergency and impacts from COVID-19 in next eight weeks are prioritized and highlighted; 2. These are placed alongside priority interventions that will tackle long-term public health interventions aimed at containment of COVID-19 and address the impacts of the containment measures over the next six months.
The appeal targets 12.8 million people in need.

column2: ERB and support to women engineers
column6:
The Engineers Registration Board (ERB) is requesting support for the professional development of women engineers in Tanzania through their  three-year Structured Engineers Apprenticeship Programme (SEAP). In addition to support to the trainees, the proposal will also cover strengthening of professional associations and advocacy forums for female engineers, training of the mentors that participate in the programme and capacity building of ERB staff managing the SEAP. 

The main activity and major part of the budget is the provision of subsistence allowance to 200 female engineers that will allow them to participate fully in SEAP and receive their registration. The main outcome of the programme is 200 graduate female engineers trained and registered as professional engineers after completion of the 5 year programme.

column2: Increasing food security of vulnerable households
column6: The project aims at increasing food security and climate resilience of vulnerable households and promoting gender equity in Mali, Niger, Kenya and Somalia. The target group of the project is small-scale farmers, pastoralists and agro pastoralists and vulnerable groups, such as women-led households, Internally Displaced People (IDP) and people living with disabilities. A mix of interventions will lead to a) an improved availability of healthy and sustainably produced agricultural and livestock products at household level through interventions boosting climate resilient agricultural production, b) improve accessibility to food by strengthening climate resilient livelihoods and increasing incomes of vulnerable households through diversifying income opportunities, c) improve utilization of food by capacity building measures specifically aimed at children and lactating women, d) promote gender equity by strengthening participation of women in decision-making.

column2: Feasibility study and pilot for digital currency and banking system for the unbanked
column6: Since its establishment in 2015, Blockbonds' focus has been to develop technology solutions for the financial industry. This includes mobilizing children for advocacy campaigns on climate change and the development of community climate change mitigation plans. column2: Festival of the Desert 2012-2013
column6:
The Festival in the Desert started out as a local music festival of nomads in Essakane in northern Mali near Timbuktu. It has now become one of the largest cultural events in Mali. Through Norwegian financing, the Association du Festival au Desert (EFES)  will implement a three-year plan to professionalize the festival and develop the festival into an environment friendly event inspired by several festivals in Norway.  

The environmental activities, called “Operation Clean Desert” will counteract one of the most negative impacts of tourist attractions of this kind: the accumulation of garbage. In addition to the consequences for the esthetics of the desert, garbage also has a negative impact on the fragile ecosystem and biodiversity of the desert where everything, including biodegradables, takes much more time to decompose.  Focus will be on collecting and incinerating the garbage,organizing a campaign on the negative consequences of tourism and the introduction of solar panels for lighting the festival tents.  

Cultural cooperation between musicians from Norway and from Northern Mali is planned.

column2: UNFPA-Humanitarian and Life-saving Activities in Sudan
column6: UNFPA-Humanitarian and Life-saving Activities in Sudan: The project will enhance effort to access and avail lifesaving SRH services to the most vulnerable population in Sudan, guided by the minimum initial service package for SRH in emergencies. The project’s primary focus is on reducing excess maternal and neonatal mortalities and morbidities, addressing the needs of survivors of sexual violence, and providing clinical management for rape cases, reducing the burden of sexually transmitted diseases, preventing HIV, and minimizing unintended pregnancies through family planning services. The project also aims to enhance coordination among all stakeholders on the ground and support the transition into comprehensive SRH services as soon as the situation allows. The project is further focused on improving accountability to affected populations, including people with disabilities, and on the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse. The project exemplifies UNFPA’s commitment to uphold the principle of "Leave No One Behind" within humanitarian settings.

column2: Pen instead of Gun: Education for Peace, Justice and Development
column6: ISHA Development Committee (Agreement partner) søker for 2011 om støtte til prosjektet Pen instead of Gun: Education for Peace, Justice and Development i Somalia. Organisasjonen søkte om støtte til dette prosjektet i årene 2007-2010, fikk avslag de to første årene, men har mottatt NOK 200 000 for hvert av årene 2009 og 2010 (GLO-3989 SOM 08/017, P-360-ref. 0801315 for 2009; og GLO-3989 SOM-10/0003, ref. 0901625 for 2010). Implementerende institusjon/lokalpartner er ISHA Aid (tidligere Dharkayn Development Organisation, omdøpt Isha Somalia i 2008 og Isha Aid i 2010). Mht. dette prosjektet (Pen instead of Gun) søker organisasjonen om støtte til det tredje av tre år (2009-2011), søknadsbeløpet for 2011 er NOK 492 610, noe som vil innebære et maksimalt samlet støttebeløp for hele perioden på NOK 892 610 (medregnet tildelt beløp på NOK 200 000 for hvert av årene 2009 og 2010). Det overordnede prosjektmålet er å gi grunnskoleopplæring til barn i skolepliktig alder i Sool-området. På brukernivå er målet at ca. 500 elever, hvorav minst halvparten jenter, skal ha gjennomført fjerde års grunnskoleopplæring (grade four) innen 2011.

column2: Galmudug and Hiiraan Peace and Join-together programme
column6:
The demand for peace and stability is great in Somalia. The TFG has not solved the complexes problems of Somalia, but the alternatives to TFG seem few. The civil war has destabilized much of the country and led into a “chronic” humanitarian crisis. 
Yme in association with NorSom have worked in Central Somalia (Mudug, Galgaduud and Hiiraan) since 2006 and know the area well. Yme has today become one of the main WASH actors in Somalia. The Implementing partner throughout all the projects in Central Somalia has been GSA (General Service Agency). They have their head office in Galkacyo,  Mudug and also one office in Dhusamareeb, Galgaduud.
Objective 1; To indentify the possibility to conjoin the peace seeking stakeholders in the Galmudug and Hiraan region. 
Objective 2; Indentify together with the stakeholders best practices for peace building activities

column2: NPA- Capacity building
column6:
A new democratic national constitution is an essential starting point in moving towards a new and progressive Zimbabwe. 

Norsk Folkehjelp and its partner Zimbabwe Insititute (ZI) is of the view that a new democratic constitution is the centrepiece of governance and development. 

ZI proposes to support the work of civil society groups in voter education in order to educate and raise awareness among people in relation to the constitution reform process. Civil society is a critical stakeholder in Zimbabwe’s political process. It is particularly pertinent to engage civil society as they have been deeply involved in the struggle for a new constitution in Zimbabwe. It is equally important that the civil society’s role as a watch dog is robustly supported. 

Objectives:
a). Enhance the work of the Parliamentary Select Committee in the making of a new constitution.
b). Provide the necessary technical expertise to ensure views of the people are captured correctly.

The Norwegian Embassy in Kampala has together with SIDA been funders of NBI/NELSAP 3 River Basin Management Project for the past four years. Norwegian funding to NBI/NELSAP has been approximately NOK 25 Million. The 3 River Basin Management Project cover significant watershed areas for the lake Victoria eco system, and therefore to the Nile River. 
The Sio-Malaba-Malakisi River Basin Project is one of the three river basin management projects being implemented within the framework of the Nile Equatorial Lakes Subsidiary Action Program (NELSAP) of the Nile Basin Initiative (NBI), which has been supported by Norway; the other projects are Mara and Kagera river basin projects. The project objective is to establish a sustainable framework for the joint management of the water resources of the catchments; in order to prepare for sustainable development oriented investments to improve the living conditions of the people and to protect the environment.

The Sio- Malaba- Malakisi (SMM) has presented four investment projects for consideration for funding to the Norwegian embassy in Kampala. Of these four the Norwegian embassy in Kampala has found three investment projects of interest due

A ToR is developed for the mission. The Swedish Embassy has recruited a consultant who will travel with the team, translate to English and write the report. 

Åsne Århus Botillen has good knowledge of the Generacao-BIZ program as she has been involved in collecting and analysing data from the project related to an evaluation. The Overall Goal of the action is: To contribute to the promotion and attainment of an inclusive democratic, peaceful and developmental Zimbabwe through Zimbabwean-driven national dialogue processes aimed at political and electoral reforms that reduce disputes over electoral outcomes.

Priority Area 2: Institutional Building (focusing on Protecting the Vote)

Objective 2: To facilitate political party strengthening in EPAs database development for inclusive and efficient EPAs recruitment and training by July 2023

Outcome 2: Enhanced capacity of political parties to protect the vote in 2023 elections.

Priority Area 3: Equality and Inclusion

Objective 3: To promote increased political participation of women and youth political party leadership processes and the 2023 elections.
Outcome 3: Gender inclusive political parties with opportunities for political participation of women and youth

Main Target group: 
Political parties are the main targeted beneficiaries, and they will benefit from the project’s institutional strengthening activities and dialogue activities which will help to create conditions for peaceful electoral contests and management of political transitions.

column2: WB Multi Partner Fund 2022-2024
column6:
The main objective of the multidonor fund is to provide a platform for coordinated financing for the sustainable reconstruction and development of Somalia, with a focus on core state functions and socio-economic recovery.
The MPF serves several key functions as a complement to IDA financing. It provides a mechanism for development partners to easily channel ODA through country systems in Somalia, either as co-financing for IDA investments or new investments projects, which may later be scaled up by IDA. It helps reduce fragmentation, by enabling development partners to pool resources. Moreover, co-financing of IDA investments helps the portfolio achieve greater economies of scale and impact at scale through country systems. Pilot investments in core areas of focus such as climate change and women empowerment/gender equality are envisioned. 
The MPF-financed policy dialogue and knowledge work is designed to inform the portfolio and advance CPF objectives in a way that serves a broader group of stakeholders. Knowledge products are intended to serve as public goods, helping inform sectoral and thematic discussions with implications beyond the immediate portfolio. Similarly, platforms for policy dialogue are designed to advance national discussions of critical importance for Somalia to achieve its development goals. Enhanced focus on climate change adaptation and mitigation will feature prominently.
The World Bank’s risk exposure is increasing in Somalia, with significant implications for current operations and the operational pipeline. The MPF helps teams go above and beyond standard Bank procedures on risk management. With MPF support, the Bank is able to implement a more ambitious, strategic and coordinated approach to risk management. The enhanced approach has three thematic areas: 1) environmental, social and security risk management (ESSRM); 2) fiduciary risk and project management; and 3) enhanced FCV support.

The main objective of the multidonor fund is to provide a platform for coordinated financing for the sustainable reconstruction and development of Somalia, with a focus on core state functions and socio-economic recovery.
The MPF serves several key functions as a complement to IDA financing. It provides a mechanism for development partners to easily channel ODA through country systems in Somalia, either as co-financing for IDA investments or new investments projects, which may later be scaled up by IDA. It helps reduce fragmentation, by enabling development partners to pool resources. Moreover, co-financing of IDA investments helps the portfolio achieve greater economies of scale and impact at scale through country systems. Pilot investments in core areas of focus such as climate change and women empowerment/gender equality are envisioned.

Knowledge products are intended to serve as public goods, helping inform sectoral and thematic discussions with implications beyond the immediate portfolio. column6:
WFP will deliver school feeding to shock-affected schoolchildren that help meet their basic food and nutrition needs and increase school enrolment and retention
school feeding in take-home rations modality with a duration of two school trimesters will benefit  26,423 displaced and returnee children.

To further improve conditions of learning for girls and deter barriers to girls’ education, 
WFP will distribute menstrual hygiene kits.
Learning spaces will receive handwashing stations to improve WASH conditions, promote the safe resumption of classes, and ensure the safe distribution of food to children.

column2: Partnerships for food security and livelihoods - Malawi
column3: PELUM - Participatory Ecological Land Use Management - local office
column6:
The project aims to increase food and nutrition security for small-scale food producers and their communities in Malawi. The long-term impact is to strengthen climate-resilient local food systems by putting small-scale producers at the center and allowing for the widespread use and consumption of locally adapted crops and varieties (including neglected and underutilized food plants), and promoting self-sufficiency.

Outcomes are:
1) Local biodiversity management
2) Local value chains of agrobiodiverse products
3) Innovative Farmer-Researcher partnerships
4) Collaborative environment for policy change

Main activites include:
1) Research agendas on PPB/crop diversity and local food plants/nutrition; increased capacities for PPB, utilization of LFPs, and agroecological crop management; improved seed storage; strong dissemination linkages to create insterest in/market for PPB and nutrition work, and to stimulate demand for marketing.
2) Production and dissemination of high-quality seed of local adapted varieties; increased capacities for food production and value creation/addition; improved local value chains of agrobiodiverse products; strengthened market linkages among value chain actors; increased market access for farmers organizations.
3) New ways of famer-researcher collaboration; increased capacitites for farmer-managed seed and food systems research; successful co-created innovations.
4) Increased influence through evidence-based advocacy; policy reforms proposed; increased capacities for policy influencing. 

Resources will be allocated toward mobilizing, supporting and engaging women’s leadership roles in food production, processing and marketing to empower women as key actors in food production and address the economic and legislative barriers they face. Power dynamics and paradigms will be targeted, including active work on policy change related to women’s access to land.

The funding is available for plots in the range of 25 to 3000 Ha, and the standards of seed quality, maintenance and management planning are strict. Furthermore the programme includes technical advice. About half of the plots are established on forest reserves through agreements with the NFA, whilst the remaining areas rest on private or communal land. Support to community groups is also being piloted (so far 200 Ha in 14 districts established). Support in collaboration with districts and district forest staff is being planed for in two districts. To  date almost 11.000 ha have been established under the scheme.
It has a climate effect through establishing forests to capture carbon, it has an environmental effect through the re-establishment of lost forests; is has economical implications and is a good example of Public-Private Partnership. It supports local organisation at two levels: community groups and producers organisations (Uganda Timber Growers Association has been established with support from the SPGS).

column2: AET - Education in Southern Sudan 2008-2011
column6:
To improve the capacity and skills of the staff of GOSS, State Ministries and civil society organisations to plan, manage and deliver rehabilitation and development programmes effectively and efficiently both by themselves and in cooperation with donors and international community, especially in key areas such as health, education, agriculture, gender and governance.

Objectives
[1] By the end of the programme at least 180 men and women with improved further and higher educational qualifications and skills relevant to rehabilitation and development are employed and using their skills in government structures, in civil society organisations and in businesses in Southern Sudan.

[2] By the end of the three years 30 men and women have studied and completed courses in other countries which were relevant to development needs but were not available locally and have returned for employment in Southern Sudan.

[3] GOSS and state partners have accepted the principle of equal representation of women on the programme and gender sensitive selection procedures were developed and agreed which ensured that at least% 50 of the people who directly benefited from the programme were women.

column2: Smart SDG Cities, Ghana
column3: UN-HABITAT - United Nations Human Settlements Programme
column5: UN-HABITAT - United Nations Human Settlements Programme
column6:
Background: Rapid urbanization in Ghana over the past three decades has coincided with rapid GDP growth. This has helped to create jobs, increase human capital, decrease poverty, and expand opportunities and improve living conditions for millions of Ghanaians. Yet urbanisation has been accompanied by challenges related to efficiency and inclusion, including slums, lack of basic services, underdeveloped manufacturing, and insufficient transport infrastructure.
The project: The novelty of the program in a Ghanaian context is to localise the SDGs in cities. The project does so by introducing the SDG Cities global initiative to a network of 10 cities and variety of local institutions across Ghana to advance the achievement of Smart SDGs. The project was initiated by the Ghanaian Ministry of Finance, who is expected to be a key partner in the implementation. Other partners include the Ministry of Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development, the National Development Planning Commission, the UN Capital Development Fund, the Institute for Housing and Urban Development Studies and the United Nations Innovation Technology Accelerator for Cities. A gender transformative approach is integrated in project design and implementation. Project Key Performance Indicators will include women inclusion in data collection and strategic planning processes.

Impact: Accelerated achievement of the SDGs in cities, including enhancing urban climate resilience and promoting a green transition of cities in Ghana with the use of digital tools. 

Outcome 1: Improved support structure for accelerating SDGs in cities, Outcome 2: Improved evidence-based planning, Outcome 3: Strengthened local institutions, able to effectively progress economic, social and environment dimensions of sustainable urban development through digital training resources and tools, Outcome 4: Increased, measurable SDG impacts in cities through deploying public and private sources.

column2: Empowering Cultural Practitioners in Malawi for Enhance Artistic Freedom of Expression
column6:
Artists in Malawi face censorship and legal constraints and have limited platform for artistic expression. These problems impede the ability of practitioners to engage meaningfully with the community and influence change. Thus, the project seeks to overcome these obstacles by providing the necessary training, resources and support to empower artists.  It seeks to create a thriving culture sector in Malawi where freedom of expression is respected, upheld and celebrated. 
The impact of the project is an enabling and thriving culture sector that contributes towards greater freedom of expression, democracy and socio-economic development in Malawi. The project is designed to enhance the capacity of cultural practitioners in Malawi to freely express themselves, advocate for their rights and contribute to a vibrant and inclusive cultural sector.

column2: EYE Universal Program on SRHR
column6:
This program aims to reduce maternal deaths and unintended teenage pregnancies in the districts of Mayuge and Kamuli (impact) by increasing the utilization of integrated SRHR services by adolescents and young people in Eastern Uganda. The program targets to reach 278,062 young people between the ages of 10 and 24 and 276,533 beneficiaries above the age of 25.
1.	Empower adolescents and young people aged 10-24, including those in hard-to-reach communities and those most at risk, to decide over their own bodies, make informed choices, and utilize high quality, integrated SRHR information and services (individual level)

2.	Increase capacity of health facilities in the target districts to provide universal access to acceptable high quality integrated SRHR and GBV services, particularly for the most vulnerable adolescents and youth  (service delivery level) .

3.	Enhance and optimize the enabling environment at the sub-national and national      level (community, district and national level) for adolescents and young people to exercise their SRH rights, make informed choices, and demand SRH services (eco-system level) and to hold leaders accountable.

column2: Primary Health Care Essential Medicines Support Programme for Malawi
column6:
The Health Sector Programme of Work I, through Central Medical Stores have not been able to purchase the required amounts of drugs and supply needed for the EHP for two years. CMS( Chair of the Board) and the MoH (PS 1) have requested donor support for an emergency procurement of drugs and supplies for at least six months. The request states that CMS will be the responsible procurer and distributer of the items.

 Due to the disarray of CMS, in a state of transition as well as the misappropriated procurements and leakages through the CMS system in the past, the donors in question (USAID,DFID,KfW, Norway, UNICEF and GFATM) have in principle agreed to support a 12-months supply of necessary drugs and supplies, but not using the CMS system/channels. Norway will channel most of the commited, but not disbursed funds to POW I (MWI 07/033) directly to UNICEF Malawi, who also will be the contractual partner with the Embassy. MoF will be requested to approve of this wirement. Germany/UK/USG will fund a supply chain management agent, DELIVER, to ensure that the drugs and supplies are delivered at point of service delivery

column6:

- To provide modern technical education and support to local schools in the surroundings. In particular, to be an additional resource for the Solar Energy and Environmental Technology Education Program (SEETEP) project (KEN-10/0030-1.)
- In general, to provide opportunities to any in need of technical assistance in the eradication of poverty and to promote environmentally sound solutions to local community’s day-to-day challenges (solar cell products, LED-lamps, water catchments, etc).
- Additional support for students in surrounding secondary schools, regarding practical science and technology/workshops

column2: Dam safety
column6:
Agreement between the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (Norad) and the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing of Ghana regarding support in establishment of a national dam safety unit (NDSU).  The Goal of the Programme is:

To minimize the serious threat to society caused by potential dam break which can cause serious consequences in terms of deaths, injuries and damage to property and environment to an internationally acceptable level.

The Purpose of the Programme is:

The need for a centralized body set up to ensure that safety measures are in place for all dams are apparent. To ensure that an adequate and uniform level of dam safety is maintained with respect to the failure consequences the dam imposes. 
Norad case no 1000683

•	Explore, generate and ‘feed in’ technical options to accommodate political interests and perspectives in Somalia
•	Engage key constituencies and non-State armed groups in Somalia in dialogue on future governance arrangements

Target audience for the political options includes the parties to the 2008 Djibouti Peace Agreement, the Transitional Federal Government (TFG) of Somalia, non-State armed groups in Somalia and de facto authorities of Somaliland and Puntland, political parties/actors in Somalia.

column6: This project (LFSP) consists of three strategic pilars for cooperation on forest with Liberia. LFSP is developed by the World Bank in close collaboration with the authorities in Liberia. The project will strengthen institutional capacity to manage woodlands and support activities contributing to sustainable economic activity and management of protected areas. The project will also support the development of a system for measuring and reporting emissions. The program funds training of local small-scale farmers in climate resilient agriculture, including modern plant materials, tools and technology. The program also supports local land-use planning and mapping of natural resources (including soil quality), a prerequisite for strengthening local resilience.

column2: Centre Régional Africain pour le Développement Endogène et Communautaire - Scaling Up Tax Justice Mobilising CSOs media, and parliamentarians
column6:
The project aims at (impact) improved policies and laws to track and stop illicit financial outflows, enhanced fair and equitable tax revenue mobilization and strengthened social contracts in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ghana, Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Cameroun, and Tunisia.

Outcome 1) Capacity of civil society organizations in the targeted countries strengthened to advocate for and engage citizens on tax justice, Domestic Resource Mobilisation (DRM), track and stop illicit financial lows (IFFs).

Outcome 2) Capacity of media organizations in the targeted countries strengthened, to publish stories on tax justice, DRM and IFFs. 

Outcome 3) Capacity of national caucuses of the African Parliamentary Network on Illicit Financial Flows and Taxation (APNIFFT) reinforced. Member of Parliament (MPs) equipped with technical skills to monitor and design supportive policies for equitable taxation to improve DRM, track and stop IFFs.

To enhance expertise on gender equality, particularly the gender dimension of tax justice, TJN-A’s member organisations include feminist organisations and TJN-A collaborates with regional and global women’s organisations such as Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET) and the Association for Women’s Rights in Development (AWID).

column2: GCERF Enhanced Resilience to Violent Extremism (Sahel & Littoral States)
column3: GCERF - The Global Community Engagement and Resilience Fund
column5: GCERF - The Global Community Engagement and Resilience Fund
column6:
Fund replenishment, or core support with a soft geographic earmarking to the Sahel region, relevant West-African coastal states, and the Horn of Africa. GCERF’s Sahel programme is the point of departure, with the G5 Sahel countries and so-called ‘littoral states’ as the main beneficiaries. The Sahel programme focuses on the Liptako-Gourma region (“Fuseau Centre”) and is in the process to expanding it to other parts of the G5 countries: “Fuseau Ouest” (Mali-Mauritania border) and the “Fuseau Est” (Niger-Chad border). G5 Sahel consists of Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania and Niger. Ghana, Benin, Togo, Ivory Coast, and Nigeria fall into the category of so-called littoral states. The Norwegian grant will mainly be utilised in Mauritania, Chad, Ghana and Niger. Overall objective (impact): The emergence of resilient communities against violent extremism in the most vulnerable communities. 

Target Groups: 
-	Group 1: Internally and externally displaced young men and women living in host communities in rural areas. 
-	Group 2: Bereaved households due to extremist, self-defence militias, or government forces operations. 
-	Group 3: Local authority actors, including customary chiefs and religious leaders to enable existing structures to build sustainable pockets of peace.

All GCERF projects have a gender equality cross-cutting theme to ensure a conflict sensitive and inclusive response. In addition, each grantee benefits from tailored trainings for example on gender sensitive programming.

column4: Private sector in other donor countries
column6:
Renew Capital’s SPRINT program aims to catalyse entrepreneurial ecosystems of Mozambique, Malawi and Ghana. Their approach Invest + Impact mobilizes capital into Africa’s missing middle and help companies through the critical stages of growth. SPRINT Program will seek to channel NOK 120 million of private and commercial capital into innovative startups and growth-oriented SMEs, in addition to providing technical assistance. Target companies will be offering innovative, scalable and tech-enabled solutions to bolster the blue economy, combat marine litter and facilitate climate change adaptation.
Programme impact – Vibrant, more climate resilient and gender-responsive startup and SME ecosystems in Mozambique, Malawi and Ghana

Programme outcome: 
1 - Enhanced incubation and scaling of innovative private sector solutions and business models that results in a more investable pipeline of deals
2 - Increased provision of capital into and management of climate-smart and gender-responsive companies
3 - Improved enabling environment and startup and investment ecosystems for climate-smart and gender-responsive startups and SMEs

column6:

i. Establishing the Pemba Interfaith Center
ii. Enhancing coordination and linkages between interfaith structures and other multi-actor stakeholders
iii. Strengthening inclusive platforms to build social cohesion and peace

Outcome 2: Income and employment opportunities for youth and women in a changing climate are improved
i. Mobilizing youth for agricultural value chains and markets
ii. Enhancing knowledge of youth on climate smart agricultural production

Outcome 3. Youth are organized and actively engaged to promote social cohesion and peace
i. Public spaces are used by youth to express positive ideas/views on peace building and social cohesion
ii. Youth knowledge is enhanced to promote social cohesion and peace

Outcome 4. Rights holders and duty bearers are empowered to participate in national and regional arenas for peace building
i. Youth ambassadors engaged to advocate for peace in multi-stakeholder forums
ii. Duty bearers are educated and influenced to respond to early warning signs of violence

Through advocacy and capacity development ensure the sport sector in Zambia is equitable, inclusive and rights based and girls and women are empowered to participate, lead and develop as active members of their communities. 

The overall NIF project’s primary objective is to enhance opportunities for marginalized persons to benefit from and participate in sports. For to achieve this, NIF focuses on 1) To build lasting partnerships and networks to gain sustainable organizations that deliver safe, equitable and inclusive sports activities, 2) To enhance management resources in the development of inclusive and equitable partner programs with resources, and 3) Strengthened capacity of sports organizations to implement safe, equitable and inclusive sport. Emphasis is on the inclusion of women and girls, children/youth, persons with disabilities, and refugees.

column6: The aim of WE4D is to improve the employment and economic situation of women in Africa, especially in companies and sectors that promote the green transformation of the economy. The programme is implemented in the following fields of action: (1) labour market-oriented education and training, (2) transition to the labour market, (3) employment in value chains, (4) competitiveness of start-ups and MSMEs and (5) regional scaling of approaches. To promote the green transformation, WE4D focuses on green sectors (Sustainable Agriculture/ Agroprocessing, Circular Economy/ Waste Management/ Biomass, Eco-Tourism, Blue Economy and Aquaculture, Renewable Energy) and conventional sectors with a potential for greening (Construction, Transport and Logistics). Persons with disabilities (PwD) are among the target groups of the project. The programme will be implemented in six countries: Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda.

column2: Regional Conference on Agriculture,  Food Security and Climate Change
column6:
Agriculture and food security have not been given sufficient emphasis in the climate change discussions so far. 

The Netherlands, in close cooperation with Norway, the World Bank, FAO, Ethiopia, and New Zealand, is organizing an international conference on agriculture, food security and climate change in the Hague, The Netherlands 1-5 November 2010. The objective is to develop  a roadmap for inclusion of agriculutre and food security agenda in the climate change negotiations, especially during the next United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change -Conference of Parties (UNFCCC COP) that will take place towards the end of 2010 in Cancun in Mexico. 

For Africa as the world’s most agriculture-dependent continent, progress in this area could be critical, and therefore, a preparatory conference for the African region will be convened in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from 6 to 8 September 2010. The objective is to identify Africa’s issues, challenges and opportunities in achieving climate-smart sustainable agriculture. It will also establish African priorities related to agriculture, food security and climate change for consideration in the Hague conference. The Addis Ababa Confe

In accordance with the Government of Mozambique’s National Mine Action Plan, Halo Trust is working in the provinces of Maputo, Manica and Tete. In 2011 Halo aims to complete the mine clearance of Confirmed Hazardous Areas (CHAs) in Maputo province and the subsequent Mine Free District (MFD) process. There are 200 pylons transporting electricity from the South African border to the city of Maputo. During the civil war these pylons were mined to defend them from sabotage. Following the end of the war, and to conduct maintenance on the line and having safe access through the mine fields, a bulldozer was used to push the mined soil away from the pylons and thus created spoil piles with landmines. The spoil piles need to be excavated and the ground inspected for landmines. Halo Trust is using an Orbital Screener to separate fine soil from larger items and mines.

column2: Future Proofing the Grain Value Chain in Northern Ghana
column3: WARC Group LLC - The West African Rice Company
column5: WARC Group LLC - The West African Rice Company
column6: Impact: The expected effect on society is strengthened food security in rural Northern Ghana. Outcomes: Expected effects for the direct target group (see bottom of section) are 1. Agricultural sector is strengthened through market linkages, 2. Farmers access high-quality inputs and services through hubs, and 3. Farmers use regenerative agricultural practices. Outputs: Warc will open 25 trading hubs in rural Northern Ghana (half with 2x50MT silos), creating 185 direct jobs (40% women), serving 15,000 farmers with improved inputs, technical training, and providing fair markets. Warc will purchase 15,000MT maize from farmers, adding EUR 5.3 million to their incomes and sell to downstream buyers, including Koudijs Ghana, one of Ghana’s largest poultry feed processors, and Nestle. Intended target groups are farmers in Northern Ghana (direct target group) and the population of Northern Ghana at large (end target group).

column2: Landbruk for utvikling NIBIO-Malawi Digital Plant Health Service MaDiPHS
column6:
Crop losses caused by plant pests, diseases and weeds have been estimated at 42% worldwide. Synthetic pesticides are the predominant control methods but these are associated with negative environmental and health concerns. The extensive use of the chemicals to control pests has sparked renewed interest for Integrated Pest Management (IPM).

Climate change implies hotter and wetter weather, and this will often lead to more pests and diseases in agricultural crops. New pests and diseases might also appear and have large negative implications on the production. Early warning – and effective handling of these pests are therefore of great importance.

The Malawi Digital Plant Health System (MaDiPHS) will give the agricultural extension system as well as the farmers an effective tool to detect and handle pests and diseases at an early stage. The main goal is to establish an agricultural plant health service at the national level in Malawi, based on coordination of internationally developed digital systems.

Key achievements:

- Establishment of an international platform for integration and coordinated access to data from multiple existing digital systems.

- Establishment of a national digital plant health service tailored to fit Malawi users, hosted and managed by national government institutions.

- Improved and extended strategies for integrated pest management (IPM) targeted at main crops and pests in Malawian agriculture.

column2: Hauge Micro Finance - Burundi
column6:
The project will provide unconditional cash transfers (UCTs) to microfinance clients residing in Burundi's poorest province, Kirundo, aiming to increase investments, business growth, job creation and improved living standards. 

The project's hypothesis of change is that providing UCTs to individuals who have prior microfinance experience and who have received training in money management, market understanding and entrepreneurship are more likely to put the funds to productive use, such as investing to scale their businesses and increase their income. Additionally, the UCT amount will be of a considerable size, so that it not only alleviates short-term consumption needs, but will be spent on long-term investments. 

To ensure secure fund distribution, our partner organization HFM Burundi will utilize their existing infrastructure, employing rigorous digital and in-person validation methods to ensure that the money reaches its intended target population. The team at HMF Norway will employ its digital monitoring infrastructure to ensure good governance and transparency. Moreover, the Development Learning Lab (DLL) at Chr. Michelsen Institute (CMI), the Norwegian School of Economics (NHH) and the University in Bergen (UiB) will assess the project's impact and outcome, and conduct research to benefit the wider development community. 

Spanning five years, the first year will focus on capacity building at HFM Burundi by strengthening its operational capabilities and digital infrastructure. Creating awareness and fostering understanding in the province regarding the project's objectives and the source of the funding will be vital. DLL will adapt their project assessment frameworks to the local context and calibrate the UCT
amount allotted to each recipient. In the subsequent four years, the HFM Burundi will distribute the funds on the ground, whilst HMF Norway provides project management and monitoring, and DLL will collect insights and conduct their assessment.

column2: Support to construction of six rural distribution projects
column3: Uganda Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development
column5: Uganda Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development
column6:
Support to the construction of six rural electrification projects - extention of app 550 km of 33 kV distribution grid to the villages of Mubende – Kyenjojo, Kabale – Kisoro and Rakai – Sembabule. Expected app. 15,000 connections in after 10 years, off whch 3000 in year 1 after commissioning. 

The Goal of the project is to meet the rural population’s need for improved economic and social development in a sustainable way through increased access to affordable electricity services. The Purpose of the project is to extend the power from national grid to district headquarters, administrations, businesses, production units, and households, not yet served by the grid. The main target groups for the electrification are district headquarters, trading centres and other productive enterprises with the aim of increasing economic activities for income generation, provision of electricity for social services (health, education and water supply) and household energy use.

Gender activities will be piloted in the projects, to be designed by REA with support from Energia as a separate project

column2: GW Promoting domestic resource mobilisation for a just energy transition Mali
column6:
The economic transition from fossil fuels to renewables must not place undue burden on, or unjustly affect, those least responsiblefor the climate crisis. While we must scale up clean energy such as solar and wind power to avoid climate-breakdown, Global South countries where large deposits of lithium, cobalt, and copper are located, must also benefit from this process. To address the problem, Global Witness (GW) will work in partnership with civil society network, Publish What You Pay (PWYP), to convene, strategize, and campaign to expose unfair models of extraction that inhibit DRM, investigate harmful and illicit practices, and address barriers to countries benefiting from the renewable energy transition, while supporting strong governance and a robust civil society enabling environment in those target jurisdictions. 
The project’s objectives are to strengthen Global South civil society and its Northern networks to advance global equity by achieving responsible, transparent management of critical minerals resource wealth to optimise DRM, in the context of the energy transition. Target groups include communities affected by: human and environmental harms from irresponsible extractive industries; the suppression of DRM due to poor governance and illicit financial flows; and climate change impacts.
A South-South CSO alliance will be developed to engage on these issues in collaboration with PWYP and their national chapters
working with communities on critical mineral and energy transition issues in Mali.
A complementary South-North CSO/NGO alliance will be built, supporting the participation of Global South CSOs in leadingadvocacy within international fora and networks.
GW and partner investigations will ground South-North advocacy at the national and international levels. They will expose how exploitative and abusive economic models prevent Global South countries from equitably benefitting from the transition to a green economy

column2: DRC Resilience Programme (WFP Addendum)
column6:
The WFP-FAO  joint resilience programme in the DRC aims to strengthen the resilience of fragile communities, with the following goals: 
1. Reducing food insecurity and poverty and malnutrition help build resilience and promote social cohesion. The joint resilience-building programme supports smallholder farmers and vulnerable communities achieve food security and better nutrition to enable them respond to shocks and have better sanitation.
2. The provision of food assistance and capacity building to crisis affected populations enables communities to grow their own food and diversify their incomes. Through the support of the programme, affected populations are able to join hands to diversify their livelihoods through farmer organizations.
3. Empowering women contributes to breaking the vicious cycle of violence against them. The joint resilience approach gives women the necessary tools to manage better their family’s dietary requirements, resources and take active role in the management of farmer organizations.
4. The joint resilience programme provides an integrated support to vulnerable communities and contributes to social cohesion and peace. By combining resilience with WASH and nutrition support, communities derive multiple benefits, leading to consolidation of peace.
5. The joint resilience programme continue amidst Covid-19 as building the resilience of vulnerable populations to shocks is key for a sustainable response to the pandemic. The strong anchor the resilience programme has in targeted communities is leveraged to pass on messages on Covid-19 preventive measures, mitigate rumours and stigma against the survivors and affected populations.

2020 Target: 104,000 households, benefitting 600,000 people. Geographical Areas: North and South Ubangi, Tanganyika, North Kivu, South Kivu. Partners: Ministries of Agriculture and Rural Development and their technical departments, national and international NGOs, including Search for Common Ground.

column2: Strengthening Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights in Angola
column6:
The project seeks to increase the coverage of family planning/contraceptive services by using the Menstrual Health Management (MHM) as an entry point. UNFPA has past experience with MHM, especially with the introduction of reusable sanitary pads and behavioural change interventions with girls. The project will complement the actions of the Ministry of Education, which are being developed in 900 public schools in the (current) 18 provinces of the country, with technical support provided by UNFPA. The project also aims to reduce maternal mortality from haemorrhage by 50% through a misprostol study and training of 500 health professionals. The project also includes community mobilization efforts to address social gender norms that limit the realization of the sexual and reproductive rights of girls and young women. Moreover, as a third component, the project seeks to tackle the problem of gender-based violence in Angola. 

The project will be implemented in five provinces: Bie, Cunene, Luanda, Malanje, and Namibe.

column2: Strengthening Resilience of Vulnerable Communities through Climate Resilient Livelihoods and Integrated Environmental Practice in Northern Ghana
column3: FAO - Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations
column5: FAO - Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations
column6:
Strengthening Resilience of Vulnerable Communities through Climate Resilient Livelihoods and Integrated Environmental Practice in Northern Ghana (the Upper East and Sanannah regions).
The three main objectives of the project are: 
1) improved livelihoods of 3 000 (approx. 15 000 beneficiaries) pastoralists’, farmers’ and fishers’ households through integrated fish, crop and livestock production and improved access to water.
2) increased productivity and income through climate-resilient practices and market integration with focus on women empowerment.
3) strengthen early warning systems and sustainable natural resource management for risk reduction against climate-induced shocks.

The direct beneficiaries of the project will be the 3000 pastoralists, farmers’ and fishers’ households (15 000 people). 50 % of the beneficiaries will be female-headed households located in the most vulnerable districts of the Upper East and Savannah regions in northern Ghana. column2: Oxfam IBIS - Fair recovery - Strengthened civil society and media for fiscal justice Kenya
column6:
Putting African governments on a path to a fair recovery will require governments, regional and international actors to redouble their efforts to strengthen progressive and gender sensitive tax collection, while at the same time reversing the plans for austerity, halt the debt crisis, and put an end to harmful Illicit Financial Flows that all conspire to undermine public budgets and weaken the link between increased tax and development outcomes. The project will strengthen the capacity of civil society and investigative journalists to push for fiscal justice, putting the financing of the SDGs and a strengthened social contract at its heart. The programme will focus on three countries –  Ghana, Uganda and Kenya. In addition, the programme will seek to influence regional economic communities, the African Union, and global institutions and donor countries to create the conditions that will support African governments to pursue fiscal justice in response to the crises.

Objective 1: Tax revenue and public budgets are expanded and made significantly more progressive and gender-sensitive in the target countries (Uganda, Kenya and Ghana).

Objective 2: Regional and global institutions, policies and agreements support the fulfilment of fiscal justice in African countires.

column2: Strømmestiftelsen - ELCAP
column6:
ELCAP - Enhanced Livelihoods through Commercial Agricultural Production

The project's overall goal is to sustainably improve the livelihoods of 6000 smallholder farmers in the Singida region in Tanzania. According to the application this will also contribute to create 9,944 jobs.  

According to the proposal the project will Improve the lives of the 6,000 smallholder farmers by strengthening support structures to commercialise maize, pigeon peas, sorghum and sunflower value chains so smallholder farmers can choose the crop that best suits their needs and attain broader product distribution. There will be a focus on improved input and practices, not at least the introduction of methods for waste sorting and use of organic waste in the agricultural production (Biochar). The organic waste sorting system can potentially also create other revenue in itself. Solid actors such as Norsk Gjenvinning, Returkraft, Norges Geotekniske Institutt, Norwegian University of Life Sciences and CFU Tanzania are partners in the project and will provide technical support.

column2: ILO-Law-Growth NexusII
column6:
The Law-Growth Nexus II project will stimulate and support local stakeholders and national governments in Kenya, South Africa and Zambia to promote the development of SMEs through more inclusive and “smarter” labour regulations, and build capacities in national organizations to deliver advisory services to the SMEs.
The project will work with a broad spectrum of local stakeholders and national Governments, e.g., governmental ministries, employers’ and workers’ organizations, private sector representatives, business membership organisations, business media, academia, non-governmental organizations, international organizations and donors. However, it is envisaged that the tripartite organizations will be the project’s main partners.
The project will be based in ILO Pretoria, South Africa, and have national project staff in Kenya, South Africa and Zambia. The project will be technically backstopped by the Decent Work Support Team for Eastern and Southern Africa, and administrational and financial supervised through the Area Office.

  2:	Infrastructure Development

column2: Modern Cooking Facility for Africa (MCFA)
column6:
The Modern Cooking Facility for Africa (MCFA) is an innovative instrument established and managed by Nefco, the Nordic Environment Finance Cooperation, which seeks to develop new, sustainable and commercially viable markets for the clean cooking sector. MCFA will contribute to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 on access to modern, affordable and clean energy access by financially incentivising private companies to develop and sell clean cooking technologies to consumers. 

The objective of MCFA is to enable and incentivise private companies to distribute up to 739,000 modern and clean cooking solutions across six target countries, providing clean cooking access to up to 3.7 million Africans. This objective is based on the first call for proposals and round of funding to cookstove service providers. A second funding round will be launched late 2023, and the targets for the program will be updated according to the new contracts with selected service providers. 

Increasing access to cleaner and more sustainable cooking sollutions, such as sustainably produced bioethanol, bio-LPG, biogas, electric cooking solutions and solid biofuels from sustainable sources, e.g. pellets and briquettes will not only provide energy access, but also help reduce CO2 emissions through reduced deforestation, and improve indoor air quality and reduce respiratory diseases especially for women and children.

MCFA is financed by Sweden, Norway and the European Union, and targets the markets in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Kenya, Mozambique, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Malawi.

column2: Climate resilient livelihoods - World Bank MDTF
column6:
Improve household resilience to climate shocks (boost hh level incomes and food security) and reduce HHs exposure to climate change risks.

The Climate smart enhanced public works programme (CS-EPW) aims to provide temporarily work opportunities for ultra-poor households with labour capacity, focusing on creation of community assets at a prescribed wage rate. The program will target 520 000 households across 35 local authorities (LA). Each LA will prioritize 10 micro-catchments and hotspots, employing a maximum of 500 participant households within a catchment area exceeding 300 hectares. Additional micro-catchments and hotspots will be identified based on the number of participants allocated to each LA. Prioritized projects include land resource conservation, afforestation, forest regeneration, environmental and sanitation initiatives, and sustainable livelihoods.

The overall objective of CS-EPWP is to contribute to the overall objective of the SSRLP through the creation of visible, durable, and quality assets within micro catchments and proving cash-for-work that will assist to improve household level incomes and food security and reduce household exposure to risks associated with climate change using landscape restoration activities to build resilience.

column6: The core objective of the AOAV Liberia Observatory project is to establish an independent institutional function which works collaboratively with government and non-government actors, and that builds capacity to report independently on conditions of armed violence in Liberia. The establishment of an Armed Violence Observatory requires collaborative relationships between a number of actors, including government, media, academic institutions and non-governmental organisations.The project will provide regular, publically-available measurement and monitoring on the incidence and impact of armed violence. Data will be disseminated in order to inform policy makers and development practitioners, as well as to raise awareness about issues related to violence among the general public. Armed violence, both threatened and actual, continues to pose a significant threat to security, stability and hence sustainable development in Liberia. Armed violence is a fundamental challenge to humanitarian and developmental goals.

column2: Strengthening Birth Registration Systems to Protect Every Child from Child Labour
column6:
The overall goal of the project is to increase the rate of birth registration in the three selected model countries, Côte d’Ivoire, Mozambique and Nigeria, by 2024 as a key strategy to combat modern slavery and prevent and respond to violence and exploitation of vulnerable children. 

UNICEF will support global and continental initiatives and national efforts in the three countries in Sub-Saharan Africa to increase and accelerate birth registration for all children from birth by strengthening civil registration and child protection systems, government capacity, and community engagement, with the overall aim of protecting children from modern slavery, including child labour, human trafficking and exploitation. Protecting children from child labour requires that every child has access to services that protect them. This means that children have access to education, including quality and relevant learning, that vulnerable households can access social protection programmes to tide over difficulties, and that parents and caregivers have adequate wages and opportunities for decent work.

column2: University in Mogadishu Female Genital Mutilation
column6:
The main aim for this project is to fight violence against Somali women in general, and Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) in particular The project further aims to increase public awareness about the devastating effects of FGM and also to build momentum for a campaign against FGM, leading eventually to legislation against FGM in Somalia. 
The 2010 project will, for the main part, be a continuation of work done in collaboration with the Norwegian Nurses Organisation. The project will through various workshops and information activities, public debate and health interventions, continue to bring the topic of FGM to the forefront in public opinion and debate in Mogadishu. Religious leaders and secular leaders, together with speakers from the university’s Shari’a Law Faculty, will be used to garner support for a ban on FGM, and to enlighten people about the Koran’s teachings against mutilation of the body /human temp

column2: Implementation of two rural electrification projects
column3: Uganda Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development
column5: Uganda Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development
column6:
Implementation of two rural electrification projects. Implementing partner Rural Electrification Agency (REA). The goal of the project is to meet the rural population’s need for improved economic and social development in a sustainable way. The purpose of the project is to achieve an improved livelihood through access to electricity in rural areas. 
The expected outputs are: 
1. Construction of the distribution line from Muanzi to Kiganda (35 km HV 33 kV and 23 km LV 415/240 V), including 7 transformer units of 50 kVA and 6 transformer units of 25 kVA. 515 expected connections. 
2. Construction of the distribution line from Muhanga via Kisiizi to Kyempene with tee offs to Rugyeyo via yakashenyi, to Mukiyenje and to Nyabushenyi. (82 km HV 33 kV and 90 km LV; 415/240 V), including 1 transformer unit of 100 kVA and 10 transformer units of 25 kVA. 1164 expected initial connections.

A consultant shall be hired though an open tendering process, to undertake project supervision on behalf of REA.

column2: Oxfam IBIS - Fair recovery - Strengthened civil society and media for fiscal justice Ghana
column6:
Putting African governments on a path to a fair recovery will require governments, regional and international actors to redouble their efforts to strengthen progressive and gender sensitive tax collection, while at the same time reversing the plans for austerity, halt the debt crisis, and put an end to harmful Illicit Financial Flows that all conspire to undermine public budgets and weaken the link between increased tax and development outcomes. The project will strengthen the capacity of civil society and investigative journalists to push for fiscal justice, putting the financing of the SDGs and a strengthened social contract at its heart. The programme will focus on three countries – Ghana, Uganda and Kenya. In addition, the programme will seek to influence regional economic communities, the African Union, and global institutions and donor countries to create the conditions that will support African governments to pursue fiscal justice in response to the crises.

Objective 1: Tax revenue and public budgets are expanded and made significantly more progressive and gender-sensitive in the target countries (Uganda, Kenya and Ghana).

Objective 2: Regional and global institutions, policies and agreements support the fulfilment of fiscal justice in African countires.

column2: Outreach and Dissemination of the aids2031 South Africa Project
column6:
aids2031 is a consortium of partners established at the initiative of UNAIDS to look at what has been learned about the AIDS response as well as consider the implications of the changing world around AIDS. The initiative convenes nine multi–disciplinary working groups, one of which is the aids 2031 Costs and Financing Project coordinated by the Results for Development (R4D) Institute and whose objectives are to estimate the long term costs of AIDS, given assumed trends in the epidemic and a range of prevention, treatment, and mitigation scenarios; and to explore how certain policy actions or other factors in the next few years, might significantly raise or lower those long-run costs.  

In 2009-2010, Norad financed a costing and financing study in South Africa as one of two country case studies. This exercise was very timely in light of leadership and policy changes in RSA, and allowed to apply the costing, priority-setting and financial mobilization tools and engage the Govt and civil society in analysis and policy dialogue concerning options and quantification of current and future costs related to the aids response. column2: NCA. Sustainable Emergency Recovery and Respons. Somalia 2011
column6:
The overall goal of NCA's projects in Gedo, south-central Somalia, is to mitigate the effects of drought and protect human dignity by providing emergency life saving support and to develop sustainable livelihoods for local communities and to reduce the population’s vulnerability to conflict, humanitarian and natural disasters.

“Emergency Response to the Drought Affected Population in Gedo and South Mudug” is a six months emergency response project to provide emergency life saving assistance. The overall goal of the project is to mitigate the effects of drought and protect human dignity by providing emergency life saving support to 17,967 households and their livestock affected by the La Niña drought in Gedo (Garbaharey and Burdhubo districts) and South Mudug (Xaradhere and Hobyo districts) in south-central Somalia. 

The outcomes are:
1.	Water supply: 
98,802 persons and their livestock in Gedo and South Mudug provided with secured access to adequate and sustainable water supply by the end of August 2011.
2.	Emergency Relief Food: 
9,000 persons (60% females) provided with access to emergency relief food in 45 villages in Garbaharey district and in 23 villages in Burdhubo

The programme aims to drive a just transition from coal and charcoal to renewable energy and clean cooking solutions in three African countries, by:

• Facilitating the divestment of African and Chinese financial institutions from coal fired power plants and increasing financial flows to renewable energy, including women-led renewable energy enterprise. The project promotes the green energy transition including reduced use of fossile coal.

column2: Fiduciary risk assessment of poverty reducing budget support in Zambia
column6:
Norway on behalf of a joint GBS donor group consisting of UK (DFID), Netherlands, Sweden and Finland, is seeking to carry out a fiduciary risk assessment (FRA) of future (from 2011 onwards) poverty reducing budget support in Zambia. This FRA will be an input and a chapter in an overall joint donor appraisal of the prospects for providing future poverty reducing budget support (PRBS) to Zambia. 
The primary objective of the FRA report and advice will be to understand as much as possible within the assigned time and resources available, the fiduciary risk environment for providing PRBS to Zambia from 2011 onwards. The FRA should provide guidance on mitigating any significant risks to proper use of GBS funds in Zambia and outline a process for monitoring performance, taking into consideration the existing and evolving monitoring framework under the current and planned PRBS.

column2: Close the Gap: Sufficient, Competent and Motivated Nurses and Midwives - Zimbabwe
column6: The Norwegian Nurses Organisation (NNO/NSF) aims to create democratic, accountable, inclusive and sustainable organisations for nurses and midwives in four countries in Africa. Zimbabwe Nurses Association - ZINA is a new partner for NNO as of 2024. The aim is to build institutional strength and capacity to be  effective watchdog and advocate for nurses and midwives, and solution provider for the government, contributing to a stronger and more resilient health system to deliver Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and good health for all in Zimbabwe in the long term. The project includes a focus on nurses and midwives’ equal opportunity to leadership training and positions (gender equality) and the rights of nurses and midwives with disabilities. It also aims to train nurses and midwives in health-related climate adaptation, in the face of increased climate change and extreme weather related health emergencies. Finally, the project aims to train the nurses and midwives to provide the best possible assistance to patients with disabilities and with SRHR to female patients.

column2: Lfu NIBIO - Institutional capacity building on Sustainable Soil Health to improve adaptation and mitigation to Climate change in agriculture sector
column6:
Institutional capacity building on Sustainable Soil Health to improve adaptation and mitigation to Climate change in agriculture sector in Tanzania

Impact
Institutional and human capacity on sustainable soil health management increased in case study districts, Tanzania 

Outcome 1 - Improved soil productivity (e.g., soil fertility, soil biodiversity, soil carbon storage)
Outcome 2 - Increased stakeholders’ knowledge on soil health management and adoption
Outcome 3 - Strengthened institutional collaborations on climate smart soil health improving measures.

Outputs
1. Climate smart soil management technologies toolbox developed (including soil health indicator framework, digital soil mapping). This output will contribute to Outcome 1
2. Capacity building program and training modules on soil health developed. This output will contribute to Outcome 1 and 2.
3. Farmers, researchers, extension personnels and public sector agencies competence on soil health management improved. This output will contribute to Outcome 1, 2 and 3.
4. Policy frameworks for up-scaling sustainable soil health programs . This output will contribute to Outcome 3

Project partners (Tanzania) 
-TARI – Tanzania Agricultural Research Institute (main project partner and contract partner) 
-Ministry of Agriculture, (Department of land use planning)
-Innovation platforms/groups
-Soil health living lab actors/ stakeholders and VC actors (producers, input suppliers, processors, traders, consumer groups)

Using sport and recreation to strengthen and build safe and active communities through education and capacity development in the empowerment, leadership development and participation of youth, girls and women, and persons with disabilities in urban communities throughout Zambia. The partners are training youth in sexual reproductive health. 

The overall NIF project’s primary objective is to enhance opportunities for marginalized persons to benefit from and participate in sports. For to achieve this, NIF focuses on 1) To build lasting partnerships and networks to gain sustainable organizations that deliver safe, equitable and inclusive sports activities, 2) To enhance management resources in the development of inclusive and equitable partner programs with resources, and 3) Strengthened capacity of sports organizations to implement safe, equitable and inclusive sport. Emphasis is on the inclusion of women and girls, children/youth, persons with disabilities, and refugees.

column2: Improved livelihoods and resilience
column6: Poor and vulnerable communities have improved livelihoods and resilience through enhanced income generation. The programme will target refugees, host-communities and other vulnerable populations, including activities in refugee settlement camps. The program work to ensure access to public services for vulnerable groups and strengthen civil society organisations to hold governments responsible for human rights and ensure inclusive participation of citizens in decision-making. It has measures to ensure inclusion of persons with disability in all their activities. Gender equality is explicitly promoted in the activity and girls/women’s access to services promoted. The program aims to contribute to reduced social and economic inequalities between men/boys and girls/women. It also includes climate-smart agriculture and green practices such as solar energy, improved cookstoves, forest conservation and community waste management, and work with the communities to increase resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction measures, like early warning systems, diversified cropping, and secure access to water.

column2: Provision of adequate tree seed portfolios (PATSPO) – project phase II
column6:
The project will help the government of Ethiopia achieve the ambitious landscape restoration plan of 15 million hectares. The project will ensure that forest-restoration and tree-planting initiatives have access to high-quality seeds of the most important tree species. PATSPO is designed to support the national forest and landscape restoration programme, part of Ethiopia’s green growth strategy.
PATSPO is a multi-species programme designed to provide: 
- organizational establishment of the tree-seed sector, including stakeholder identification and roles and responsibilities, based on sector analysis.
- species-specific knowledge for priority tree species.
- a critical mass of tree genetic resources for the future, comprising exploration, mobilization, conservation, establishment, management and improvement.
- capacity to monitor and deliver quality seeds and seedlings of the many species required for large-scale restoration.

column2: Additional support to Media Trust Fund
column6:
This is an extension of the ongoing support to MTF as stipulated in the Contract dated 11.8.04. While the overall goal of MTF remains development of “a professional, gender balanced, free, sustainable, relevant and independent media, in particular at the community level”, the planned output of the extension is:

•	Establishment of six community radio stations in Mwinilunga, Isoka, Nchelenge, Macha (Choma), Katete and Luangwa (Chibombo) 
•	Capacity building of staff/volunteers involved in the running of community radio stations, with the view to ensure sustainability in the running of stations after the project period
•	Periodic maintenance and servicing of equipment (up to March 2009)
•	Monitoring of progress at the community level
•	Preparation of final reports, including a final audit for submission by end May 2009

The target group is primarily the population of communities in which the new radio stations are planned, which according to MTF’s estimate is around 600.000 people.

The goal of the project is to lay the foundation for prevention of witchcraft based violence. This will be done with a research with the purpose to establish the prevalence of witchcrafat practices and to find out the forms of witchcraft-based violence that are meted out to children, women and the elderly in Malawi. 

Simultaniously, lobbying will be carried out to influence the outcome of the new witchcraft bill so that it is human rights friendly. The current act is under review by the Law Commission. The main thrust of the lobbying is to ensure that Malawi continues not to criminalize witchcraft. Rather the new bill should criminalize the practice of witchcraft accusations and contain adequate provisions that discourage witchcraft based violence towards the elderly, women and children accussed as witches.
