column2: Right to a dignified life and sustainable livelihood Phase II
column6: The project will take place in four countries, Kenya, Malawi, Cote D’Ivoire and Ghana is based around a Fairtrade approach called the Women’s School of Leadership (WSOL) that aims to build the capacity of participants to be more resilient and empowered. It does so by selecting a group in each country (flower works from Fair Trade producers in Kenya and members of different Fair Trade cooperatives in the remaining countries) and training them on different modules. These modules seek to build capacity of participants on good governance, democracy, participation, market access, transparency and different issues tied to gender equality. There is a strong focus on gender equality; on improving conditions for women and developing better systems in cooperative and farms that strengthen gender equality.  The title of the project is “Right to a dignified life and sustainable livelihood Phase II) which highlights that it is a continuation of this WSOL approach from Phase 1 in Kenya, Ghana and Cote D’Ivoire. There are also smaller components on youth in Ghana and Cote D’Ivoire as well as increasing intra-continental sales of commodities produced on Fair Trade terms

column2: Continental Shift Initiative
column6:
After the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, all coastal states automatically have the right to the continental shelf. This shelf extends a minimum of 200 nautical miles. Shelf beyond 200 nautical miles must be documented to the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf. Coastal states have ten years to present such documentation.
From 2008 to 2014, Norway assisted Cape Verde, Mauritania, Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, and Sierra Leone in the work of documenting the outer limit of their continental shelves beyond 200 nautical miles. The project was led by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The technical aspects were carried out and coordinated by GRID-Arendal and the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate. The technical part also included a very large data collection program funded by Norway. The project, called the Continental Shelf Initiative, resulted in the countries submitting a joint data presentation to the Commission in 2014.
The Shelf Commission currently has 30 presentations on the waiting list before West Africa's. Therefore, a waiting time of 4-7 years for commission processing is expected. In the meantime, it is important to maintain necessary shelf competence in these states so that they can defend the shelf submission to the Commission. To meet this need, the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate has held annual workshops since 2017, financed by Norway, where all countries participate with their technical experts to update themselves on developments in the relevant fields, new data becoming available, and the potential development of precedents in the Commission's published recommendations.
It has been shown that all professionals from the old network attended, and the professional updates and discussions were therefore very effective. All participants and the secretariat in Cape Verde consider such workshops to be a good tool for maintaining both competence and networks and have expressed a strong desire for continuation.

column2: Make Artisanal Fish-Smoking Viable Again MAFVA
column6: The project will support woman cooperatives in Thiaroye, Kayar and Mbalin in the transformation of the fish smoking business. The supported woman cooperatives will improve their access to fresh fish, adopt large scale Nopale fish smoking kilns and development business opportunities. Over time, these changes will lead to a stronger participation of the woman cooperatives in the economic development of the fish processing sector. The project supports women’s cooperatives in Thiaroye, Kayar, and Mbalin to transform the fish-smoking business by promoting the adoption of environmentally friendly practices. Specifically, the project will facilitate the use of large-scale Nopale fish-smoking kilns, which significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions compared to traditional ovens. This initiative aligns with climate change mitigation efforts by lowering the carbon footprint of fish processing activities. The project enhances the resilience of women’s cooperatives by improving their access to fresh fish and creating diversified business opportunities in fish processing. These measures strengthen the economic sustainability of the cooperatives, enabling them to adapt to potential climate-related disruptions in the supply chain and maintain their participation in the economic development of the sector.

column2: Social safety nets - World Bank MDTF
column6:
The Government of Malawi`s core safety net programmes are targeting all 28 districts, but only reaches 10% of the poorest population.  This multi-donor trust fund will provide additional financing into their core programmes, strengthen and enhance these. The MDTF will serve as a mechanism for pooling development partners` funding for the Malawi social cash transfer programme (SCTP) and bring under one single instrument the current separate arrangements for funding different districts under different funding modalities and arrangements. The project is structured to co-finance and scale up existing components and activities in line with the Government of Malawi`s strategic vision for an integrated social protection program. This includes redefining safety net program`s coverage thresholds, making changes to beneficiary targeting approaches, strengthening harmonized delivery systems, and redefining adequacy of safety net benefit levels and complementary shock-responsive approaches. The programme seeks to address land degradation, biodiversity loss and impacts of climate change through interventions such as land conservation, afforestation, natural regeneration and promotion of sustainable livelihoods in selected catchment areas.

The beneficiaries are the ultra-poor and labour-constrained households, and the ultra-poor with labour availability. The project paper talks about scaling up regular SCTP from 123 000 to 258 000 HH. For emergency cash-transfers the total target is 300 000 HH in rural areas and 105 000 HH in urban areas. 

With the fluidity of the MDTF, these numbers are expected to be reviewed in May 2024 during the midterm review to incorporate the additional support and how that impacts the results framework/deliverables.

column2: UNICEF Protection for conflict-affected children in Southern Sudan
column6:
The overall goal of this project is to contribute to building a protective environment for vulnerable children in Southern Sudan, especially children recruited and used by armed forces and groups and conflict-affected children.

The project will aim for an inclusive reintegration for such children, including children released from SPLA and other vulnerable children. UNICEF will also strengthen the capacity of government agencies and other counterparts to enhance the protection services for children in the area affected by conflict.

As a result of this project, it is expected inter alia that approx 1,000 children released from armed forces as well as 1,500 additional vulnerable children will be reintegrated; that some 5,000 children will benefit from programmes facilitating their psycho-social wellbeing; that family tracing and reunification networks will be strengthened; and that social workers of State Ministries of Social Development will have enhanced capacity to provide psycho-social support.

column2: Village Capital Empowering Sustainable Entrepreneurship in Africa
column6:
The initiative intends to strengthen the capacity of Entrepreneur Support Organisations (ESOs) and high-growth potential climate-focused startups in Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and Tanzania. The initiative will take a dual-track approach: 1) equip impactful, community-led ESOs with the resources and experience needed to drive systems change, social and economic resiliency, and sustainable growth of national entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 2) accelerate and cultivate a long-term pipeline of high-growth, investible startups building solutions to enhance economic growth and resiliency in the blue economy, climate adaptation, food security, and renewabla energy sectors. 

The initiative will be divided into five separate components: i) landscape analysis and initative design, ii) ESO capacity building and support, iii) co-led direct entrepreneur support programs, iv) extended entrepreneur support, synthesis, and dissemination of data and learnings, and v) catalysing amd mobilizing capital. 
The program works to increase gender equity through direct work with entrepreneurs, ESOs, and their broader networks. They will use their in-house developed tools to increase gender equality, namely the Peer-Selection Framework and the Smarter Systems Toolkit, to mitigate bias and unlock overlooked opportunities for women entrepreneurs. Their online product, Abaca, incorporates equity-enhancing frameworks and data analysis tools to better understand the impact of their work on women entrepreneurs.

column2: Scaling up Nature Based Solutions (NBS) for Climate Change Resilience in Tanzania (Resolve - NBS)
column3: IUCN - International Union for the Conservation of Nature
column5: IUCN - International Union for the Conservation of Nature
column6:
The project will demonstrate how effective nature based solutions (NbS) can be scaled-up in production landscapes and priority ecosystems through bridging policies, knowledge and practical actions for climate change adaptation, mitigation, biodiversity conservation and livelihoods improvement. It is designed for institutional strengthening, accelerate adoption of Nature-Based Solutions and enhance the livelihoods of communities in the selected landscapes thus achieving three short-term outcomes in the project cycle, and in the long-term, scaling the livelihood, food security and climate resilience benefits to the rural communities in Tanzania. The project aims to ensure that NBS related policies and planning is gender mainstreamed and that women are included in solutions implemented in the selected locations. IUCN will partner with WWF, CEOrt, CAN Tanzania, EAMCEF, NCMC, Care, SAGCOT, SAT and relevant government actors.

Goal: The overall goal of the project is that men and women in local communities increasingly use effective Nature Based Solutions to handle the effects of climate change on food systems and natural ecosystems.
Outcome 1: Improved integration of NbS in climate resilient planning, financing and implementation  
Outcome 2: Nature Based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly resourced at local level.  
Outcome 3: Increased experience with and knowledge about effective NbS for climate resilience in selected landscapes.

column2: Poverty Reduction in the Gorongosa National Park Buffer Zone
column6:
The overall impact of the project is: Contribute to human development and poverty alleviation through an integrated approach of education, improved access to health services, improved agricultural practices and ecotourism development based on the restored biodiversity and ecological processes.

The proposal has been strategically positioned to enable activities for girls’ education and empowerment, poverty reduction in the former conflict zone, the investment into climate smart agriculture practices through agro-forestry approaches and targeted conservation enterprise development support to facilitate post-conflict reintegration and economic growth, particularly targeting women run micro and small to medium size enterprises:  The “Gorongosa Poverty Reduction” project comprises three core areas of support : 
1) Empowering girls through establishing “Girls Clubs”, among other sources of support, in 42 schools in the northern Buffer Zone, based on the lessons learnt from the initial piloting of the approach in 16 schools in Gorongosa and Cheringoma Districts during 2018; 
2) Transforming value chains through strengthening cashew nut and coffee-based agro-forestry models as climate-smart agriculture options and creating jobs among post-harvest facilities; and
3) Creating conservation livelihood opportunities through sustainable enterprise creation focusing on: fisheries, forestry and ecotourism.

The goal of this program is to increase sustainability and resilience in the aquaculture sector in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), through improved aquatic animal health management and biosecurity governance.  WorldFish and the Norwegian Veterinary Institute (NVI) will use their expertise and implement the project in two African countries, namely Ghana and Kenya with support from the Africa Aquaculture Research and Training Centre (AARTC) at WorldFish Abbassa.Improved capacity for aquatic animal health management will be strengthened through research and education. Among other deliveries, 12 Master students, 6 from Kenya and 6 from Ghana will recive practical and tehcnical training as part of their master degress. Norwegian Veterinary institute is an important partner.
The goal of this program is to increase sustainability and resilience in the aquaculture sector in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), through improved aquatic animal health management and biosecurity governance.

column2: Beyond the Grid Fund for Afrca (BGFA)
column6:
Over 600 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa live today without access to electricity. The Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa (BGFA) aims to reduce this gap by stimulating and accelerating the emergency of new business models to incentivise the private sector to offer affordable and clean energy access at scale to people living in rural and peri-urban areas. The BGFA programme aims at actively promoting, incentivising and transferring best practices regarding gender equality in BGFA target countries. BGFA does this through requiring awardees (energy service providers) to offer equal opportunities for men and women

Beyond the Grid Fund for Africa forms part of the ‘Power Africa’ initiative launched by former President Barack Obama and contributes to the Sustainable Development Goal 7 as well as the Paris Agreement on Climate. The planned period of implementation is in total six years. The BGFA programme aims, with so far four funding rounds, to establish up to 1.45 million energy connections by 2028, benefiting more than 6.5 million people in Burkina Faso, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Liberia, Mozambique, Uganda and Zambia
